title: Every Console send synchronously computes trust status + fingerprint digest for every installed user skill on the event loop (admission-dominated, ~80–130 ms per skill)
trigger: Every Console send and every queued send, on the event loop, when at least one user-installed (non-builtin) skill exists. The frozen skills_context also feeds the agent bridge (console_chat_controller.py:28446), so the capture is not limited to sends that contain a skill-mention sigil.
cost:
Measured in isolation with the bench scripts at scratch/second-lens-io-on-loop/{bench,bench_min,bench_states,bench_kshape}.py. Setup: a real LocalSkillsService + SkillTrustService with bootstrap_trust, the built-in character-creator enabled, and user skills copied from obra/superpowers 4.3.1 (14 skills, 35 files). The machine was at load 38-51 on 18 cores, so I use the deterministic counts, taken at data-dir depths 15/19/23/27, as the primary evidence. They are exactly linear in depth.

File-marker shape (Linux without Secret Service). capture_skill_context_maximum:
- K=0: 2,258 Python calls, 0 opens, 0.5 ms.
- K=1: 63,514 / 72,730 / 81,946 / 91,162 Python calls and 2,835 to 4,923 opens across the four depths, with 9 acquire_storage calls.
- K=14: 872,864 calls, 39,690 opens and 126 acquires at depth 15.

macOS/Windows keyring-marker shape (a proxy that hides marker_path/store_dir), extrapolated to the real depth of 6 (~/.local/share/tldw_cli/<user>):
- Per user skill per send: 30.3k Python calls, ~960 opens, 7 acquires.
- K=14: 426k calls and 13.5k opens.

Converting at 0.5-1.05 us per profiled Python call (my best min is ≈1.05; the verifier's run implies ≈0.72) gives ≈15-32 ms per user skill per send. The ≥100 ms threshold is crossed at about 4-7 skills. One superpowers pack costs ≈0.21-0.45 s per send. The extrapolation understates the cost: config-rooted walks are only ~7 levels shallower in reality, the admission path measured here is the cheaper un-enrolled branch, and the cached keychain read after 30 s idle is excluded.

Direct CPU minimums at depth 15, still inflated by load: K=1 93 ms, K=5 518-540 ms, K=14 2.06 s. status_for_skill costs 70 ms against 0.15 ms for the raw scan_skill_directory, so admission dominates, not hashing.

Trust state barely helps. With K=5 skills untrusted (no manifest) the capture costs 387 ms; with the manifest locked it costs 439 ms. That is 72-85% of the trusted cost, so any user who imported skills pays it.

Wrapping the whole capture in one outer operation: K=1 shows no gain; K=5 falls from 660 to 369 ms and K=14 from 2,064 to 972 ms. That confirms the verifier's point that _execution_scope leases must be unified.

Caller trace, untruncated grep with 2 call sites:
- session.py:3603 calls it unconditionally from _build_console_turn_execution_context.
- The Send button (chat_screen.py:4837) and handle_console_send_message (19063) lead to the async _send_console_message_from_visible_action_observed, then _dispatch_console_draft_send (19262), then ConsolePromptQueueUIController.dispatch. dispatch captures at prompt_queue.py:932 when queueing, or reaches _stage_normal_chain, which captures at :984 or calls _launch_chain (:996). _launch_chain goes to wiring.py:2226 and then _admit_console_turn_to_runtime (:271), which is sync.
- The queue edit path also captures (prompt_queue.py:732).
- The other call site is console_chat_controller.py:22581, the fleet/regenerate path.

Nothing offloads or caches the capture; there is no to_thread and no memo. The frozen context also feeds the agent bridge, so plain-text sends pay it too. No open task covers it. TASK-32921 (Done) handled keyring only, and TASK-32804.12 does not name this.
fix: Take it off the send path. Keep a skill-context snapshot on the Console skill controller, computed via asyncio.to_thread at mount/resume and after skill/trust mutations, keyed on a cheap freshness token: the index mtime, the trust manifest generation, and the skill-dir mtime_ns. The send path then freezes that snapshot. The digest re-check at execute time (ensure_frozen_definition) already guards staleness. If a synchronous capture must stay, run the whole capture inside one local_content_lifetime.operation() plus one _execution_scope so N skills share one admission. Context: TASK-32921 (Done) fixed only the keyring part; its notes say the per-skill work still runs on the loop but miss that admission, not hashing, dominates. Umbrella: TASK-32804.
fix_notes: The precomputed-snapshot approach changes when authority is frozen. A skill edited between the snapshot and the send freezes the old digest. ensure_frozen_definition (console_chat_controller.py:23052) re-checks the digest only at mention/execute time, and it returns early when no digest was frozen. Blocked->trusted transitions also need invalidation, so the freshness token must include trust-manifest generation and script-grant changes. Moving the capture to asyncio.to_thread before _launch_chain adds an await point before acceptance, which races with preparing_before_acceptance and session switches. asyncio.to_thread also copies contextvars, so an active outer content operation would raise local_content_operation_context_changed. A single outer local_content_lifetime.operation() only halves the cost because _execution_scope tracks its leases in its own _active_execution ContextVar and does not reuse operation leases. Unify those so N skills share one admission. The cheapest partial win: skip the capture when the draft has no MENTION_SIGIL and the turn is not agent-dispatch-eligible.

title: Console mount AND every resume awaits LocalSkillsService.get_context in a coroutine worker (on the loop): ~58 ms with zero user skills, +~80–100 ms per skill
trigger: Once per Console visit (mount, or resume when the mount did not already refresh), plus unknown-slash-command handling and each Evals visit. The Console re-mounts on every visit (TASK-24452), so this is per-visit.
cost:
LocalSkillsService.get_context() was measured on a persistent event loop, in the same isolated setup and scripts as F1. The deterministic counts are exactly linear in depth.

File-marker shape at depths 15→27:
- K=0: 21,636 → 30,708 Python calls, 1,044 → 1,812 opens, 4 acquires.
- K=1: 54,512 calls, 7 acquires.
- K=5: 186,016 calls, 19 acquires.
- K=14: 488,411 calls, 46 acquires.

macOS/Windows keyring shape, extrapolated to the real depth of 6:
- K=0: 11.5k calls, 351 opens, 3 acquires.
- K=1: 29.1k calls.
- K=5: 99.3k calls.
- K=14: 262k calls.

At 0.5-1.05 us per call, one Console visit costs ≈6-12 ms with no user skills, ≈15-31 ms with 1, ≈50-104 ms with 5, and ≈130-275 ms with a 14-skill pack.

Direct CPU minimums at depth 15 (load ~40): K=0 30-33 ms, K=1 72 ms, K=5 262 ms, K=14 1.0 s.

The first Console mount also builds the trust service on the loop, through the factory in the content-source lambda (_content_sources reads owner.trust_service). That build includes keyring backend discovery, a get_user_data_dir call and is_recovered. It was not measured, to avoid touching the keychain. ensure_local_skill_trust_service (the async pre-warm) is called only from the Library and Skills screens (untruncated grep, 3 sites) and never from the Console.

Trace:
- chat_screen.py:16935 (in _start_console_view_after_reconciliation, reached from on_mount) and chat_screen.py:23831 (on_screen_resume, `if not mount_already_refreshed`) both call run_worker(coroutine) with no thread.
- The coroutine goes through skill.py:64 (await get_context), then SkillsScopeService._call (skills_scope_service.py:162), which invokes the method synchronously via _maybe_await.
- The content_call async wrapper (local_content_lifetime.py:105-119) only enters operation(). It never offloads.
- chat_screen.py:19217 re-fetches on every unknown /command.

The Console re-mounts on each visit (TASK-24452), so this runs once per visit. P1 holds for any user with at least 1 skill and is borderline for zero-skill users. With a skill pack it exceeds 100 ms per visit and shares F1's cost engine, so it should be fixed together with F1. Not covered by any open task.
fix: Run the fetch off-loop with one line: context = await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: asyncio.run(local.get_context())), or better, give LocalSkillsService/SkillsScopeService a sync get_context_snapshot() and call it via asyncio.to_thread, as SkillsScopeService.get_library_user_content_evidence already does (skills_scope_service.py:196). Apply the same fix to Evals _probe_store_skills_presence. Reuse the F1 snapshot so a visit does not recompute when nothing changed.
fix_notes: Prefer a sync get_context_snapshot() on LocalSkillsService called via asyncio.to_thread, mirroring get_library_user_content_evidence_context. Avoid the asyncio.run-inside-to_thread lambda. Keep _enforce_policy on the loop. Moving the fetch off-loop also moves the first local_skill_trust_service factory build onto a worker thread, and that memo (app.py local_skill_trust_service property) has no lock, so a concurrent send-path capture on the loop could build a second trust service. Pre-warm it or add a lock. For Evals, pass the resolved store dir and use to_thread as well.

title: get_user_data_dir() is uncached and costs ~47 ms warm (5 storage admissions, data-root file lock, 1,591 opens); 203 call sites incl. 29 on the boot path and a 5 s UI timer
trigger: Boot, before first paint: ~27 resolutions in TldwCli.__init__, unconditional for most. The Schedules screen hits it every 5 s while visible. Assorted UI handlers hit it once each.
cost:
get_user_data_dir() was measured warm in isolation (bench.py and bench_min.py). The counts are deterministic and exactly linear: at data depths 15/19/23/27 it made 53,576 / 63,599 / 73,616 / 83,636 Python calls (+2,505 per level), 1,694 → 2,942 opens (+104 per level), and 5 acquire_storage calls. Extrapolated to the real ~/.local/share/tldw_cli/<user> (depth 6), that is 31.0k calls and ~760 opens, or ≈15-33 ms per call at 0.5-1.05 us per call. Fitting the time-versus-depth line directly from the min runs (56 ms at depth 15, 107 ms at depth 27) gives ≈18 ms at depth 6.

Direct CPU minimum at depth 15: 56-70 ms. get_chachanotes_db_path (67 ms) and default_heartbeat_path (67 ms) cost the same.

Boot call count comes from an isolated full-boot runtime probe (scratch/second-lens-ratchets/boot_run2.log:162-189). It shows 31 main-thread get_user_data_dir admissions inside TldwCli.__init__ (sum 2.58 s at depth, load ~25), plus 9 more in the pre-ready boot phase. Named sites include app.py:7899/7909, _build_chatbook_db_paths ×3, the watchlists wiring ×2, prompt_history ×3, Logging_Config ×2 and _build_local_skills_stack. The verifier's AST walk found 27. Each call pays the full cost, because verified_user_data_directory returns None outside a companion-guard operation (config_participants.py:245-250).

Pre-first-paint boot tax: 31 × 15-33 ms ≈ 0.46-1.0 s. Even at 10 ms per call it is ≥0.3 s, so P0 on boot stands.

The Schedules screen also pays 15-33 ms on the loop every 5 s while visible. schedules_workbench.py:858 set_interval(5.0) calls _refresh_scheduler_liveness (1121), which calls default_heartbeat_path() at 1142 with no memo. The timer is paused only while the screen is covered.

TASK-32804.1's warm-config fast path does not cover this; warm get_cli_setting is already ~0. Related: TASK-32804.1 AC#2 (amortise admission), still In Progress.
fix: Memoize the resolved lexical path the way TASK-32804.1 served warm get_cli_setting hits. Cache (config-cache identity, configured data_dir) → path. Re-verify cheaply on hit, using one os.stat of the leaf compared by st_ino/st_dev, and drop the cache on config reload or recovery maintenance. Hoist the Schedules heartbeat path into on_mount. TASK-32804.1 covers config reads only; this sibling path was not included.
fix_notes: A process-wide memo skips the ADR-127 root-selection lock and the secure_private_directory ownership/no-follow walk. A leaf-only st_ino/st_dev re-check does not re-verify parent components, which weakens a security-reviewed boundary. It would also need invalidation on users_name or data_dir config changes, profile switch, and recovery restore/maintenance (TASK-32562 is actively changing this code). A lower-risk first step: resolve once per construction by computing get_user_data_dir() at the top of __init__ and passing the base into the wiring helpers and db-path builders, then hoist the heartbeat path into SchedulesWorkbench.on_mount. That removes most boot calls with no cross-call cache.

title: Root cause: storage admission re-derives fixed evidence from disk on every acquire (≈12–15 ms, hundreds of verified-parent opens), with no amortization across calls
trigger: Every @content_call method, every acquire_storage site, every config_participants operation (get_user_data_dir, db-path helpers), and every _execution_scope. The loop-visible payers are F1-F3.
cost:
acquire_storage(path).close() was measured in isolation (bench.py and bench_min.py). The counts are exactly linear: at depths 15/19/23/27 it made 4,471 / 5,207 / 5,943 / 6,679 Python calls (+184 per level) and 261 / 325 / 389 / 453 opens (+16 per level). At the real depth of 6 that is ≈2.8k calls and ~117 opens, or ≈1.4-3 ms per acquire. CPU minimum over 400 reps: 6.2 ms at depth 15 and 10.7 ms at depth 27 (load ~40). operation(1 path) costs 11-14 ms at depth 15.

It is re-derived on every call with no amortisation. It is the multiplier behind the P0s:
- 9 acquires per user skill per send (7 in the keyring shape).
- 126 per send with a 14-skill pack.
- 5 per get_user_data_dir call.
- 3-4 per get_context, plus about 3 per skill.

Lease sharing is partial, and I measured it. One outer local_content_lifetime.operation around the capture gives no gain at K=1 and cuts K=5 from 660 to 369 ms and K=14 from 2,064 to 972 ms. The ~45-50% that remains comes from _execution_scope keeping its own _active_execution lease map (skill_trust_service.py:103-146), which does not reuse the operation's leases.

The cost is measured on the cheaper un-enrolled branch. qualified_for is false with no recovery-bootstrap dir, so enrolled profiles also run admission_authority, the hold wait and the post-wait startup_permission+_scope revalidation (storage_admission.py:904-949). The real per-acquire cost is therefore ≥ this measurement.

It stays P1 as the root cause (1.4-3 ms per call directly) and is not double-counted as a P0. Partially tracked by TASK-32804.1 AC#2 ('admission handshake amortised per derivation or per scope'), which is In Progress and whose fix only bypasses warm config reads. TASK-32562 owns this code.
fix: Amortize inside storage_admission rather than bypassing per caller. Cache the startup_permission, registry and _scope result keyed on a generation token: (st_mtime_ns, st_ino) of the bootstrap root and registry.lock, plus a process-local counter bumped by maintenance close/drain and re-enrollment. Re-derive only when the token changes. Keep the full check on the maintenance and first-acquire paths. Owner program: TASK-32562. TASK-32804.1 (In Progress) fixed only config warm reads, by bypass.
fix_notes: A generation-token cache keyed on st_mtime_ns/st_ino is fragile. mtime granularity and same-tick writes, Windows semantics, and records added by other processes can all serve a stale 'allowed', and this boundary must stay fail-closed. Coordinate with TASK-32562, which is rewriting this code. Lower-risk amortization is by scope: make _execution_scope reuse the enclosing local_content_lifetime operation's leases (and the reverse), then wrap known multi-call chains (skill capture, boot wiring) in one operation. The full check still runs once per chain.

(a) Redacting only getMessage()+exc_text changes MAX_REDACTED_LINE_CHARS semantics, because the token-boundary cap applies to the whole formatted line today. The redaction tests from TASK-23190/19555 must stay green. Caching on the LogRecord is thread-safe because handlers run in sequence on the emitting thread. title: ChaChaNotes trace callback expands every bound parameter (BLOBs hex-encoded) per statement and per trigger step: 3 MiB image insert takes 1.2 s
trigger: Every ChaChaNotes connection registers the callback (ChaChaNotes_DB.py:3524). It fires on every statement and on each trigger subprogram. Hot path: a Console send with an image attachment runs _accept_durable_turn -> _run_durable_db_call(store.commit_durable_turn) at console_chat_controller.py:12069 in to_thread inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. It also fires on add_message/update_message and on every BLOB write to message_attachments, character_cards, notes and console_trace_artifacts.
cost:
All measurements ran on an isolated scratch profile (HOME, XDG_* and TLDW_CONFIG_PATH in scratch/second-lens-pat-memory-F1), Python 3.12.11, SQLite 3.49.1, audit tree 840ed2ca58. Only one site registers the callback: grep -c over tldw_chatbook finds 5 refs, and base_db.py:738 is called only from ChaChaNotes_DB.py:3524, on every ChaChaNotes connection.

(1) Pure sqlite3, one INSERT with a bound BLOB inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT, callback does the same lstrip().split() work as the guard:
- 0.25 MiB: 0.1 ms without callback, 8.4 ms with it (0 triggers); 78 ms with 3 triggers.
- 1 MiB: 0.2 ms vs 37 ms (0 triggers); 1.0 ms vs 575 ms (3 triggers).
- 3 MiB: 0.7 ms vs 114 ms (0 triggers); 0.4 ms vs 814 ms (3 triggers).
- Callback count is 3 + 2 per trigger fired (9 with 3 triggers). CPython hands every callback sqlite3_expanded_sql, with the BLOB hex-encoded.

(2) Real CharactersRAGDB.add_message with the callback on vs cleared, interleaved runs, medians:
- 0.25 MiB image: 164 ms vs 20 ms
- 0.5 MiB: 354 ms vs 23 ms
- 1 MiB: 801 ms vs 23 ms
- 3 MiB: 1,933 ms vs 40 ms
- That is roughly +0.6 ms per KiB of image.
- A 1 MiB image insert fires 36 callbacks, and 12 of them carry a ~2.1 MB expanded string.
- A no-op `lambda s: None` callback costs the same as the real guard (492 vs 446 ms, vs 30 ms with none). The cost is SQLite expansion plus str creation in C, not the Python body.

(3) Scope correction: text and reads are NOT materially taxed.
- add_message text: 1 KB 17.0 vs 16.5 ms; 8 KB 15.7 vs 14.9 ms; 64 KB 25 vs 21.5 ms.
- add_note: 2 KB 12.6 vs 13.3 ms; 20 KB 18.3 vs 16.3 ms; 200 KB 25 vs 15 ms.
- 10k point SELECTs: 100-134 ms vs 101-174 ms, which is noise.
- So the "every write" framing is overstated. The real cost is specific to BLOB writes.
- console_trace_artifacts does not carry images: console_exchange_capture.py:93/398 stubs data: and base64 payloads. That trigger is not a real image path.

(4) Realistic image sizes. prepare_image_payload (chat_image_events.py:270-275) passes images of 2048 px or less through untouched, and resizes larger ones to 2048 px (PNG optimize / JPEG q85). Screenshots and photos therefore land at about 0.3-3 MiB, a stall of about 0.15-1.9 s per image. Position-0 images bind into the messages INSERT (15 triggers). The rest go through message_attachments executemany (console_dispatch_repository.py:170-200).

(5) Trigger trace:
- Default path, off the loop: exchange_capture defaults to true (config.py:3794/8507) and trace_normalized_writes defaults to True (config.py:8313-8316). The boundary factory is wired at console_runtime.py:3462. So a MANUAL/QUEUED send always gets a preparation (console_chat_controller.py:10509), goes to _accept_durable_turn (:11005), then _run_durable_db_call, which calls asyncio.to_thread for file-backed DBs (:11511-11512, :12069). The event loop is not frozen. The send itself stalls before provider dispatch (first token) by the time above, while holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
- Non-default path, on the loop: with capture turned off, an image-only draft (empty text) or an @/command-prefixed draft gets preparation=None, because _ordinary_library_text (:8888-8891) needs non-empty text. It then falls through to self.store.persist_message_if_needed(echoed_user.id) (:11081). That runs synchronously on the event loop via _persist_new_message_or_defer (console_chat_store.py:17281), a full UI freeze of the same 0.15-1.9 s per image.
- Rarer BLOB paths pay the same tax: character_cards (12 triggers), chatbook import, fork, and roleplay projection rewrites (console_chat_store.py:13583).

Verdict: it is real and large per image. It stays P1 rather than P0 because in the default config it stalls the image-send pipeline, not the loop, and only sends with images pay. The capture-off image-only sub-case is a real loop freeze that the fix should also cover. Fix caveats from the first verifier still apply: the generation counter backs a fail-closed guard, so every BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/executescript/commit()/implicit-rollback edge must be covered. A backstop that compares in_transaction before and after each statement in the cursor wrapper is the robust option.
fix: Stop using set_trace_callback. The connection runs with isolation_level=None, so every transaction is opened and closed by TransactionContextManager's explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. Bump authorization._transaction_generation there. As a backstop for raw BEGIN/COMMIT, check the unexpanded SQL text in the _QuiescentSQLiteCursor.execute wrapper, which already sees every statement. Add a regression test that inserts a 3 MiB BLOB and asserts it stays under ~50 ms.
fix_notes: The generation counter backs a fail-closed security guard (semantic-mutation authorization and the trace-GC delete lease), so a missed boundary is a correctness and security bug, not only a perf one. When moving the bump into TransactionContextManager, every other boundary path must be covered as well. That includes raw BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK through conn.execute and cursor.execute, and executescript (a separate method the execute wrapper does not see). It also includes Connection.commit()/rollback(): they issue COMMIT/ROLLBACK that the trace callback sees today. It also includes SQLite's implicit auto-rollback on SQLITE_FULL/IOERR/BUSY. A robust backstop is to compare connection.in_transaction before and after each statement in the _QuiescentSQLiteCursor wrapper and bump on every edge. Removing the production callback also stops tests that install their own set_trace_callback from silently replacing the guard. The regression test should pin both the timing (a 3 MiB BLOB insert under ~50 ms) and the generation advancing on every boundary path listed above. fix_risk is medium, bordering high.

title: Normalized trace re-projects every history message per provider call and base64-encodes every image in history; revision envelopes base64 attachments just to derive kind or compare equality
trigger: Once per provider call (every agent round) with capture on by default: stream_chat -> _reserve_trace_call (console_provider_gateway.py:5610) -> _LazyTraceBoundaryFactory -> ConsoleTraceBoundaryFactory.__call__ (console_trace_runtime.py:622, BEGIN IMMEDIATE) -> prepare_current_surface_delta (console_trace_service.py:2560) -> _resolve_reference_values over all active history keys. Plus once per add_message (ensure_current_revision, ChaChaNotes_DB.py:13572) and once per update_message (mutate_message, :13603).
cost: Code-verified: O(history) per provider call, with about 3 SELECTs per revision key, a full parent-surface re-projection per inherited key in forked sessions, and a base64 of every history image and attachment. Finder's measurement (not re-run): 27 ms and 55 MiB peak per call with 5x3 MiB images in a 100-message history, and 4.9 ms text-only. All of it is inside a ChaChaNotes write lock.
fix: Use a light envelope wherever only identity, kind or equality is needed. For example, `image_data IS NOT NULL`, attachment count and length or sha from SQL, or compare raw bytes, with no base64. Revisions are immutable, so cache projected provider values per (revision_id, live message version) on the long-lived trace service. Only base64 at the final provider-value boundary, and only for the entries being newly bound.

The cheapest safe first step is to hoist get_owner out of the per-key loop and batch the get_semantic_revision lookups into one IN query. A revision_id -> value cache is only valid while live_locator_retired_at IS NULL, because values resolve from the live messages row. Retired locators must still raise, and the cache must never be shared with trace/viewer readers because these values are unmasked. Comparing raw bytes instead of base64 must keep exact provider-byte equality, since the docstring invariant is that masking never alters provider bytes. The light envelope for _create_initial_revision/_content_kind is low risk: use `image_data IS NOT NULL` and an attachment EXISTS check. For mutate_message equality, compare the raw BLOBs, not base64.

title: web_fetch cache is bounded by entry count, not bytes; expired entries are never swept (up to 256 x 1-5 MiB retained for the process lifetime)
trigger: Once per web_fetch call and once per web_crawl page (opt-in tool gate); expired entries linger until the key is re-looked-up or the cache overflows.
cost: Estimated: bounded at 256 entries; realistically about 5-25 MB retained after the TTL; theoretical ceiling about 256 MiB at the default max_bytes.
fix: Add a byte budget, for example 32 MiB, summing len(text) and evicting the earliest expiry first. On each put, sweep entries past their expiry. Both happen under the existing _fetch_cache_lock.
fix_notes: Low risk. Sweeping expired entries inside _cache_put under the existing lock is a one-loop change. The byte budget should count len(text). Apply the same treatment to _search_cache_put (:1164).
reason: Code exists as quoted (web_tool_impls.py:139-142, :177, :215-226). Entries are dropped only on a re-lookup of the same key (:1032-1038) or on overflow. What gets cached is extracted text, not raw bodies: web_fetch at :1129, and the web_crawl warm-write at :1986, which bulk-populates the cache. The cache is hard-bounded at 256 entries (search cache: 128). The web tools are opt-in gated builtins, and typical extracted pages run 10-100 KB, so realistic retention is single- to low-double-digit MB. The 256 MiB worst case needs 256 distinct pages that each extract to about 1 MiB of text. This is a bounded cache with lazy TTL expiry, not an unbounded leak, so I downgraded it from P2 to P3.

title: Trace service surface-projection cache keeps one whole-surface projection per segment forever
trigger: Every successful normalized trace call replaces its segment's entry, and a new conversation or fork adds one. Entries are never evicted on success.
cost: Estimated, and higher than the finder's figure because the checkpoint pins _ParentState and _DescriptorRoot. A 200-node conversation is roughly 100-200 KB. Eviction must go through a helper that pops the entry and then calls _prune_unreferenced_parents, so no orphaned _ParentState is left behind. It must never evict the segment currently being admitted: :2716 indexes _parent_capabilities[id(checkpoint)] without a guard, so evicting that segment between the checkpoint lookup and use would KeyError. Evict only on insert of a different segment_id, under the factory RLock. An OrderedDict with about 32-64 entries is enough.

title: Every hosted LLM call builds and discards its own requests.Session, so connections are never reused across sends, agent turns or chunks
trigger: Every hosted, non-llama.cpp Console send (gateway worker thread -> chat_api_call -> chat_with_<provider>/hosted_chat_request -> owned_json_post). Every agent tool-loop turn (AgentService -> chat_api_call). Every summarization chunk (_post_with_retry, 7 sites). All run off the loop in worker threads.
cost:
Micro-benchmark (scratch/second-lens-network/bench_f1.py). Setup: a local TLS HTTP/1.1 server on 127.0.0.1; trust bundle = certifi + test CA, so each new connection pays the real certifi parse; requests 2.32.5 / urllib3 2.6.3; N=30. The 'current' shape copies hosted_chat.py:710-723: a fresh Session plus HTTPAdapter(Retry(total=0)) per POST, then close.

Results, median / p90:
- 0 ms RTT: current 15.58 / 20.71 ms; one reused Session 1.21 / 1.69 ms; fresh Session on a shared pooled adapter (the proposed fix) 1.24 / 1.68 ms.
- 40 ms RTT, injected by an in-process delay proxy: current 130.3 / 141.0 ms; reused 44.7 / 53.4 ms; fix shape 46.1 / 57.5 ms.
- So pooling saves about 85 ms per request at 40 ms RTT: 2 extra RTT for TCP + TLS 1.3, plus about 12 ms of CPU.
- create_urllib3_context + load_verify_locations(certifi) alone: 11.8-12.2 ms median per new connection.

Trigger, re-traced on 840ed2ca58:
- Every hosted-provider call goes stream_chat -> _stream_generic_chat (console_provider_gateway.py:6081) -> asyncio.to_thread(worker) (:6587) -> chat_api_call -> a new session.
- Agent turns take the same path. console_agent_bridge.py:3733 calls self._gateway.stream_chat once per model call, so every tool-loop turn pays a fresh handshake.
- Summarization uses _post_with_retry: 8 matches, the def plus 7 call sites.
- There are 26 requests.Session()/create_default_session()/build_requests_session() construction sites and 0 uses of pool_connections/pool_maxsize anywhere under tldw_chatbook. Nothing upstream pools.

Caveats that bound it, without refuting it:
1. All of this runs on worker threads, so it is time-to-first-token latency, not a UI freeze.
2. The saving is guaranteed for back-to-back agent turns and summarization chunks. For human-paced single sends it holds only while the idle keep-alive connection outlives the server or load-balancer idle timeout (often around 60 s).
3. As the first verifier found, HTTPAdapter.cert_verify still makes urllib3 reload certifi for every NEW connection even with a shared context. The fix wins by reusing connections, not by caching the context.

P1 stands: a per-send, per-turn and per-chunk cost of 15 ms of CPU plus 2 RTT, measured.
fix:
Pool the transport once, in Utils/egress.py:
- Add a module-level HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=16, pool_maxsize=16) whose init_poolmanager passes the cached ssl_context from F2.
- Mount it in create_default_session().
- Override DefaultTimeoutSession.close() so it closes only adapters that are not the shared one.

Replace the per-call session.mount(HTTPAdapter(max_retries=Retry(...))) calls (openai :950, anthropic :1750) with a small dict of shared adapters keyed by retry policy. hosted_chat's mount of Retry(total=0) is equivalent to the default adapter and can simply be deleted.

Keep per-call Session objects, so header/auth isolation and the tests that patch requests.Session.post are unchanged.
fix_notes: (1) Passing the cached ssl_context from F2 into init_poolmanager does NOT save the ~14 ms per connection with requests. HTTPAdapter.cert_verify always sets conn.ca_certs (the certifi path for verify=True), and urllib3 util/ssl_.py:459-461 then calls load_verify_locations on the shared context for every new connection. The win comes from connection reuse, not from the cached context, unless cert_verify is also overridden. (2) The shared adapter must survive Session.close(). Both `with create_default_session()` and OwnedSSEStream call close(), which closes every mounted adapter, so the close override the finder proposes is mandatory. (3) A pooled keep-alive connection combined with hosted_chat's Retry(total=0) on a non-idempotent POST means a connection the server dropped while idle surfaces as a send failure. urllib3's is_connection_dropped check before reuse is racy. Add a one-shot reconnect on connection-reset-before-response, or cap idle age. (4) Keep Session per call as proposed, so cookies and auth stay isolated. PoolManager is thread-safe across the gateway worker threads.
evidence:

session = create_default_session()
...
stream = OwnedSSEStream(response=response, session=session)  # session dies with the stream
# LLM_API_Calls.py:855 (openai streaming)
session_context = create_default_session()
# console_provider_gateway.py:6587
worker_task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(worker))  # worker -> self._chat_api_call
reason: The code matches the finding at every cited line on 840ed2ca58. hosted_chat.py:710 calls create_default_session() and mounts a fresh HTTPAdapter(Retry(total=0)); OwnedSSEStream owns the session and closes it. LLM_API_Calls.py lines 855, 950, 1750, 2718, 3559 and 4386, qwencloud.py:1176 and Summarization_General_Lib.py:1039 each build their own session per call. There are 7 _post_with_retry call sites plus the def. egress.py:1012 create_default_session returns a new DefaultTimeoutSession each time, with no shared adapter anywhere in the repo (no pool_connections/pool_maxsize usage). The Console path is confirmed: stream_chat -> _stream_generic_chat -> asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(worker)) at gateway:6587 -> chat_api_call. hosted_chat_request is used by openrouter, moonshot, deepseek, mistral, zai, groq and hosted_provider_engine. Installed requests 2.32.5 reverted the 2.32.0 preloaded SSLContext, so each new connection runs urllib3 create_urllib3_context plus load_verify_locations(certifi). I measured that at 12.2 ms median in isolation. The cost is off the event loop, on a worker thread, so it is time-to-first-token latency, not a UI freeze. No open task covers it: core-code-review-2026-09-17 report.md:3031 lists it only as an untimed hypothesis. P1 stands: it is a per-send cost of 10-20 ms or more on a hot path, and larger for back-to-back agent turns and summarization chunks.

title: Every httpx client builds a fresh SSLContext from certifi (12-24 ms), and about 15 sites construct one on the Textual event loop
trigger: Boot model-catalog refresh (a coroutine worker on the app loop, daily, per stale consented provider). User actions: settings Discover, endpoint and TTS probes, server-switch test, wizard probes, vLLM probe (on the loop). Every agent run's lifeline loop (off the loop, per send).
cost:
Micro-benchmarks (scratch/second-lens-network/bench_f2.py and bench_f2_gateway.py), run in the isolated env against the audit tree. Two runs each; the machine is noisy.

Construction cost, median / p90:
- httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30) with verify=True: 15.5-26.6 / 32-75 ms.
- httpx.Client(): 17.9-29.3 ms.
- AsyncHTTPTransport(): 13.4-13.5 ms.
- The audit tree's tls_trust.build_httpx_async_client(timeout=30): 15.1-18.2 / 35-60 ms.
- The same client with verify=<cached SSLContext>: 0.46-0.70 ms.
- ConsoleProviderGateway(config_provider=...): 16.98 / 37.69 ms, against 0.18 / 0.80 ms once httpx_verify returns a cached context. All of the gateway's construction cost is the SSLContext.

New, stronger on-loop trigger the first pass missed:
- chat_screen.py:16183 eagerly evaluates self._ensure_console_chat_controller(), inside _build_console_center.
- _build_console_center is called from compose_content (:16497).
- That runs ConsoleRuntime.ensure_provider_gateway -> ConsoleProviderGateway.__init__ (console_provider_gateway.py:2750) -> _new_owned_http_client (:3600) -> build_httpx_async_client.
- Result: about 17 ms (p90 about 38 ms) on the app loop during Console compose. That is first paint of the default and fallback landing screen (app.py:15966 falls back to TAB_CHAT), once per session. This meets the rubric's 'first paint or boot >=10-20 ms' bar for P1.

Boot catalog refresh: I simulated the 11-provider refresh_stale_configured_providers shape (a client per provider, then an awaited fetch) against a 1 ms heartbeat.
- Current: worst loop gap 23-70 ms, with 3-7 gaps longer than one frame.
- Cached context: worst gap 11.5-17 ms (machine noise), with 0-1 frame drops.
- This fires once per 24 h per stale, consented, keyed provider (plus OpenRouter).

Corrections to the first pass:
(a) The 'per agent send, off the loop' clause applies only to llama.cpp agent turns. For hosted providers, _stream_generic_chat uses requests (F1) and never touches _active_http_client.
(b) Off-loop construction barely disturbs the UI: a worker thread building clients back-to-back gave a median loop gap of 1.3 ms and p99 of 9-11 ms.

I enumerated all 56 httpx client and transport construction sites without truncation. None is per-keystroke, and none is per-send on the loop. The other on-loop sites are user-initiated probes (P2 on their own).

P1 holds on the strength of the per-session first-paint cost plus the daily boot refresh. The fix is low-risk: a cached context gives the 0.18 ms figure above.
fix:
In tls_trust, cache one ssl.SSLContext per normalized trust setting (functools.lru_cache keyed on the setting plus the custom CA's mtime/digest, cleared when [network] ssl_verify is saved). Make httpx_verify() and ssl_context_for_transport() always return that context, never a bare True.

Route the raw httpx.AsyncClient(...) sites (settings_endpoint_probe, server_switch_modal, FirstRunSetupWizard, first_run_voice_step_state, vllm_connection, monitoring_engine, local_watchlists_service) through build_httpx_async_client. This also stops them bypassing the TLS policy. Pass verify=ctx to llamacpp_bounded's AsyncHTTPTransport.

Caveat: httpcore calls set_alpn_protocols on the shared context for each connection. That is benign while every client is HTTP/1.1.
fix_notes: (1) httpx create_ssl_context honors SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR when verify=True and trust_env=True. A cached certifi context would silently drop that override for corporate users who rely on it, so key the cache on (setting, custom-CA digest, trust_env, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR) or reproduce that logic. (2) httpcore calls set_alpn_protocols on the shared context per connection (connection.py:147). I found 0 http2=True sites, so this is benign today; note it. (3) Invalidate the cache when [network] ssl_verify is saved and when the custom CA's content changes. (4) Routing the raw sites through build_httpx_async_client changes their TLS policy, which is correct but is a behaviour change. monitoring_engine's per-subscription ssl_verify=0 must still win through an explicit verify=. (5) requests_verify() for custom-CA users also re-parses the CA and sha256-hashes the files on every session. It could share the same cache.
reason: Confirmed at tls_trust.py:234-259. httpx_verify() returns a bare True/False for the default and disabled settings, so each httpx client runs httpx._config.create_ssl_context, which calls ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) per client. I measured: httpx.AsyncClient() median 37 ms (12.8 in the finder's run), httpx.Client() 36 ms, AsyncHTTPTransport() 12 ms, and AsyncClient(verify=cached ctx) 0.19 ms. The event-loop callers are real. (a) Boot: app.py:16041 _schedule_startup_model_catalog_refresh -> run_worker(self._refresh_model_catalogs), a coroutine worker -> refresh_stale_configured_providers loops the 11 AUTO_REFRESH_PROVIDER_LIST_KEYS -> discover_models -> discover_openai_compatible_models, which builds build_httpx_async_client at :878-880 per stale provider. That fires once per 24 h per keyed provider, plus OpenRouter without a key, and only after consent is recorded. (b) User-initiated probes: settings_endpoint_probe:634, server_switch_modal:225, FirstRunSetupWizard:951 and vllm_connection:614 all construct raw httpx.AsyncClient. local_server_discovery:580 runs only while Console setup is blocked. (c) Per agent run, off the loop: console_agent_bridge.py:6509 builds a new _ModelCallLifeline loop per run, and the gateway's per-loop cache (_active_http_client / _loop_clients) builds a new client for each loop. The repo has 54 raw httpx.Client/AsyncClient constructions against 13 routed through the builders. title: Watchlist runs build a fresh AsyncClient on the app loop for every feed and every sitemap/url_list URL, with no connection reuse
trigger: A due scheduled watchlist check through the scheduler coroutine worker on the app loop, or Check Now / Rerun (coroutine workers). One client per feed, and one per URL for url_list and sitemap.
cost: Client construction measured at 12-37 ms median per client, on the loop, times N URLs per run. The per-URL TCP+TLS handshake adds to run wall time only (estimated about 2 RTT per URL).

The cross-URL sharing can come later if it is ever measured. Any repair of the config read must also convert the timeout to ms (60 s -> 60000). Otherwise every scrape times out after 60 ms and burns all retries, each with its own browser launch. The test mocks use key names the code never reads (web_scraper_request_timeout, web_scraper_stealth_mode), so tests will not catch this.

title: WorkflowsScreen composes twice on every visit (whole-screen recompose after lazy authoring init)
trigger: Only the first Workflows visit per app run (and Retry after a failed authoring open). Subsequent visits construct with a ready controller and do not recompose.
cost: Estimated one extra BaseAppScreen compose, mount and layout (nav bar, footer, about 15 placeholder widgets) once per run, a few tens of ms. It is not per visit.
fix: Ensure authoring before the first compose (resolve the controller in the constructor or navigation step), or compose a placeholder region and mount only the authoring region once it is ready. Alternatively mark the route reusable.
fix_notes: Do not mark the route reusable as a cheap fix. on_unmount releases the drafts.subscribe and session.subscribe subscriptions, and reuse would need the TASK-24452 lifecycle audit. The cheaper options are to rebuild only the #workflow-authoring container (remove_children plus mount the authoring subtree) instead of the whole screen, or to await ensure_workflow_authoring in the navigation step before the screen is constructed. Either way, the focus capture and restore that BaseAppScreen.recompose() provides no longer happens; that is acceptable on first mount.

async def on_mount(self):
    if self.controller is None:
        await self._initialize_authoring()
...
        self.controller = WorkflowsController(...)
        await self.recompose()
reason: The code exists (workflows_screen.py:126-129 on_mount and 148-157 _initialize_authoring, which runs await self.recompose()), but the claimed trigger of 'every visit' is wrong. WorkflowsScreen.__init__ (lines 47-55) builds the controller from app.workflow_documents and app.workflow_drafts when both are set. ensure_workflow_authoring (app.py:19210-19223) sets them on the app, and nothing resets them; the only other assignment is the None initialisation at app.py:8168. The DB open itself is already offloaded (authoring.py:55-57 uses asyncio.to_thread). As a side effect the user briefly sees misleading 'Not ready · authoring owner unavailable' copy. title: Every storage admission re-walks directories from '/' with one open() per path component: 82k opens in TldwCli(), 70k on the loop at mount, ~4.9k/s at idle

cost:

The walk primitive (private_paths._open_verified_parent: open O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW + fstat + stat + close per component, from '/') measured 11 µs min and 33 µs p50 per component at load 36.

OVERLAP: with only F1's load_settings fast path (ARM=fast), idle main opens go 37k -> 0 and mount 69.5k -> 33k. So F2's always-on idle cost is the same money as F1.

What remains after F1 is boot-only. Ctor stays at 81.6k opens: 31 get_user_data_dir admissions at about 1.7k opens each (~52k), plus 6 DB-connect admissions. With a get_user_data_dir memo as well, the residual is about ctor 29k + mount 18k at depth 11. That is about 20-28k opens at real depth, or roughly 0.3-1.3 s of pre-ready main-thread time. That is still well above the 100 ms bar on boot, so P0 stands for the structural root.

- Not reproduced as exclusive: 'every >100 ms stall in the first 5 s after ready is inside pinned_directory/acquire_storage'. With the F1 fast path, main-thread admissions in the 8 s after ready dropped 99 -> 16, yet 9 lags over 100 ms remained (max 1.47 s). A 172 ms gen2, the screen pre-import thread and thread helper spawns share those stalls.
- Qualification JSON parsing and ctypes.CDLL per call are negligible (about 10 µs); the cost is the per-pin re-walk from '/'.
fix: Make the admission primitive O(1) per call. Hold a verified O_DIRECTORY fd for the recovery-bootstrap root and the data root for the process lifetime, re-validating with fstat (st_dev, st_ino, uid, mode) instead of an openat walk from '/'. Cache the parsed control-record and registry JSON keyed on (st_ino, st_mtime_ns, st_size). Load the installed native_qualification.json and the libc fstatfs handle once at module level. This needs an ADR-126/127 amendment, since TASK-32920 already saw a 460 ms pinned_directory boot stall and TASK-32562 recorded the Windows analogue (391k native opens).
fix_notes: Part of the proposed fix is negligible. I measured _Evidence.model_validate_json at 5 µs and ctypes.CDLL(None) at 4 µs per call, so caching the qualification JSON and the libc handle saves ~10 µs per admission. The cost is the openat walks from '/'. A process-lifetime O_DIRECTORY fd re-validated only by fstat does NOT prove the path still resolves to that inode after an ancestor rename or symlink swap, which weakens the ADR-126/127 no-follow guarantee. TASK-32562's owner has explicitly refused validation caches, so this needs an ADR amendment and owner sign-off. A lower-risk lever: within one admission, pin the shared ancestor once and openat relative to it, instead of re-walking from '/' for each of the ~9-10 pins per acquire_storage. That keeps per-operation freshness and dedupes walks. Cache the parsed records/registry only keyed on the pinned fd's (st_ino, st_mtime_ns, st_size) observed in the same operation.

title: No GC tuning at boot: 4 gen2 collections during mount (517 ms, max 179 ms), a 153 ms gen2 in the first idle seconds, 520k tracked objects
trigger: Yes. Allocation-driven automatic collections on the main thread during import (measured), construction and mount. Later gen2 passes rescan the long-lived boot heap on screen visits.
cost:
gc.callbacks timing across 10 isolated boots.

BASE and FAST arms:
- Import: 3 gen2 passes (about 10, 20-25 and 30-80 ms), 118-192 ms of total import GC.
- Mount (main thread): exactly 4 gen2 passes every run, totalling 439-537 ms, max 134-210 ms.
- After ready: one more gen2 of 166-489 ms within 8 s (main or worker thread; both hold the GIL), and sometimes a 366 ms gen2 while typing.
- About 610-617k tracked objects after idle. There is no GC policy in the code (0 gc.freeze/set_threshold/disable in tldw_chatbook).

COUNTERFACTUALS (warm profile, 1 run each):
- gc.freeze at _ui_ready (the finder's main proposal): mount is unchanged (4 gen2, 476 ms), since the freeze comes after. The one-off collect+freeze costs 143 ms and freezes 500k objects. Later gen2 passes shrink 4-5x (settle 36 ms vs 166-179, typing 49 ms).
- Bracket (gc.disable from before import to _ui_ready, then collect+freeze+enable): 0 GC pauses in import, ctor and mount, and one 222 ms collect at ready. Settle gen2 was 33 ms. Mount main CPU was 5.1 s vs 5.9-6.0 s. Net saving is about 600 ms of boot-window pauses.
- Freeze right after ctor: mixed. Mount was 268 ms in the warm run vs 465 ms in the fresh run, and the gen2 count rose 4 -> 5 via the 3.12 long_lived_total heuristic. Do not rely on it.

The cost is real and fixable. P1 holds: known TASK-31966 (ADR required), boot-phase scope new. The fix note should prefer the disable-bracket through mount plus freeze at ready, since freeze-at-ready alone leaves the ~480 ms of mount pauses.
fix: Run gc.collect() then gc.freeze() once at _ui_ready (app.py:16160), or right after TldwCli() construction, so the ~0.5M long-lived boot objects move to the permanent generation. Optionally gc.disable() across import and ctor, then re-enable. TASK-31966 requires an ADR before any global GC policy change, so file the boot measurement there.
fix_notes: TASK-31966 AC#2 requires an approved ADR first. Freezing at _ui_ready also freezes the first Console widget tree. Textual parent/child cycles mean that tree can never be collected once the Console re-mints its widgets (TASK-24452), a one-time bounded leak. Prefer gc.collect()+gc.freeze() right after TldwCli() construction and before mount (import plus ctor objects only), or pair it with a later unfreeze. A gc.disable()/enable() bracket around import and construction is the lowest-risk slice. On 3.12, freezing changes the long_lived_total heuristics, so measure net pause frequency.

title: The Console gateway builds its httpx.AsyncClient (httpcore import + SSLContext) eagerly at mount, and the TLS factory rebuilds an SSLContext for every client

The other construction sites are console_launch_wake.py:197 (same runtime, same once-only) and personas_preview_controller.py:437 (a second gateway, on a Personas visit). Per-send (a correction: it is per RUN, not per turn): per the console_agent_bridge.py:3109-3131 docstring, one lifeline loop is created per run_reply (2445), and the gateway's per-loop cache (3658-3697) builds a new client for it. 4. Moving the 30 raw per-call sites onto a shared client is separate, lower-value work: those are mostly cold paths, some already off the loop.

title: Each open terminal session busy-polls: runtime loop at 200 Hz and input flusher at 100 Hz (beyond the known 50 Hz monitor)
trigger: From the moment an armed terminal session starts until it is closed, one runtime thread polls at about 200 Hz nominal (162 Hz actual on macOS) and one flusher thread at 100 Hz nominal (about 83 Hz actual). This happens whether or not the pane is visible, including at an idle prompt.
fix:
1. Block the runtime thread in `selectors`/`select.select` on the PTY master fd plus a self-pipe that `take_input`, stop and close write to. It then wakes only on output, input or exit. As a stopgap, back off exponentially from 5 ms to about 100 ms while `worked` stays False.
2. For the flusher, call `_input_pending.wait()` with no timeout, and have `close` set `_input_pending` after `_close_requested`.

Related to open TASK-31503, which covers only the monitor; these are new sites.
fix_notes:
- **selectors/self-pipe rework (medium risk).**
  - When the output actor has no credit (`next_read_size<=0`), the PTY fd must NOT be in the read set, or the loop busy-spins on a readable fd.
  - Wakeups are then needed from input admission (`take_input` source), credit restoration (`process_output`), stop, and the shell reaper (`_shell_reaped`). That is four or more producers writing the self-pipe.
- **Backoff stopgap:** `stop.wait()` cannot be woken by input today, so a 100 ms max backoff adds up to 100 ms to keystroke echo and output unless input admission and credit restoration also set a wake Event.
- **Flusher:** `request_priority_close` already sets `_input_pending` after `_close_requested` (posix_backend.py:618-625), so an untimed `wait()` is safe on that path. Any exit path that skips `request_priority_close` would park the daemon thread forever: no CPU, but one leaked thread per session. Make EOF/finalize set the event too.
evidence:

while not stop.is_set():
    event = self.take_input(session_id) ... chunk = self._read_runtime_output(...)  # non-blocking os.read -> BlockingIOError
    active, exit_code = self._poll_runtime_exit(...)  # wait_for_shell_exit(timeout_seconds=0.0)
    if not worked: stop.wait(_RUNTIME_POLL_SECONDS)

title: Auto-wake cancel probe runs a BEGIN IMMEDIATE write transaction and is polled at up to 20 Hz; the deadline watcher opens a fresh SQLite connection every 250 ms
trigger:
During an automatically woken fleet delivery:
- the watcher runs at 4 Hz for the delivery;
- the settle and wait_agents loops run at 20 Hz while the woken run waits on or settles sub-agents.

These run on the worker thread and the to_thread pool, never the UI loop.
cost:
A raw SQLite simulation of the probe shape (WAL, synchronous=FULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE + savepoint + 3 SELECT + 2 UPDATE + COMMIT) on APFS measured:
- 0.14 ms on a held connection;
- 0.34 ms with a per-probe open and close.

At ≈24 probes/s that is <1% of a core off-loop, plus ≈24 small fsync'd WAL commits/s. Linux fsync may be costlier.
fix:
1. Split the probe into a cheap in-memory check (cancel event, wall-clock deadline, the kill-switch setting via the cached get_cli_setting) evaluated at poll cadence, and a durable `check_active` limited to about 1 Hz or step boundaries.
2. Observe through a deferred (read) transaction, not BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
3. Keep one connection for the watcher instead of `run_owned_db_call` per tick.
fix_notes:
- **A deferred read transaction is not a drop-in change.** `check_active` intentionally WRITES `last_observed_at` (the clock-reversal and elapsed-time anchor) and re-activates status; the docstring says 'Observe elapsed/live bounds durably'.
- **Safe cut:** keep the in-memory cancel/Stop event at poll cadence and run the durable `check()` at ≤1 Hz or at step boundaries. That raises kill-switch and wall-budget enforcement latency from about 50 ms to the durable cadence; state that tradeoff explicitly.
- **Watcher:** reuse one held connection, or skip `operation_owned_connection`, to stop the 4 Hz reopen.

def check_active(...): with self._admission_transaction(chain_id) as conn:  # transaction(): BEGIN IMMEDIATE
while self._pending_handles(fleet, settling):
    if should_cancel() or (self._automatic_work is not None and self._automatic_work.should_cancel()) ...
    time.sleep(_FLEET_POLL_SECONDS)  # 0.05
# fleet_wake: while True: await asyncio.sleep(0.25); await run_owned_db_call(ledger._db, context.check)

Verified on 840ed2ca58:
- `AutomaticWorkContext.should_cancel` → `check()` (automatic_work_runtime.py:79-104) runs `read_attempt` + `_setting('autowake_enabled')` + `ledger.check_active`.
- `check_active` (DB/automatic_work.py:397) runs `_admission_transaction` → `transaction()` (:60-80): PRAGMA synchronous=FULL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE + SAVEPOINT.
- `_check_admission` then ALWAYS issues two UPDATEs (last_observed_at, status='active'). So every probe is a durable fsync'd write commit, not just a lock.

Poll sites:
- `_settle_fleet` (agent_service.py:3980-3991), 50 ms sleep, on the agent worker thread.
- `wait_agents` (:6402-6447) through the run-wide probe, which `_run_owned` wraps with `automatic_work.should_cancel` (:4770-4772).

All of this runs only when `current_automatic_work()` is set, i.e. auto-woken fleet deliveries, and all of it is off the event loop.

Severity downgraded to P3: the measured per-probe cost is sub-millisecond, and the path is the opt-in autowake/fleet flow. No open task covers it; TASK-31501 is the analogous 1 Hz shape for trace maintenance.

title: Recovery admission is reacquired from scratch per model call, per tool call and per guard nesting level
known_task: TASK-32860 (related consolidation only; no perf scope)
trigger: Per tool call (a fresh thread plus a full reacquire), per model call (async_worker_guard on the private run loop, before the first token), and per run (4 nested execution levels on the agent thread), plus per fleet child.

I confirmed model calls run on a private 'console-agent-loop' _ModelCallLifeline thread (bridge:6509-6520, 3882), not on the Textual loop. Adopting it needs check_states and a security review or ADR, which is why fix_risk is high. Lower-risk levers: (a) drop the redundant nested @guarded on _run_one when it runs under a guarded run_turn, since each level re-observes and re-enters execution_scope for every source; (b) make acquire_storage/execution_scope cheaper for an already-leased path; (c) keep one admitted lease bundle per run only if the security owner agrees. Do not gate on 'viewed run is streaming' alone: the tick also runs for background sessions, and the banner reflects the viewed session. Reusing the cached result for the send-path preflight is riskier, because dispatch must validate the lineage at send time. Keep that path live or re-validate the token there.

title: assistant_canvas_html_blocks runs a fresh MarkdownIt parse of the selected message 2–3 times per transcript refresh (5 Hz while streaming)
trigger: Streaming poll at 0.2 s -> _sync_native_console_transcript -> refresh_key differs because content grew -> transcript.refresh_messages -> _transcript_rows -> _flat_transcript_rows -> _action_row_signature + _action_guide -> 2x action_groups -> 2x MarkdownIt parse of the selected completed assistant message. fix: Add an exact fast path: `if '```' not in content and '~~~' not in content: return ()`. A CommonMark fence cannot exist without one of these, so most messages skip the parse. Optionally have ConsoleTranscript compute _action_groups once per rebuild and reuse it for the signature, guide and row.

The real fix is memoization keyed by (message.id, message.status, message.content), for example a small functools.lru_cache on a helper taking (id, content), since the result depends only on role, status, id and content. Hoist a module-level MarkdownIt instance. Computing _action_groups once per plan build is optional; memoizing the parse alone removes more than 99% of the cost. The same parse is reused by the :142 and :1000 call sites, which also benefit.

title: Launch-wake discovery full-scans agent_runs on the event loop at every boot (twice when results are pending), plus an N+1 seed on the loop
trigger: Every boot where autowake is on (the default) and agent_runs.db exists. That file is created by any Console agent-mode use. The second pass plus the N+1 seed only happen when discovery found pending results, which is rarer.
cost: Replicated in scratch with stdlib sqlite3, using the real agent_runs schema, both indexes and the exact query, with a new read-only connection per run on a warm cache. The plan is 'SCAN child USING INDEX idx_agent_runs_conversation' plus 'SEARCH parent USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_agent_runs_1'. 5k rows (4 MB): 6.4-7.4 ms. 20k rows (16 MB): about 42 ms. 20k rows (94 MB): 44.5 ms. 10k rows (47 MB): 16.5 ms. title: resolve_for_send probes the llama.cpp server over HTTP on every call, and modal opens await it just to compute a thinking-history policy
trigger: Each llama.cpp send makes one /health round trip before dispatch. Opening the Alt+M popover or the Console settings modal on a llama session waits for the probe (and for F2's config admissions) before the modal appears.

Note that removing the probe entirely changes UX: today an unreachable server produces a friendly pre-send 'unreachable' block rather than a dispatch error. For the modal path, a probe-free resolve changes semantics slightly: effective_thinking_history_policy_for_session currently returns `saved` when the server is unreachable (not ready), and would instead compute the continuation-derived policy. That is arguably more correct, but confirm the modal tests.

title: ConsoleProviderGateway builds an httpx.AsyncClient (SSL/certifi context) eagerly in __init__ on the UI loop, even though only llama.cpp paths use it and per-loop clients are built anyway

title: Canvas policy watcher polls at 4 Hz for the whole app lifetime, hopping to a thread each tick to read a 2 us cached value
trigger: Runs for the whole process lifetime from App.on_mount at 4 Hz, whether or not Canvas is used. Canvas defaults to enabled, so the loop never exits.

title: The llama.cpp stream loop re-parses each SSE line 2-3 times and sanitizes every chunk, although the joined reply is re-sanitized at close
trigger: Per streamed chunk on the app loop for llama.cpp. The redundant second parse applies only when thinking is displayable or local_structured_thinking is set. The third (usage) parse applies only to automatic/prepared generations. The per-chunk capture sanitize applies only with trace_legacy_writes=true (default off). The generic-branch double parse is on a to_thread worker.
cost: Measured: one json.loads of a typical llama.cpp SSE chunk costs 3.75 us. The default-path waste is about one redundant parse plus envelope sizing, roughly 5-8 us per chunk and under 10 ms across a 1k-chunk reply. That is far below any perceptible threshold, so this is hygiene only.
fix: Parse each SSE line once and pass the dict to the usage, thinking and content extractors. Drop the per-chunk sanitize, since the aggregate is sanitized in `_flight_capture` (keep budget accounting by length). Size string items by `len(item.encode())` without building a JSON envelope, and hoist the settlement constant to module scope or cache it.
fix_notes: Parse-once is safe: parse data once and hand the Mapping to _maybe_record_usage, _structured_local_thinking and the content extractor. Do not hoist the settlement import to module scope: _max_trace_accumulated_bytes is a deliberate ADR-097 boot-ratchet lazy import. Cache the int instead (functools.cache or a module-level memo). Dropping the per-chunk sanitize has little value because it is default-off. It would also keep raw, unsanitized chunks in the in-flight capture memory until close, and it would charge capture_budget on raw sizes. Output stays correct because _flight_capture re-sanitizes both completed and in-flight tails, but it weakens defence in depth, so leave it alone. Sizing string items by len(encode) needs a matching allowance for the envelope and escaping overhead, or the accumulation cap drifts.

Every delta returns _evidence_update -> _update -> _envelope(), and project_thinking immediately passes update.envelope to store.replace_message_thinking, so the full text is needed on every delta anyway. The safe, high-value fix is to skip the redundant _bounded_text full encode on the append path, for example with a trusted internal constructor or object.__setattr__ on a validated copy. The byte caps are already enforced exactly and incrementally at 177-186. That removes the dominant cost (the encode), while the remaining concat is a cheap memcpy. (c) bench_f3_loop.py: the spawn does not stall the asyncio loop (max heartbeat gap 5.5-6.6 ms at both 108 MB and 949 MB parent RSS; macOS uses posix_spawn). So this is added latency plus CPU, not a UI freeze: about 3 x 60-100 ms added before the first token on every default-route model call and every tool-loop iteration, independent of conversation size, plus about 200 ms of child CPU per call. That is a stall of at least 100 ms on the common send path, so P0 stands. Blind spot: the reference latency gate in Tests/Benchmarks/test_console_trace_call_latency.py runs reserve and mark on the main test thread, which holds a registered handle, so it never exercises the spawn. Tests/Chat/test_console_trace_runtime.py::test_real_gateway_and_settlement_release_operation_owned_handles pins the per-operation release, so a fix must keep handles off dead threads by using one long-lived registered writer thread, not by skipping the release.
fix: Give trace writes one long-lived registered connection: a runtime-owned single-thread executor (for example ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix='trace-writer')) whose connection stays registered with the quiescence registry, so backup and VACUUM can still quiesce it. fix_notes: A dedicated long-lived trace-writer thread (ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)) whose handle stays registered with the quiescence registry is the right shape, because the registry already tolerates held idle handles like the main thread's. The reservation must also route there, since it currently runs on the per-turn lifeline thread. Cross-thread submission from the lifeline loop via run_in_executor is fine. Keep the factory RLock semantics. Do NOT fix this by caching the helper's prepare result per path: the helper exists to validate path privacy without opening inodes locally, and caching reopens the TOCTOU window it closes. The same churn hits the 1 Hz maintenance loop (F7) and GC (F6) through run_owned_db_call, so one shared fix covers all three.

title: Trace GC re-marks the entire reachable ledger in BEGIN IMMEDIATE every 60 s after any send: O(total history) background work that blocks on-loop trace writes
trigger: The console_runtime maintenance loop, at most once per 60 s after any send (the epoch changes every call), only when no provider stream is active. It runs off-loop through run_owned_db_call but holds the ChaChaNotes write lock for the whole mark and sweep.
cost: bench_f6.py builds the ledger with REAL Capture-On sends through the real gateway, factory and settlement, in 15-send conversations (user 300 B, assistant 1.2 KB). It then times the real TraceGarbageCollector.collect (mark plus sweep, each in BEGIN IMMEDIATE) after one more send, median of 3. Results: 511 calls (5.6k ledger rows): 93 ms wall / 73 ms CPU. 1k calls (11k rows): 109 / 101 ms. 2k calls (22k rows): 226 / 182 ms. 4k calls (44k rows): 447 / 339 ms. That is linear at about 10 us per ledger row, or about 110 us per lifetime call (about 11 rows per call: about 5 events, 1 call, 1 response link, about 2 surface nodes and 2 revisions). Load avg was 40-100. One send advanced current_graph_epoch from 0 to 11, which confirms that every send changes the epoch. The console_runtime maintenance loop (3298-3395) therefore runs a full O(history) collect at most once per 60 s after any activity, whenever the provider is idle. Extrapolated: about 2.2 s of write-locked work per active minute at 20k calls, and about 5.5 s at 50k. It runs off-loop through run_owned_db_call, and each such call also pays the F3 helper spawn. The UI freezes only when a send-time UI-thread write (message save, admit_message_provenance, direct-route reservation) lands inside the window and waits on busy_timeout. The cost is not constant at idle, since nothing runs without an epoch change, so P1 rather than P0. TASK-31501 covers only the 1 Hz legacy poll. No open task covers this GC.
fix: Only schedule GC when an orphaning mutation happened. Sends only append reachable rows, so keep a separate 'reclaimable' epoch bumped by detach, purge, replacement, or retention expiry, not by every revision. Chunk mark and sweep into bounded short transactions. Also pause GC while a turn is being prepared (the pause_trace_maintenance_dispatch hook exists for VACUUM; extend it to logical GC). This is new scope beyond TASK-31501's 1 Hz poll.
fix_notes: A separate 'reclaimable' epoch has to cover every orphaning path: detach, purge, replacement, retention expiry (time-based, so it needs a timer or next-expiry check rather than a mutation bump), and calls leaving open states that previously pinned segments as roots. Missing one silently stops reclamation. Chunking mark into short transactions breaks the single-snapshot reachability guarantee that the epoch check relies on; sweep already re-checks the epoch, so chunked marks must invalidate on any epoch change. Extending pause_trace_maintenance_dispatch to logical GC is reasonable.

title: Legacy trace maintenance 1 Hz tick costs 6-9 ms CPU per tick in steady state, not '3 SELECTs' (about 0.6-0.9 % of a core idle, forever)
trigger: Always on after the first Console chat-store creation, for every profile with a ChaChaNotes DB: 1 Hz for the life of the process with no idle, visibility or config gate.
cost: Isolated scratch env (real CharactersRAGDB and LegacyTraceMaintenance, migration logical_complete, loguru sinks removed, load avg about 45 on 18 cores). Scripts are in scratch/sl13-f7f9/ (bench_f7.py, duty_f7.py). (1) Production path `await run_owned_db_call(db, m.run_batch)` (console_runtime.py:3290): 30/30 ticks spawned the `python -I -S private_sqlite_helper_entry.py` child (CountingPopen). Per tick: median parent CPU 37 ms, child CPU 50.6 ms, wall 162 ms. Every tick also runs close_connection, which does `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. Measured over 20 s at the real 1 s cadence: 3.30% of a core in the process plus 4.13% in the child, 7.43% total. (2) Best case, where the executor thread keeps its handle (plain to_thread on a 1-thread pool): 1/30 spawns (the first tick only), median 13.3 ms CPU per tick (min 7.8 ms), about 1.2-1.4% of a core over 20 s. Almost all of that is the F9 admission walk: the same transaction with `_core_operation` bypassed costs 0.02 ms. (3) Does production avoid the spawn? I pre-seeded an 8-thread default pool with K threads holding unowned ChaChaNotes handles. The asyncio default executor hands idle ticks out round-robin (FIFO), so the tick visits every pool thread in turn. Spawns tracked exactly (8-K)/8: K=0 gave 30/30, K=2 gave 23/30, K=4 gave 16/30, K=6 gave 8/30. A tick avoids the spawn only if EVERY pool thread holds a handle. The pool is never reaped, and 997 to_thread sites across many DBs feed it, against only 25 run_owned_db_call and 37 operation_owned_connection sites, so some threads will lack a handle and spawns are effectively guaranteed at some rate. Real-profile adjustment: the admission part shrinks by about 55% at a real HOME depth (see F9), so expect about 0.5% of a core with no spawns and about 5-6% with every tick spawning (the child CPU does not depend on path depth). The P0 bar (more than about 1% of a core at idle) is met at any spawn rate of about 7% or more of ticks, and it is a 1 Hz fork/exec plus a write-lock BEGIN IMMEDIATE and a WAL truncate for the life of the process. Gating verified: runs whenever chachanotes_db has .transaction (console_runtime.py:3119, 3218), with no idle, visibility or config gate. The loop also makes an extra owned call (current_graph_epoch) every 60 s. TASK-31501's premise ('asyncio.to_thread ... 3 SELECTs') is stale and should get these numbers. Fix note stands: park the loop on logical_complete with an event wake. A 30-60 s backoff alone still spawns once per wake.

fix_notes: Add the helper-spawn-per-tick evidence to TASK-31501. It also makes that task's premise ('asyncio.to_thread ... 3 SELECTs') stale. Parking the loop once logical_complete, with an event-driven wake from the legacy exchange writer, removes both the write lock and the spawn. Backing off to 30-60 s still spawns once per wake unless the F3 held trace-writer connection is used. A read-only (non-immediate) completeness check alone does not stop the connection churn.

title: With a custom PII ruleset, the on-loop prefix match spawns one regex-worker subprocess per PRIOR provider artifact on every send
trigger: Only when [console] exchange-capture PII redaction is enabled with a runnable custom ruleset. Then every agent tool-loop model call spawns once per prior tool-call/tool-result artifact inside the write-locked reservation. With the builtin ruleset, redact_pii_value re-runs in-process per artifact (CPU only).
cost: Estimated, not measured end to end. The spawn mechanism is the same shape as the private-sqlite helper I measured at about 45 ms child CPU per interpreter start, so about 1.8 s for 40 prior artifacts at iteration 20, while holding the write lock.
fix: New site for TASK-31505. Do not recompute the projection for prior artifacts: the durable artifact already stores the projected bytes. Compare incoming raw values against a cached (artifact_id -> projected digest) computed once at persist time, or memoize the projection per (revision_id, value digest) for the session. Move any remaining spawn off-loop and outside the transaction, as the task's ACs require.
fix_notes: durable_values[key] already holds the persisted projected bytes, so the incoming raw value only needs to be projected once per (policy revision, value) and memoized. An in-process memo scoped to the turn or run is the safest option. Persisting a digest of RAW pre-projection content in the DB would store a fingerprint of PII-bearing text, so use a keyed HMAC or keep the memo in memory only. Any remaining spawn must happen before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, as TASK-31505's ACs require. Folding this site into TASK-31505 is better than filing a separate task.

title: Turn configuration snapshot deep-copies config, world books and dictionaries at capture, then re-freezes the already-frozen snapshot per execution context (2-3x per send)
trigger: Every send: capture at the wiring.py:271 submit path, then re-freeze at the controller's _finalize_turn_execution_context (console_chat_controller.py:22820). Both run on the loop. There is an extra re-freeze on promotion (:8313) and on a new attempt (console_turn_preparation.py:211/403), not on every send.
cost: Measured in an isolated env under load: 10.3 ms to freeze and 10.8 ms to re-freeze for 3x300 world-book entries plus 200 dictionary entries; 2.5 us for an empty payload. That is 2x per send, so about 20 ms on the loop for heavy lorebooks and negligible otherwise.
fix: In _freeze, return immutable scalars (str, int, float, bool, None, bytes, enums) as-is and return MappingProxyType or tuple values that _freeze itself produced unchanged (keep a module-level WeakSet or marker, or re-freeze only mutable containers). Have _detached_configuration and _execution_context_with_attempt copy an already-detached snapshot (dataclasses.replace with a skip-refreeze flag, or object.__new__ plus slot copy) instead of re-running __post_init__.
fix_notes: The proposed WeakSet marker does not work: MappingProxyType is not weakref-able (verified: 'cannot create weak reference to mappingproxy object'). An id()-based set is unsafe after GC. The safer and shorter fix: in `_detached_configuration`, when `type(configuration) is ConsoleTurnConfigurationSnapshot`, return the instance itself. It is frozen, and every field is already detached by its own `__post_init__`. Failing that, copy slots through object.__new__ and skip `__post_init__`. The scalar short-circuit in `_freeze` is safe only for exact immutable types (str, int, float, bool, None, bytes, Enum). Keep deepcopy for any other leaf. Separately, the capture calls _collect_active_world_books and the world-book manager, which opens one ChaChaNotes transaction per book on the loop. title: mark_response_started runs a synchronous BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the event loop when the first streamed chunk arrives

The durable state must also be RESPONSE_STARTED before settlement advances it. If the marker is offloaded, settlement has to await that future, or both have to run on the same single-thread executor. title: ConsoleTraceService._surface_ref_cache retains one full surface projection per conversation segment for the process lifetime
trigger: Each distinct conversation segment sent to with Capture-On adds or replaces one entry in the process-lived service. Entries are never evicted by size.

On a miss, `_surface_projection` rebuilds from the paged nodes, but a checkpoint-bearing projection from :2409 is not re-derivable by that path. Verify this before evicting checkpointed entries, or evict only entries with checkpoint=None.

title: Console library-activity snapshot costs turns x rows, strictly re-decodes every library row, and fetches all trajectory rows synchronously on the UI loop on every message-selection keypress and every send
trigger: j/k (action_select_next/previous), click-select, or clear-selection in the Console transcript -> call_later(_notify_selection_changed) -> _sync_console_control_bar -> sync_projection -> store.library_activity_snapshot(), synchronous on the event loop.
