title: Root cause (outside the slice): every ScheduledTasksDB operation starts a private-sqlite helper child process, 39-46 ms per call against 0.6 ms for plain sqlite
trigger: Every service.db.* call in the Schedules workbench (F1-F5), the scheduler loop, the sync engine, and any other store that opens per operation on macOS/Linux.
cost:
MEASURED in an isolated scratch profile (scratch/l2-f7/bench*.py; HOME/XDG/TLDW_CONFIG_PATH in scratch, TLDW_TEST_MODE=1, audit tree 840ed2ca58, py3.12). The machine was heavily loaded during the runs (load avg 23-43), so absolute numbers run about 1.5x the first pass's quieter 39-51 ms. The ratios hold.

PER OPERATION (median of 30, Popen counter patched in): _get_connection+close 65.9 ms; list_task_runs 62.2; get_sync_state 77.6; count_unread_results 72.0; get_conflicts 72.7; list_reminder_tasks 71.7; list_automation_definitions 74.4. Each made exactly 1.0 helper spawn per call. A raw sqlite3 connect+WAL/sync PRAGMAs+query took 0.47-0.87 ms, and a bare `python -I -S -c pass` spawn took 13.7 ms.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (new evidence): stubbing prepare_in_helper drops get_sync_state from 85.6 to 30.9 ms (min 17.2), so the helper child is about 55-65% of the cost. Nearly all of the rest is the Backup_Recovery storage admission. acquire_storage runs twice per op: once from _core_transaction/_core_operation around connection()/transaction(), and once from the _with_storage_admission wrapper on connect_private_sqlite. cProfile counted 502 posix.open() syscalls per get_sync_state (pinned_directory/_open_verified_parent walks, control-record reads).

THE PROPOSED FIX IS NOT ENOUGH ALONE: a HELD connection that still enters _core_operation per op costs 14.2 ms median (min 9.5) and still makes 245 open() calls per op. That admission is per OPERATION, not per connection. The same held connection with no admission costs ~0.0 ms.

SEQUENCES (median of 20, 4 spawns each): boot sequence 282.6 ms (252-425), 81.6 ms with the helper stubbed. Schedules-mount sequence 300.0 ms (275-349), 83.1 ms with the helper stubbed.

EXHAUSTIVE TRACE of the event-loop triggers (unoffloaded synchronous opens):
(1) BOOT, every launch.
- TldwCli.__init__ (app.py:7738) -> _wire_watchlists_and_notifications_services (:8121/:10351) -> ScheduledTasksDB(...) at :10469. The constructor's warm _schema_is_current makes 1 open, before first paint.
- App.on_mount (app.py:14734) calls self.scheduling_service.db.reconcile_stale_automation_runs(...) synchronously at :15027. That is 1 transaction open on the loop.
- :15045 asyncio.create_task(recover_inflight_transfers()) runs on the loop. Its sync bodies _recover_stuck_definitions -> db.list_automation_definitions (scheduling_service.py:2166) and _recover_stuck_reminders -> db.list_reminder_tasks (:2216) make 2 more opens on the loop.
- Total: 4 spawns on the boot path, 3 of them on the event loop.
(2) EVERY Schedules VISIT. The 'schedules' ScreenRoute (screen_registry.py:128) is NOT reusable=True, so on_mount runs on every visit.
- on_mount (schedules_workbench.py:~829) calls _refresh_owner_select -> db.get_sync_state (:4590), _refresh_conflicts_badge -> db.get_conflicts (:5013), and _refresh_results_badge -> db.count_unread_results (:5040), all synchronously.
- _request_tasks_refresh -> run_worker(coroutine, NOT a thread) -> load_tasks -> `await service.list_tasks(...)`, whose body calls self.db.list_reminder_tasks synchronously (scheduling_service.py:606) on the loop.
- _refresh_server_reachability's _probe coroutine (:4739) calls _refresh_owner_select -> get_sync_state again on the loop.
- Total: 5 helper spawns on the event loop per visit, about 5 x 40-85 ms = 200-425 ms of freeze.
- Correctly offloaded (not counted): list_automation_results/list_automation_definitions via asyncio.to_thread (:1362, :1425), and the orphan settle (:4700).
(3) Not hot: the SchedulerLoop tick (30 s) keeps DB work in _offload/to_thread (loop.py:233-235), and the queue reloads every 60 ticks. There is no idle background tax.

The only prepare_in_helper call site is private_sqlite.py:1878. HelperLease.start (private_sqlite_process.py:366) Popens a fresh child every time, with no per-path cache or reuse. No test-mode or env bypass exists, and no backlog task covers the helper spawn or acquire_storage cost (grepped backlog/tasks).

VERDICT: P0 stands. Boot pays about 120-250 ms of loop-blocking helper spawns on every launch, and every Schedules visit freezes the loop for about 200-425 ms. Both are well over the 100 ms common-path bar.

Fix-plan corrections:
(a) A held connection alone leaves about 10-14 ms and 245 open() calls per op from per-operation admission, which is still about 50-70 ms for a 5-op visit. The admission scope check needs its own caching or cheapening, or the 5 visit and 3 boot call sites should simply move to asyncio.to_thread. That is the smallest diff that removes the UI freeze.
(b) Caching the helper verdict is security-sensitive, as the first verifier said.
(c) acquire_storage's roughly 250 open() calls per admission is an app-wide tax on every admitted store operation, not only this store. The DB-layer and Backup_Recovery owners should get this as its own finding.
fix: Highest leverage: give ScheduledTasksDB a held per-thread connection, like the ClientNotificationsDB._held_connection template. The store's own docstring flags this as 'its own task': explicit BEGIN plus isolation_level=None, auditing the ~22 transaction() bodies. Alternatively, cache the helper's per-path preparation verdict by (dev, ino, mode) so repeat opens of an already-verified file skip the child process. Report this to the DB-layer slice as well, because any per-operation-connection store pays the same cost.
fix_notes: A held per-thread connection (the ClientNotificationsDB._held_connection template at client_notifications_db.py:163) is the safer lever. It must register with the Backup_Recovery participants (_register_core_connection/_core_access) so that maintenance or restore can close it, and the ~22 transaction() bodies need explicit BEGIN when switching to isolation_level=None, as the store docstring warns. The alternative of caching the helper's verdict by (dev, ino, mode) weakens a deliberate per-open security check (the helper validates without opening inodes locally, to avoid TOCTOU). Treat it as security-sensitive and needing owner sign-off, not a free perf win. Raise this with the DB-layer owner as an app-wide finding, because other per-operation stores pay the same cost.
reason: ScheduledTasksDB._get_connection (scheduled_tasks_db.py:215) calls BaseDB._get_connection (base_db.py:818), which calls connect_private_sqlite and then _connect_registered_sqlite (private_sqlite.py:1709). On every non-Windows file-backed open that calls prepare_in_helper (:1878), and HelperLease.start (private_sqlite_process.py:367) runs `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-I', '-S', private_sqlite_helper_entry.py])` per call. Nothing caches or reuses the helper per path; the only prepare_in_helper call site is :1878. The store deliberately opens a connection per operation (its docstring calls conversion 'its own task'). git log -S shows the helper-per-open arrived 2026-09-07 (61a49de2e0), after all the holistic perf reviews (08-22 to 09-04). TASK-24457 (Library, 8 connections, filed 08-29) predates it and prices only the PRAGMAs, and no backlog task mentions the helper spawn cost. connect_private_sqlite has 94 call sites repo-wide, so every per-operation-connection store pays this.

title: The Research workspace refetches sources twice per visit when a device overlay exists
trigger: on_mount -> _start_catalog_refresh -> _refresh_workspace_catalog -> _apply_catalog_state, once per visit and on each data-source switch, only when overlay_store.load returns a record for the selected workspace
cost: All off the loop. The first worker is cancelled shortly after it starts. Waste is about one duplicate list_recent(limit=20) sqlite read, plus possibly one aborted capabilities call (an HTTP call for server workspaces), plus a redundant 'Loading' status and receipt re-sync. That is a few ms of thread-pool work, not a doubled fetch set.
fix: After the overlay loads, re-render the existing page with the new folders (region.sync_workspace using the cached controller.visible_source_page) instead of refetching. Or load the overlay before the first refresh starts.
fix_notes: The finder's option A (re-render from controller.visible_source_page) usually will not work. When the overlay returns, the first worker is typically still in flight and visible_source_page is None or belongs to the previous workspace. Two safer fixes. (1) Load the overlay before the first _start_sources_refresh. This adds one small local JSON read of serial latency. The quick-notes refresh can still start in parallel. (2) Skip the second restart while a research-workspace-sources worker is still running. _refresh_source_workbench reads self._source_folders only at its final sync_workspace, after every await, so the in-flight worker will pick up the new folders anyway. Re-render with sync_workspace only if that worker already finished. Keep the overlay_generation, capture and is_current_request fences as they are.

self._start_sources_refresh()          # before overlay load
overlay = await asyncio.to_thread(self.overlay_store.load, workspace.ref)
...
self._source_folders = overlay.source_folders
self._start_sources_refresh()          # again: exclusive cancels the worker, not its in-flight to_thread/HTTP
reason: The code matches this pin. In _apply_catalog_state, research_workspace_screen.py:573 calls self._start_sources_refresh() before `await asyncio.to_thread(self.overlay_store.load, workspace.ref)`, and :600 calls it again after the overlay is applied. _start_sources_refresh (:1068) runs _refresh_source_workbench with group='research-workspace-sources', exclusive=True, so the second call cancels the first worker and starts a new one. The trigger is real. _start_catalog_refresh fires from on_mount (:254), and the route is not reusable, so that is once per visit, plus the data-source switch at :342. app.py:12596 always builds a ResearchPresentationOverlayStore in production. load() returns non-None only when this workspace has a saved overlay (pane preferences, folders or annotations), so the double fetch hits users who have customised a workspace. No backlog task covers it; I found no hits for sources refresh or overlay_store.load in backlog/tasks. Everything stays off the loop: _recent_operations uses to_thread, and LocalResearchWorkspaceAdapter offloads every sqlite call with to_thread. The cost claim is overstated. The first worker usually does not finish. Its first await is a 20-row sqlite read in a thread, and the overlay load is a small local JSON read, so the cancel lands early. The realistic waste per visit is one duplicate 20-row receipts read plus at most one partly sent capabilities request, not 3-4 extra HTTP calls. The 'Loading ... sources' status and the receipt sync also run twice. P3 is correct.

(2) The per-key logger.info 'Attempting to save setting' line with redacted values goes away. title: Every Settings category switch re-mints both panes from scratch; heavy categories cost 215-900 ms of loop time, and a mount-echo Changed storm reruns the staging cascade
trigger: Yes. A rail click, j/k+Enter or search Enter goes through _select_category, sets active_category, and runs watch_active_category -> _swap_category_panes -> recompose of both panes on the loop. The worker is a coroutine, not a thread. The 25+ _refresh_settings_workspaces_pane callers use the same path.
cost:
Isolated real TldwCli, run_test at 211x44 on a scratch profile. The guard audit hook saw 0 writes outside scratch. Raw data is in scratch/s53-lens2/{base1,base2,p3a,p3b,leak1}.out. All numbers are main-thread CPU (thread_time) per category switch. Machine load was 20-64 on 18 cores, so absolute values are probably 1.3-2x an idle machine.

Per-switch cost (loop CPU / worst single handle):
- Providers: 430-720 ms / 60-280 ms, with 1.9-4.4K file opens on the event loop.
- Speech: 660-1300 ms / 90-450 ms.
- Image Gen: 400-1030 ms.
- Library/RAG: 390-1060 ms.
- Appearance: 260-640 ms.
- Light categories: 80-230 ms.
- Console Behavior: 1.4-3.8 s, with ONE handle of 0.9-3.4 s. This is worse than the finding says, and the extra cost is not widget minting.

Console Behavior root cause: _render_console_behavior_card calls _current_reasoning_target() during compose (settings_screen.py:18263 -> :6275). That resolves a full Console turn-configuration snapshot (console_chat_controller.py:22494/22513) just to read provider_selection. Timed per switch it costs 1.0-3.0 s CPU and 22.8K-46.5K file opens on the loop. Inside it, capture_mcp_definition_maximum (:1335) alone is 0.86-1.46 s CPU and 19,760 opens (Backup_Recovery storage admission / pinned_directory). Levers (a)-(c) would not remove this. It should be filed separately as P1 loop-blocking.

Claims that are confirmed:
- Stylesheet.apply: Providers 718 calls / 170-230 ms; Speech 1,304 / 350-430 ms; Library/RAG 612-696 / 175-195 ms. That is roughly 35-55% of each switch, net of GC.
- Speech also pays SpeechTTSSettingsPanel._sync_responsive_layout: 3 calls, 200-220 ms per switch.
- Hidden subtrees are minted and styled anyway: Providers 112/252 pane widgets, Image Gen 139/277, Library/RAG 75-108/204.

Mount-echo storm: real but small (3-8% of a switch), so lever (c) has the lowest payoff:
- Library/RAG: 21x _mark_library_rag_settings_staged at 14-22 ms, plus 21x draft-status at 7-9 ms.
- Console Behavior: 27x draft-status at 12-17 ms, plus persist_perm at 27-34 ms (647 opens).
- Providers: persist_catalog at 20-37 ms, plus 3 load_settings calls at 66-103 ms.

The re-mint also inflates the heap behind F2. Detached pane widgets stay alive, +850 per 8-switch round. The top external retainers are the closure from Textual Input's screen-level text_selection_started_signal subscription and Textual LRUCaches.

Severity: the rubric lists settings as a less-frequent path, but 0.4-3.8 s stalls on every heavy switch are well beyond 'moderate', so P1 stands.
fix:
Three levers, in order of payoff:

(a) Cache per-category panes instead of recomposing on every switch. Use a ContentSwitcher (or a dict of SettingsRegion children) keyed by category: mount a category on its first visit, toggle display afterwards, and recompose only when that category's data actually changed (after save/revert, workspace mutations). This is the same pattern as TASK-24452's reuse.

(b) Lazy-compose Collapsible bodies and gated rows on first expand instead of minting hidden subtrees.

(c) Kill the mount-echo storm. Have the _stage_* helpers return whether the draft changed, and early-return from _mark_*_staged / _persist_* when nothing changed and the draft was already clean. Alternatively, mount controls under prevent(Input.Changed, Select.Changed, Checkbox.Changed) and seed state explicitly.
fix_notes:
Lever (a), per-category pane caching with ContentSwitcher, is riskier than stated:
- Collides with shared per-category widget ids. _render_impact_pane_header (:22438) yields id="settings-selected-category-draft-status" for every category, and the state banner (:9717) is also per category. With several cached panes mounted, the many query_one("#...") calls (for example _update_draft_status_widgets at :9056) would hit a hidden category's copy.
- Raises the live widget count, which the finder shows makes per-key cost worse.

Safer order: (c) first, then (b), then (a).

On (c): screen.prevent() around the region recompose will not catch Select echoes, because those are posted from each Select's own _on_mount in its own pump. A value-equality early return in the _stage_*/_mark_* helpers is safer. Some handlers deliberately rely on the constructor echo (the _model_catalog_form_values comment at :15174), so audit that before suppressing.

    for pane_id in ("#settings-detail-pane", "#settings-impact-pane"):
        pane = self.query_one(pane_id, SettingsRegion)
        await pane.recompose()
# handle_library_rag_*_changed -> _stage_library_rag_value -> _mark_library_rag_settings_staged
#   -> validation + preview + classes + soft warning + _update_draft_status_widgets (per mounted Input echo)

The code matches on pin 840ed2ca58. watch_active_category (settings_screen.py:3789) runs run_worker(_swap_category_panes), and inside `async with self.batch()` at :3913 that worker calls `await pane.recompose()` on both SettingsRegions (:2718, whose compose calls back into _render_detail_pane at :21578). Nothing caches or reuses panes. _refresh_settings_workspaces_pane (:21371) forces the same path through mutate_reactive.

The mount-echo storm is real in Textual 8.2.8:

- Select posts Changed from _on_mount through _init_selected_option (_select.py:600-629).
- Checkbox is not affected, because its __init__ wraps the set in prevent().

The Library/RAG handlers (:27931 onward) only check _library_rag_edits_suppressed(), and that is False at compose. So every echo runs _stage_library_rag_value and then _mark_library_rag_settings_staged (:10352: validation, preview, classes, soft warning, draft-status). The Console Behavior permission-summary echo goes _persist_permission_summary_settings -> _saved_permission_summary_payload -> load_settings() (:6418).

I re-read the finder's raw probe output (scratch/s53/out/cat2.json, cat3.json, catgc.json). It came from a real TldwCli under run_test in an env -i scratch profile, and the per-category busy numbers match the finding: Providers 330-617 ms, Speech 570-1083 ms, Library/RAG 324-1346 ms, Console Behavior 484-859 ms.

No open task covers switching categories inside Settings. TASK-2831 is about focus correctness, and TASK-24455/24452 are about screen switches and Console. The cost is a 200-900 ms loop stall per heavy category switch on a less-frequent screen, so P1 fits the rubric.

title: gen2 GC pauses of 120-360 ms land every 1-2 Settings category switches; the app never calls gc.freeze() after boot
trigger: Yes. The allocation churn comes from F1's pane re-mint (100-400 widgets per switch), and a gen2 lands inside whatever loop handle is running at the time. That explains 169-331 ms max handles on light categories such as tool-profiles, watchlists and diagnostics.
cost:
This run used a gc.callbacks probe timed with CPU time (thread_time). The first pass timed with wall clock, and under load 40-60 those numbers were inflated 1-2x. Raw data: scratch/s53-lens2/base2.out and freeze2.out.

Base:
- Each gen2 collection costs 161-451 ms CPU and runs inside a single loop handle.
- 6 gen2 in 22 category switches (about 1 per 3.7 switches, matching the first verifier's correction), plus 3 in 4 Settings visits.
- gen2 total is 2.03 s of 12.86 s loop CPU, about 16%.
- Untruncated grep: 0 gc.freeze/set_threshold/disable calls in tldw_chatbook.

New cause of the round-over-round growth the first verifier flagged: retention.
- The number of stale SettingsScreens equals the number of visits (1->2->3->4) and stays at 4 through the later switches. Each adds about 80K tracked objects (leak1: 674K->754K->834K->914K).
- Every stale screen is still a key in app.theme_changed_signal._subscriptions. SettingsScreen.on_mount subscribes at settings_screen.py:4187-4189 and on_unmount (:4213) never unsubscribes. Textual's Signal is a WeakKeyDictionary whose closure value captures the node, and it only prunes on publish, so screens are held until the next theme change.
- A measurement-only patch that unsubscribes on unmount stops the growth. The remaining retainer is bounded to the latest screen: app._settings_permission_summary_write.screen (:3171-3176, found by a forward path search).
- settings_theme_picker.py:363 has the same subscribe-without-unsubscribe pattern.

Fix check, gc.freeze() after boot (575K objects frozen):
- Early collections drop to 12-67 ms, but frequency doubles: 13 vs 6 per 22 switches, 8 vs 3 per 4 visits.
- Per-collection cost climbs back to 76-279 ms as the unfrozen heap regrows from 355K to 918K objects (first-visit imports plus retention).
- Total gen2 CPU over the 22 switches is unchanged (2.22 vs 2.03 s). Only the maximum improves (279 vs 451 ms).
- So freeze alone is not the fix. It must be paired with the retention fixes and F1's churn reduction, and it still needs the ADR required by TASK-31966 AC#2.

The pauses are real, app-wide (a Home visit also hit a 161 ms gen2) and user-visible, so P1 stands, with known_task TASK-31966. The theme-signal leak (unbounded per Settings visit until a theme change) should be filed as its own memory finding: P1, or P0 by the rubric's letter for long sessions.
fix: Call gc.freeze() once after _ui_ready (and optionally after the screen pre-importer finishes). This moves the boot heap into the permanent generation, so gen2 scans only post-boot objects. Per TASK-31966 AC#2 this global GC policy change needs an ADR. Pair it with F1 so there is less churn to collect. New evidence for TASK-31966: its scope is Console activation, but Settings reproduces the same pauses on every 1-2 category switches.
fix_notes:
gc.freeze() after boot is a global GC policy change, and TASK-31966 AC#2 requires an approved ADR first.

CPython 3.12 caveats:
- After freeze, long_lived_total counts only unfrozen objects, so the 25% full-collection ratio fires more often. The collections are cheaper, but the net effect must be measured.
- Any garbage cycle frozen at boot is never reclaimed.

Pair the change with F1's churn reduction, and check the round-over-round growth before attributing it all to heap size.
evidence:
gc.callbacks probe over 61 transitions (nav + 2x30 category switches):
  gen0 301 ms, gen1 370 ms, gen2 3376 ms (about 17 collections, 120-356 ms each)
  console-behavior r1 gc_ms=[12.8, 15.3, 190.4]; library-rag r1 [34.1, 33.9, 355.7]
  storage r2 [4.8, 9.3, 299.2] -> max handle 305 ms on a 149-widget category
$ grep -rc 'gc.freeze|gc.set_threshold' tldw_chatbook -> 0 files
reason:
`grep -rn -E "gc\.(freeze|set_threshold|disable)" tldw_chatbook` returns 0 hits (untruncated), so the app has no GC policy.

The finder's catgc.json (gc.callbacks probe, real TldwCli run_test, scratch profile) shows 16 gen2 collections across 60 category switches plus 1 at nav:
- Each lasted 96-356 ms: providers 96/239, speech 120/278, library-rag 356/329, storage 299, diagnostics 327, watchlists 193.
- They total about 3.46 s.

Two corrections to the finding:
- Frequency: the cadence is about one gen2 every 3-4 switches overall, not every 1-2. It is nearly every heavy-category switch.
- Heap size: the probe already ran the full TldwCli, so 'the real process holds more objects' holds only for profiles with real user data.

Notably, round-2 pauses are larger than round-1 pauses (for example providers 96 -> 239 ms). The gen2 cost is growing across switches, which is worth a follow-up check for retained widgets.

TASK-31966 (To Do) covers GC pauses but is scoped to Console activation: 79 ms, no remedy approved, ADR required. This finding adds new scope: the pauses are app-wide, reproduce on Settings, and are 1.5-4.5x larger. That makes it confirmed with known_task set, not 'known'. app.py:16355 is the deferred-startup timer block after _ui_ready, which is a sensible place for the fix.

title: The Settings route is not reusable, so every visit constructs and styles a fresh SettingsScreen (356-513 ms loop-busy, 180-195 ms max handle)
trigger: Yes. Every NavigateToScreen('settings') (F4 or the nav bar) goes through the non-reusable branch and constructs and mounts a new SettingsScreen, so repeat visits get no warm benefit.
cost:
Same isolated harness as F1. Raw data: scratch/s53-lens2/base2.out, reuse1.out, p3a.out, p3b.out.

Base (fresh SettingsScreen per visit):
- Warm visits cost 354-599 ms main-thread CPU, with a worst single handle of 120-340 ms.
- The clean visit with no gen2 was 354 ms CPU, 120 ms max handle.
- Each visit makes 558 Stylesheet.apply calls (137-148 ms) and about 900-3,300 file opens on the loop.
- 3 of 4 visits also hit a gen2 of 167-224 ms CPU.

Reuse arm, a measurement-only flip of the 'settings' ScreenRoute to reusable=True:
- Warm visits drop to 93-97 ms CPU, with a max handle of 36-39 ms.
- Applies fall from 558 to 150, and no gen2 fired on warm visits.

- Base keeps every visited SettingsScreen alive through app.theme_changed_signal (on_mount at settings_screen.py:4187-4189, no unsubscribe in on_unmount at :4213). That is 4 stale screens after 4 visits, and 928K tracked objects.

- on_screen_resume already refreshes sync rows, provider defaults, RAG status and workspaces.

The lifecycle audit from the first verifier's fix_notes still applies: timer stop/re-arm, the review/vLLM fences, _settings_mount_visit_refreshed, and the theme subscription. Opt Settings into the TASK-24452 reuse mechanism (ScreenRoute.reusable=True) after a lifecycle audit:
- Move the on_unmount fences (_discard_openai_reconnect_review, _discard_local_model_review, _rollback_vllm_default_intent, audio.cpp cleanup retries, stopping the 0.25 s timer) into on_screen_suspend, with a matching re-arm in on_screen_resume.
- on_screen_resume already performs the per-visit refresh (sync rows, provider defaults, RAG index status, workspaces), which is what reuse requires.

Siblings: TASK-31520 (Console) and TASK-31521 (Library) exist; Settings has no task.

Follow the TASK-31520/31521 audit pattern:
- Move timer stop and the review, credential and vLLM fences into on_screen_suspend, and re-arm in on_screen_resume.
- _settings_mount_visit_refreshed dedupes the mount's own ScreenResume; it must still behave on warm resumes, where no mount happens.
- theme_changed_signal subscribe/unsubscribe is per-mount and needs a check under reuse.
- The retained screen's large widget tree stays in memory across the whole session, a memory/GC trade-off (see F2).

title: Each keystroke in the Model field re-derives the whole model-profile block (65 support checks, about 4.8k provider-key normalizations, Select.set_options, 14 widget rewrites)
trigger: Yes. The trigger is Input.Changed on #settings-model-value, once per typed character, and nothing debounces it.
cost: Measured by the finder (re-read): 28-44 ms loop-busy per key in an unprofiled run, against 14-15 ms baseline, so about 15-27 ms added. The per-call counts come from the finder's cProfile; I did not re-run it.

- Call select.set_options only when the reasoning-effort option list actually differs.
- Optionally debounce the resync by about 150 ms while typing, keeping only the draft staging synchronous.

A cache keyed by (provider, model) must also include the runtime config generation. supported_generation_fields reads app_config, including the ADR-146 custom-endpoint registry, so an endpoint edit must invalidate it.

Gating set_options on a changed option list is safe. When skipping the whole resync on an unchanged signature, the placeholder and disabled state must still update when provider support flips.

title: Per-keystroke status cascades write identical text into Statics with layout=True, forcing about 2 full-screen layout passes per keystroke
trigger: Yes. Every Input.Changed in a staged category goes through _stage_* then _mark_*_staged or _update_draft_status_widgets, then several _set_static_text calls.

- Make _set_static_text a no-op when the text equals the last written value, and pass layout=False for fixed-height single-line status rows. Store the last text on the widget, or compare against widget.content.
- Route _update_draft_status_widgets and _update_guided_action_widgets through the same helper.

Compare against widget.content, which is a public property in Textual 8, rather than a cached last-written string. Other code paths also call .update on the same Statics, so a cached copy could go stale.

Only pass layout=False where the row truly has fixed height. Several status Statics wrap long text, so changed text must keep layout=True.

Routing _update_draft_status_widgets' direct .update through the helper is trivial.

title: Instant-persist inputs rewrite config.toml on every keystroke, plus one load_settings per keystroke on the loop
trigger: Yes, per keystroke in Console Behavior > Permission summary provider/model and in Providers > stale-hours. The mount echoes of these Inputs also run the load_settings compare once per visit.
cost: Partly re-measured. I measured apply_settings_mutation myself: 72.8 ms median in an isolated scratch profile. The finder measured 11 writes for 11 keys and a 139 ms median key wall against 65 ms for a staged field. The wall numbers include pilot quantization.
fix:
- Debounce both writers (about 500 ms after the last keystroke), and flush on blur, Input.Submitted and on_unmount. Keep the existing single-writer drain and generation guard.
- Compare against an in-memory 'last saved payload' (updated when a write succeeds) or the app_config mapping, instead of calling load_settings() on every key.

TASK-15470 moved these writes off the loop but did not debounce them.
fix_notes:
The writers are deliberately app-owned and keep draining after the screen leaves. A debounce timer on the screen is cancelled at unmount, so on_unmount must move any debounced pending payload into the writer queue synchronously (flush), not just stop the timer.

Keep the single-writer drain and the generation/ordering guard from the core-review race fix. Replacing load_settings() with an in-memory last-saved payload is safe only if it is updated when a write succeeds and is invalidated on an external config-generation change (_permission_summary_form_payload already tracks the generation).
reason:
The code matches.

Permission summary:
- @on(Input.Changed) for #settings-permission-summary-provider and -model (:29952 onward) call _persist_permission_summary_settings (:7265).
- On every key, that calls _saved_permission_summary_payload, which calls load_settings() on the loop (:6418).
- If the payload changed, it queues a thread writer that runs apply_settings_mutation_to_cli_config per drained pending.

Stale-hours:
- The stale-hours handler (:29937) calls _persist_model_catalog_settings (:15127).
- That runs load_model_catalog_settings(load_settings()) on the loop (:15205) and starts the @work(thread=True) writer (:15266), which calls save_settings_to_cli_config.

Neither path has a debounce. The writers coalesce only while a write is already in flight, so at normal typing speed (one key per 100+ ms against a write of about 72 ms) every key is a full config.toml rewrite.

TASK-15470 (Done) explicitly gave stale-hours the 'same treatment as the toggle' (thread, no debounce). It called the no-op guard 'cheap, cache-only', but load_settings now costs about 10 ms warm (F7). The core review flagged these writers only for an ordering race.

My isolated bench: apply_settings_mutation_to_cli_config has a 72.8 ms median (range 63-87).

Downgraded to P2. These are rarely-typed Settings fields, and the writes are already off the loop. The on-loop part is one load_settings per key plus GIL contention from the writer's TOML parse/dump.

title: Providers & Models Save persists config synchronously on the event loop (about 108 ms freeze per Save)

- evidence_store.begin_save lease handling
- in-memory app_config mutation
- reload_capabilities
- widget syncs

title: The Workspaces compose runs registry sqlite plus a per-binding stat() on the loop, N+1 per workspace row, and re-runs on every Workspaces interaction
trigger: Yes. The trigger is compose on each Workspaces category visit and on resume-to-Workspaces (_maybe_refresh_workspaces_pane_on_show). It re-runs on every one of the 25 _refresh_settings_workspaces_pane call sites, all loop-side button/checkbox/option handlers or call_from_thread landings. Each re-run repeats the full listing (W+2 registry calls) plus about 6-8 card reads when a workspace is selected.
cost: Measured in an isolated scratch profile (tmp WorkspaceDB, real LocalWorkspaceRegistryService) for get_active_workspace + list_workspaces + per-row list_folder_bindings only, card reads excluded. Medians: 0 workspaces 10.5 ms, 5x3 bindings 52 ms, 20x5 bindings 112 ms (range 81-168). Per call: get_active_workspace 5.3 ms, list_workspaces 5.2 ms, list_folder_bindings 6.4 ms. cProfile puts about 90% in Backup_Recovery storage_admission (acquire_storage, pinned_directory/_open_verified_parent, 17k posix.open per 10 passes). Caveat: admission cost was measured in a scratch profile with no pre-existing bootstrap records, so production may differ somewhat.
fix:
- Fetch the listing, the per-workspace binding counts, the persona page and the permission-store payload in one @work(thread=True) worker (the _tool_profiles_listing pattern). Compose from the cached tuple and re-fetch only after a mutation.
- Replace len(list_folder_bindings(...)) with a count query that does not stat.
fix_notes: The count-without-stat idea is aimed at the wrong cost. The win is ONE aggregated query (SELECT workspace_id, COUNT(*) FROM workspace_runtime_bindings WHERE binding_kind IN (local kinds) GROUP BY workspace_id) instead of N list_folder_bindings calls, because each registry call pays a separate storage admission. Keep the live stat for the selected card's folder rows only. If the fetch moves to @work(thread=True), wrap it in the existing _workspace_worker_connection(self) context manager (settings_screen.py:2754, already used at :20689). Otherwise each worker thread leaks a thread-local WorkspaceDB connection. registry.mutation_generation (TASK-21118) is a ready-made cache key for re-fetch-after-mutation. Risk is medium: the _reveal_workspace_* call_after_refresh helpers assume compose renders synchronously, so a placeholder-then-land compose needs those reveals re-sequenced. Separate cross-cutting lead for the orchestrator: the per-operation Backup_Recovery storage admission (~5-8 ms per WorkspaceDB call) taxes every Workspace_DB read everywhere. TASK-31502 (ChaChaNotes quiescence lock) does not cover it.
reason: The code is as quoted at settings_screen.py:20541-20569 (_render_workspaces_detail). list_workspaces is followed by len(registry.list_folder_bindings(id)) per row, inside compose. _render_workspace_card, _render_workspace_folder_bindings (:20981), _render_workspace_change_review and _render_workspace_default_assistant then add more sync reads: get_workspace x2, list_folder_bindings again, list_ssh_bindings, consent status, list_persona_profiles and permission store list/load. _refresh_settings_workspaces_pane (:21371) is mutate_reactive(active_category), which recomposes the panes. I mapped the 25 call sites to their handlers: row press, show-archived, create, rename, set-active, archive/undo/view, unarchive, folder add/toggle/remove, SSH add/toggle/remove, persona page/select, profile select, exclusions, memory toggle, clear and assistant apply, plus the on-show resume. All run on the loop. The Console switcher N+1 fixed in TASK-32804.6 is a different surface. The core review (qa/core-code-review-2026-09-17/slices/UI-settings.md 'P3 [D2]') recorded this with 'Already covered: none', and no open task exists. The finder's cost attribution is wrong, though: I measured _filesystem_binding_missing at 0.034 ms per binding, so stat() is negligible on local disk. The real cost is that every WorkspaceDB.connection() goes through the Backup_Recovery _core_operation -> storage_admission.acquire_storage path, about 5-8 ms and about 245 posix.open calls per registry call. That makes the N+1 structure much worse than estimated. Severity stays P2 because this is a Settings sub-surface, not a common path, even though a click costs about 100 ms with 20 workspaces.

title: The Speech & TTS panel restyles its whole ~258-widget subtree twice per visit, because on_mount reads size.width == 0
trigger: Yes. A probe mounted the real SpeechTTSSettingsPanel via a host recompose in a minimal App loading the real CSS bundle (isolated env, 235x52). _sync_responsive_layout ran twice: (width 0, class added) then (width 235, class removed). The trigger is every Speech & TTS category entry, and any other pane rebuild that re-yields the panel.
cost: Measured without a profiler: the on_mount add took 113.6 ms and the first-resize remove took 102.6 ms, over a 256-node subtree. About 216 ms of loop time per visit is redundant restyle, out of about 930 ms of wall time for the recompose to settle in the probe. This is consistent with the finder's 150-250 ms estimate.
fix: In _sync_responsive_layout, return early while self.size.width == 0 (let the first Resize decide), or compute the class at compose time from the parent pane width. One line.
fix_notes: The one-line guard `if not self.size.width: return` in _sync_responsive_layout is safe. Textual posts Resize when the size first goes 0 -> real, so on_resize makes the decision after first layout. Wide panes then pay 0 restyles instead of 2; narrow panes (<104) pay 1 restyle at first resize instead of 1 at mount. The number of layout passes is unchanged. At narrow widths the first frame may briefly render unstacked, which is cosmetic. Do NOT swap in set_class(update=False) at mount: descendants' styles would be stale. Check the Settings Speech tests that assert the stacked class right after mount without a pilot.pause.
reason: The code is as quoted: on_mount (:1109) calls _sync_responsive_layout (:1115), on_resize (:1141) calls it again, and _sync_responsive_layout (:1157) calls set_class(size.width < 104, 'settings-speech-stacked'). In Textual 8.2.8, add_class/remove_class -> update_node_styles -> App.update_styles(node), which calls stylesheet.update_nodes(node.walk_children(with_self=True)) SYNCHRONOUSLY (app.py:2504-2523). At full-screen sizes the detail pane is 6fr of (width - ~32 category pane) - 2fr impact pane, about 152 cols at 235 and about 134 at 211, so it is always >=104 and the class always flips add->remove. title: Trajectory search re-renders the whole ledger synchronously on every keystroke, including a full-trace json.dumps/lower() match pass
trigger: Every Input.Changed in #trajectory-search on the TrajectoryScreen, which is pushed from the Console review-selection trace launch (UI/Console_Modules/wiring.py:497-510). Also n/p and error/tool/feedback jumps via _navigate_records, filter-bar changes and turn toggles. Only while the trace screen is open.
cost: Measured. Match pass over 2000 records: ~1.6 ms at 1 KiB and ~13 ms at 8 KiB. Live results are capped at ~2 KB, so ~3 ms is realistic. DataTable clear+re-add of 500 rows: ~5 ms synchronous, plus ~65-75 ms of layout/paint (bare app). Typing into a trace of 500+ records therefore costs ~70-80 ms per keystroke, dominated by the table rebuild, not by json.dumps/lower.
fix: (1) Debounce the search input about 150 ms, using the browser-search cancellation-token pattern the repo already uses. (2) Precompute one lowercased search blob per record once per snapshot (preview + kind + model + provider + name + json args + result), keyed by record key, and match with a single `in`. (3) Compute the match set once per render and reuse it for both _turn_row_specs and update_counts instead of calling _matching_records() again. (4) Above about 1k records, route search renders through the existing _render_worker thread path with render generations.
fix_notes: Debouncing (~150 ms, cancellation-token pattern) is the main lever, because the table rebuild dominates. Passing the already-computed match set into update_counts removes the duplicate full scan (1286). A precomputed lowercased blob helps much less than claimed, since live results are ≤2 KB. If adopted, build it lazily per snapshot keyed by record key and drop it on snapshot swap, or it doubles payload memory for legacy large-payload traces. Routing search renders through _render_worker is viable because the generation guard already exists, but _build_row_specs reads screen state (_collapsed, _query, filter state) from the thread. Snapshot those inputs first. Diffing rows instead of clear+re-add would cut the paint cost further.
evidence:
def on_input_changed(self, event):  # 1607
    self._query = event.value.strip()
    self._render_ledger()            # no debounce
...args_text = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)   # 1200, per record per key
...if result is not None and query in str(result).lower():  # 1206, full untruncated result
...table.clear(columns=False)  # 1250, then add_row x up to 500+
...len(self._matching_records()),  # 1286, re-matches ALL records, not just the window
reason: Code verified at trajectory_screen.py:1607-1612: on_input_changed calls _render_ledger with no debounce. _render_ledger calls _apply_row_specs(_build_row_specs()) synchronously. _build_row_specs matches only the mounted window (_flat_slice, at most PAGE_SIZE=500). _apply_row_specs then calls table.clear (1250), re-adds every row, and at 1286 runs _matching_records() a second time over ALL records just to get a count. _navigate_records (1832) also rescans all records for n/p/error/tool/feedback jumps. Launch path: wiring.py:_present_console_trajectory pushes TrajectoryScreen. It is an occasional diagnostic screen, not a common path, and its cost only grows with large traces, so P2, not P1. The finder's cost basis is inflated for live traces. Console tool results reach the trace through console_chat_store._trajectory_tool_payload -> redact_log_line(raw_result), whose default cap is MAX_REDACTED_LINE_CHARS=2000 (in place since 6c41c7435b, 2026-08-22). Agent-step records omit args and result entirely (trajectory.py:1225-1240). So 8 KiB+ results exist only in legacy pre-cap rows or foreign imported bundles. My micro-benchmark of lower()+`in` over 2000 payloads: 1.6 ms at 1 KiB, 13.1 ms at 8 KiB, 51.8 ms at 32 KiB, so realistic live payloads cost only ~3 ms for the match pass. The dominant real per-keystroke cost is the DataTable rebuild. In a bare Textual 8.2.8 app at 211x44, clear plus 500 add_row took 4-5 ms, and the following layout/paint added ~65-75 ms over an idle-pause baseline (~28 ms extra for 50 rows).

trigger: UI/Console_Modules/video.py:1305-1307 and 1501-1504 push VideoPlayerScreen from a Console video card. For the whole playback, _pump_loop hands every frame to the UI thread at PLAYER_TARGET_FPS=24 (player_pipeline.py:38).

(2) End-to-end: real VideoPlayerScreen + real PlayerPipeline/ffmpeg in a headless bare Textual App (211x44). I timed Screen._on_timer_update (layout+paint) and ran an asyncio loop-lag probe. Frame dropping was disabled, as on an unloaded machine where frames arrive on time.

- Halfcell (the default on iTerm2, Terminal.app, GNOME and Windows Terminal), photo: callback 10.8-15 ms plus paint 11-13 ms p50, loop ~63% busy, p99 90-103 ms. This is heavier than the first pass's '~9%'.
- Ascii: ~3-4.5 ms per frame, ~10% net.

(3) Caveats found while measuring. These are correctness issues, out of scope, but they gate whether the cost is paid.
- On ffmpeg 8.1 (Homebrew), ffplay rejects the input option '-ac 2' (player_pipeline.py:309-310) with 'Option not found' and exits 1. ffmpeg then dies of EPIPE after 9-13 frames, so any source with audio stops after ~0.5 s. My bench shimmed this to '-ch_layout stereo'.
- For silent sources, frames arrived ~265 ms late under load against an 80 ms tolerance. With -re pacing they never catch up, so every frame is dropped.
- The measured cost applies on ffmpeg <=6.x with audio on an unloaded machine, and to everyone once those bugs are fixed.

Verdict: it is a sustained per-tick loop saturation for the whole playback, on an uncommon path, so P1 stands. The fix should add an ffmpeg scale filter AND move frombytes/thumbnail/Pixels.from_image/PNG encoding off the loop. For halfcell, capping the painted cell count also matters.
fix: Add a scale step to the ffmpeg filter chain that targets the render box, e.g. `fps=24,scale=W:H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease` with W/H derived from the cell count x cell pixel size, or 80x80 for halfcell. That cuts pipe bytes and all PIL work by about 100x. Do the frombytes/thumbnail/Pixels.from_image/frame_to_ascii work in the pump thread and bridge only the finished renderable. For kitty, pass a pre-sized image so TGP skips its resize, and consider a lower fps cap or raw (f=24) transmission instead of PNG encoding.
fix_notes: An ffmpeg scale filter (fps=24,scale=W:H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease) is the biggest single win. W/H must come from the cell count x textual_image get_cell_size(), and a terminal resize then needs a pipeline respawn or a conservative fixed box. Moving frombytes/thumbnail/Pixels.from_image/frame_to_ascii into the pump thread is safe, since they are pure. For kitty, the TGP renderable does its scale+PNG+b64 inside __rich_console__ on the loop wherever the Image is constructed. Pre-sizing only removes the resize step, so raw (f=24/32) transmission or pre-encoding is needed to move the rest. Also note that each frame allocates a new TGP terminal image id and cleanup() is never called, so images accumulate terminal-side until the terminal evicts them. Freeing the previous id per frame would fix that.
evidence:

...image = PILImage.frombytes("RGB", (probe.width, probe.height), data)  # 6.2 MB at 1080p
TGPImage(image, width=PIXELS_MAX_COLS, height=PIXELS_MAX_LINES)  # kitty: resize+PNG+b64 at render
scaled = image.copy(); scaled.thumbnail(...); Pixels.from_image(scaled)  # halfcell

reason: Code verified. video_player_screen.py:_pump_loop (thread worker) calls self._bridge(self._render_frame, ...) per frame (292), and _bridge uses app.call_from_thread, which is synchronous. _render_frame (310-352) does PILImage.frombytes on native-resolution rgb24 (327). Kitty mode builds a textual_image TGP Image (332). Its __rich_console__, run at paint on the loop, calls _send_image_to_terminal -> PixelData.scaled(...).to_base64(), i.e. resize, PNG encode and base64, then writes and flushes the whole payload synchronously to sys.__stdout__. PixelData also copies the full frame on construction. Halfcell does copy()+thumbnail()+Pixels.from_image on the loop (339-343). player_pipeline.py:264 is `-vf fps=24` with no scale filter, so ffmpeg pipes native-resolution frames. My benchmark at 1920x1080: frombytes 0.8 ms, copy+thumbnail 1.1 ms, and resize to 800x800+PNG+b64 12.7 ms on a smooth gradient frame. That is consistent with the finder's 24 ms kitty figure on realistic frames. Because call_from_thread blocks the pump, frames are dropped rather than queued, so loop occupancy is render cost x 24 fps: ~30-60% of the loop in kitty mode for the whole playback. It is not on a common path, but it is a per-tick cost sustained for the entire playback, so P1 stands. No backlog task covers it; task-3401.10 is the Done feature task.

title: Watchlists remounts the entire left-rail WatchlistTree (one Button per node or source, no virtualization) on every tree-data load, including counts-only refreshes after each unread item is opened
trigger: Reader (items section, local backend): 0.6 s after each pause in a walk over unread items (only 'new' items trigger it), after star/unread toggles, after bulk status changes and after every tree write verb. It rebuilds even when only counts changed or nothing changed.
cost:
Setup: the real WatchlistsCollectionsScreen, mounted via the repo harness. DestinationHarness brings the real consolidated CSS, and _build_test_app provides a scratch Subscriptions DB. Tests/conftest + Tests/UI/conftest were loaded as plugins with the bootstrap_profile sandbox marker (no real profile touched). Screen size 211x44, section 'items' (local Reader). Seeds were N watchlists x M feeds x 3 'new' items each. I ran 8 cycles of _load_tree_data() with NO data change between cycles, and a compose counter proved a fresh WatchlistTree was mounted every cycle. Script: scratch/lens2-slice54-ui8/test_bench_wl_tree.py.

Results are min/p50 on an M5 Max under load (idle-baseline max stall 3-7 ms per 0.6 s window).
- 4 watchlists x 5 feeds, collapsed (rail 32 widgets, screen 181): drain 49/77 ms (rail remove+mount 38/62, header 10/17, inspector 1). Longest single loop stall 25/36 ms. Then layout+paint 21/28 ms.
- 10x10 collapsed (rail 50 widgets): drain 71/108 ms (rail 57/78, header 11/28). Stall 35/51 ms. Paint 27/40 ms.
- 10x10 with 3 watchlists expanded (rail 80 widgets, plus 3 sync list_source_rows calls on the loop at 4.9-11.7 ms each): drain 165/264 ms, stall 133/169 ms.
- 10x10 with All-sources expanded (rail 150 widgets): drain 141/235 ms, stall 117/173 ms.
- The header's scoped_source_rows took ~0 ms for the default scope, so the 10-28 ms header cost is pure widget rebuild.
- Proxy for the proposed fix (relabel every node Button in place): 0.6-2.8 ms, i.e. ~50-100x cheaper.

Trigger (traced): ItemSelected -> handle_item_selected -> _mark_item_read_on_open (status=='new' only) -> _request_tree_counts_refresh -> set_timer(0.6, _load_tree_data). The snapshot load itself is off-loop (to_thread). Then _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces unconditionally requests RAIL+HEADER+INSPECTOR -> call_next(_drain_surface_refresh) on the message pump -> refresh_region_content(LEFT_RAIL) (remove + mount a fresh WatchlistTree) + refresh_header_content. Nothing compares against the previous TreeDataSnapshot. There are 4 more _request_tree_counts_refresh callers (lines 13975, 14035, 14261, 14310) and ~24 direct _load_tree_data callers.

Verdict: the cost is larger than the first pass's bare-app numbers (35-70 / 100-160 ms). It fires on every reading pause over unread items, the core loop of the Reader, so P1 stands. It is borderline P0 for users who keep watchlists or All-sources expanded: >100 ms single stalls even on an M5 Max, and likely 1.5-3x that on typical laptops.
fix: Compare the new TreeDataSnapshot's structure (watchlist ids/names/tags, source rows, expansion) with the previous one. When only counts changed, push the counts into the mounted tree through an in-place WatchlistTree.update_counts(counts, source_counts) that relabels the existing Buttons, and skip _SURFACE_RAIL/_SURFACE_HEADER. Hoist the per-watchlist source-rows cache onto the screen, keyed by tree-load generation, so a structural rebuild stops re-querying. Separately (outside this slice), WatchlistTree.expanded/expanded_root_kinds are reactive(recompose=True), so one expand recomposes every node. Consider patching the expanded subtree instead, or capping/virtualizing the per-source rows.
fix_notes: A counts-only in-place relabel is right, but it must respect the TASK-2200 serial drain. If a structural rail rebuild is already queued in _pending_surface_refresh, let that rebuild carry the new counts instead of patching a widget that is about to be replaced. The structural-equality check needs to cover watchlist ids/names/tags, all/unassigned source rows, expansion state, the unread pin and the disabled reasons, all of which the rail builder feeds. A screen-level source-rows cache must be invalidated by every write verb (add/remove source, create/delete watchlist). The recompose=True reactives on WatchlistTree (expanded, expanded_root_kinds, active_tag, write_disabled_reason) are a separate follow-up.

  -> set_timer(0.6, self._load_tree_data)  # 12482
_load_tree_data -> _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces():

  -> workbench.refresh_region_content(Region.LEFT_RAIL)  # remove + mount fresh WatchlistTree

reason: Code verified. _mark_item_read_on_open ends with self._request_tree_counts_refresh() (12446), which re-arms set_timer(0.6, self._load_tree_data) (12480-12483). _load_tree_data (1644) reads the snapshot via asyncio.to_thread, then unconditionally calls _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces. title: Trajectory live refresh and sub-5000-record mounts rebuild keys, filters, timeline and the whole ledger synchronously on the UI thread
trigger: TrajectoryScreen open over the Console with a revision_provider (review_selection.py:626 lambda: store.get_payload_revision(conv_id)). Any payload-revision bump (message append/complete/content update, variant ops, trajectory row writes) triggers one on-loop apply per 0.5 s tick. The first mount of any trace up to 5000 records is also synchronous.
cost: I did not re-measure the finder's 20.5 ms apply at 2000 records, but the per-record work (json.dumps+sha256, plus asdict deep copies for legacy rows) makes it plausible. On top of it, the DataTable clear+re-add of up to 500 rows measured ~5 ms synchronous plus ~65-75 ms layout/paint in a bare app. Each revision tick on a 500+ record trace can therefore cost well over 50 ms, up to twice per second.
fix: _live_rebuild_worker is already a thread, so build the row specs (and record keys) there and hand _apply_row_specs(specs, generation) the finished specs, the way _render_worker does. Lower WORKER_THRESHOLD to about 1,000 or always use the worker for mount. Skip set_records/set_snapshot when the snapshot's record count and last event id are unchanged.
fix_notes: _rebuild_record_keys both reads and mutates self._legacy_key_assignments. To move it to the worker, compute from a copied assignment map and commit the result on the loop under the revision guard, or two overlapping workers can diverge. Do not skip set_records/set_snapshot on unchanged count + last event id alone: message edits and variant changes bump the revision without changing either, and would leave stale previews or variants. Key the skip on the revision or on a content hash. Building specs in the worker should reuse _render_worker's generation guard.

title: Workflows raw-JSON keystrokes rebuild the library list and navigator; library search queries per keystroke with no debounce
trigger: Every keystroke in the Workflows Advanced JSON editor, and every keystroke in the workflow library search input.

title: Speech Playground (161 widgets) is re-minted on every Speech visit and every internal view switch
trigger: Every Speech tab visit (route not reusable) and every Playground ↔ Settings/Profiles/Blends rail switch (remove_children + re-mount). Both paths run through async workers on the loop.
cost:
Harness: scratch/l2s55r/bench_f2.py, run in the isolated profile (above) with Textual 8.2.8 headless at 235x52. It uses a real STTSWindow, the real StudioTTSPreferenceStore (loaded via to_thread), the real config read, and FakeTTSService from Tests/UI/speech_playground_fixtures for the catalog. There were 4 runs of K=8 iterations each, the first iteration discarded, at load 42-47. The Playground pane is 159 widgets. Metrics are loop-thread CPU (thread_time) and a 1 ms-sleep loop-lag probe.

(a) Rail switch Settings->Playground, which does remove_children plus a new SpeechPlaygroundPane plus catalog load: CPU min 199-244 ms, median 220-302 ms. The longest single loop stall had min 54-86 ms and median 95-250 ms, with 4-7 stalls over 16 ms per switch.

(b) A Speech visit (new STTSWindow through to a settled Playground): CPU min 200-251 ms, median 241-344 ms. Worst loop stall median 100-320 ms.

(c) The alternative of keeping the pane mounted (display False->True plus repaint): CPU 10.5-13 ms, lag_max 6-28 ms, about 17-20x cheaper.

Stubbing F1's config read cut about 30-45 ms (noisy), so the pane re-mint itself is about 200 ms under load. That is consistent with the first verifier's 188 ms median. An idle machine is plausibly about 2x faster, which is still far above P1's 10-20 ms per-visit bar. It is not P0, because Speech is a secondary tab and the best-case largest single stall is under 100 ms.

Exhaustive trace. The stts ScreenRoute (screen_registry.py:179) lacks reusable=True. app.py:12264 _create_navigation_screen returns screen_class(self) on every visit. LabScreen.on_mount (lab_frame.py:307) runs call_after_refresh(_mount_lab_body), then STTSScreen.build_lab_body (stts_screen.py:290), which builds a new STTSWindow. STTSWindow.on_mount runs run_worker(_load_studio_preferences) as a coroutine, not a thread, and that calls _mount_view(force=True). _mount_view has 4 call sites (STTS_Window.py:1775, 1800 watch_current_view->run_worker, 1853, 1902), and all run on the loop. _mount_view_unlocked runs remove_children at :1989 and mounts a new pane at :1997. Only _playground_axis_values carries over between mounts; nothing caches the pane. Each remount re-arms set_interval and _load_provider_catalog in SpeechPlaygroundPane.on_mount (:2644).

No open task covers Speech: TASK-24452/31520/31521 cover only Console, Library and Home. Fix risk is medium, per the first verifier: the playback mixin's on_unmount teardown and the 5 s audio.cpp poll would need a hide/suspend hook.
fix: Keep the Playground pane mounted across Speech view switches: mount each view once and toggle it with ContentSwitcher or display, or cache the pane instance and re-attach it. Then audit on_mount and on_unmount and opt the stts route into ScreenRoute(reusable=True), following the TASK-24452 precedent for Console. Move per-visit refresh work, such as the catalog staleness check, to on_screen_resume.

The playback mixin's on_unmount (speech_playback_mixin.py:1279) stops audio, cancels the catalog, voice and playback workers, and retires the progress timer. That no longer runs on a view switch, so playback would keep going behind the Settings view unless those steps move to a hide/suspend hook. The 5 s audio.cpp poll (F5) would also keep firing while hidden unless it is paused. Making the route reusable=True needs the same on_unmount/on_screen_resume audit that TASK-31520/31521 did, covering all STTSWindow sub-windows (dictation, audiobook, voice cloning), and the catalog staleness check must move to on_screen_resume.

title: _apply_catalog rescans voice-profile stores synchronously on the loop, 2+ times per catalog load and on select changes
trigger: Each catalog load (Playground mount, provider switch, Refresh) makes at least 2 _apply_catalog calls. Each model change makes 1 call plus a voice-worker re-apply. Voice/format changes that end a preset reproject. All of these run on the event loop in async workers or message handlers.
cost: Measured in an isolated profile: _chatterbox_profile_choices warm 9.6–14 ms per call, first call about 39–43 ms; _omnivoice_profile_choices about 0.2 ms warm; _kokoro_blend_choices about 0.01 ms. Memoize the result on the pane so _apply_catalog and reprojection only read the cache. Invalidate it on Refresh, on VoiceBlends add/import, and on Voice Cloning profile save.

Compute choices in the catalog worker with asyncio.to_thread and key them on (provider_id, catalog.revision), because _apply_catalog is sync and has many callers. Invalidate on Refresh, and on profile writes from the Voice Cloning window and VoiceBlends, which live in other widgets. Today the pane is re-minted per visit, so staleness is bounded to one visit. If F2 makes the pane persistent, also invalidate on resume. Don't bother moving kokoro/omnivoice, which cost almost nothing.

cost: Not measured. The finder's estimate of a few ms plus one layout pass per 5 s tick is plausible from the code: about 20 widget writes and forced layouts.

The early return must still apply when current is None: visibility and model changes reset it to None to force a repaint. It must also not skip the clone-setup sync when the model select changed, although the model-change path already nulls the observation. Comparing the card projection is the more robust gate if diagnostics churn.

cost: Not measured. Sub-ms per keystroke is plausible, apart from the text materialization for very long pasted text, which grows linearly.

For the _mirror_axis_edit equality skip, confirm that _apply_controls and _prime_profile_preset_controls already call _refresh_axis_markers after writing axis_values, as the docstring implies. Otherwise the skip would leave the chips stale after a catalog-driven write.

title: Fixed asyncio.sleep 'barriers' add 200 ms to every Play and 100 ms to every Pause/Resume
trigger: Every Play (button, keyboard action, auto-play after generation) and every Pause/Resume press in the Speech Playground.
cost: By inspection (fixed constants): +200 ms before audio starts on each Play, and +100 ms before each Pause/Resume takes effect. There are also 2 debug-only get_state() executor round trips per Play on a single-thread executor.
fix: Delete the fixed sleeps and the debug-only get_state() calls, and keep the awaited stop()/_retire_progress_timer() as the barrier. Make the debug logs lazy with logger.opt(lazy=True), or drop the .exists() call from the f-string. Verify on the macOS and Linux player backends that play() right after an awaited stop() is race-free.
fix_notes: Removing the 0.2 s sleep looks safe given stop()'s process.wait and the identity-guarded monitor. Verify with the mpv/ffplay/afplay backends that the audio device is released on exit, which matters for device-exclusive backends on Linux. Removing the post-play 0.1 s sleep narrows the window in which a Pause's exclusive worker cancels the Play worker, a correctness side-benefit. The :1309 unmount sleep should become an awaited cancel, not a sleep; tier-2 S21 made the same point.
evidence:
await self._retire_progress_timer()
# Small delay to ensure clean state
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
state_after_stop = await self.app.audio_player.get_state()   # debug-only executor hop
...
# _pause_audio_async: Small delay to ensure UI is ready
await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
reason: The code matches. _play_audio_async runs `await asyncio.sleep(0.2)` (speech_playback_mixin.py:718) after an awaited audio_player.stop() and _retire_progress_timer(), before play(). That is 200 ms of pure added latency on every Play, whether from the button, action_play_audio or auto-play (callers at :208, :295, :1150). _pause_audio_async sleeps 0.1 s before acting (:786). There is a further post-play sleep(0.1) at :770, which does not delay audio but holds the exclusive 'stts-playback' worker, and on_unmount sleeps 0.05 s (:1309). I checked whether the barrier is really needed. AsyncAudioPlayer.stop runs in the executor and does process.kill()/terminate() plus process.wait(timeout) (audio_player.py:561-596), so the old process has exited when stop() returns. _monitor_playback only writes state when `self._current.process is process` (identity-guarded), so a late monitor thread cannot clobber the new playback. The sleep is redundant. These are asyncio sleeps, not loop blocks, so the cost is action latency, not a freeze.

title: 10 Hz playback progress loop does 3 thread hops and a layout-forcing label update per tick
trigger: Runs for the full duration of every Playground playback at 10 Hz.
cost: Not measured. Estimated at 30 executor round trips per second plus one small layout pass per tick while audio plays. Bounded to playback, so P3.
fix: Fetch the duration once when playback starts, and read state and position in a single executor call. Update the time label only when its text changes, with update(..., layout=False). Cache widget references. Consider a 4–5 Hz cadence.
fix_notes: Safe. Fetch the duration once, write the label only when its text changes, and optionally batch state+position into one executor call. Use layout=False only if the label's width is fixed by CSS; otherwise just skipping unchanged text is enough.
evidence:

    state = await self.app.audio_player.get_state()
    position = await self.app.audio_player.get_position()
    duration = await self.app.audio_player.get_duration()
    progress_bar = self.query_one("#audio-progress-bar", ProgressBar)
    time_display.update(f"{current_time} / {total_time}")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # Update every 100ms
reason: The code matches. _update_progress_timer (speech_playback_mixin.py:1184-1248) loops every 0.1 s during playback. Each tick makes 3 awaited run_in_executor calls on the player's single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor (get_state, get_position, get_duration; audio_player.py:798-815), 3–4 query_one calls, ProgressBar.update, and time_display.update(), where #audio-time-display is a Static (speech_playground_pane.py:2944), so the update means refresh(layout=True). It also makes 3 remove_class('hidden') calls, which are no-ops after the first tick. The m:ss label changes once a second, so 9 of 10 layout refreshes are wasted, and the duration is constant. The tier-2 review (qa/tier2-code-review-2026-09-21/slices/S21-ui-modules-a.md, '30 DOM queries/second') flagged this loop. Its cancellation-race half was fixed (_retire_progress_timer is now awaited), but the per-tick cost remains, and there is no open backlog task.

title: Small sync file I/O on the loop in Voice Blends and audio export handlers
trigger: Opening the Voice Blends view (STTS_Window view switch to 'blends' mounts VoiceBlendsPane, then on_mount). Clicking Add, Import or Export Voice Blends, handled by the mixin's on_button_pressed through the MRO. Clicking Export in the Playground, which calls _export_audio and then the FileSave callback. All are one-shot user actions, not per-keystroke or per-tick.
cost:
Estimated.
- Blend JSON is typically a few KB: sub-ms read and parse, plus an fsync on write of about 1-5 ms on macOS APFS.
- The import file is not size-capped, but realistic blend files are tiny.
- The WAV copy at Kokoro's 24 kHz 16-bit mono is about 2.9 MB per minute, so a 10-minute render is about 29 MB. That is roughly 10-30 ms for shutil.copy2 (fcopyfile) on SSD, once per export click.
- Nowhere near the 100 ms common-path P0 bar, and not a hot path.
fix: Run the blend read/merge/write and the export copy through asyncio.to_thread inside a worker. Build the blend list with ''.join(...). Cap the import file size.
fix_notes:
The export copy cannot simply move to a thread. handle_export calls release_artifact() in its `finally` (speech_playback_mixin.py:982-986), and that lease must be released only after the threaded copy finishes, so move the release into the worker's finally or the source artifact can be released mid-copy.

On threading generally:
- _handle_import_file and _handle_export_file are sync push_screen callbacks. Offloading them needs run_worker(thread=True) or @work(thread=True), with notify and _load_kokoro_voice_blends (which calls query_one) marshalled back via call_from_thread. Alternatively, make them async callbacks that await asyncio.to_thread for the I/O only.
- _show_add_voice_blend_dialog is already an async worker, so wrapping the read/merge/write in asyncio.to_thread is enough there.
- Keep the read-merge-write as one threaded unit so two quick imports cannot interleave.

The ''.join and size-cap items are optional hygiene and not worth doing on their own.
evidence:

    self._load_kokoro_voice_blends()      # open + json.load + str += per blend
...
with open(import_path, "r") as f:
    imported_blends = json.load(f)        # user-picked file, unbounded
...
shutil.copy2(source_path, dest_path)     # FileSave callback, on the loop

All six cited sites exist as quoted on 840ed2ca58 and each is reached from the event loop.
- speech_settings_pane.py:265-266: VoiceBlendsPane.on_mount calls _load_kokoro_voice_blends. That does an exists() check, open and json.load of kokoro_ui_blend_file(), builds a string with += and runs query_one (mixin :844-876). The pane is mounted only when you switch the Speech view to 'blends' (STTS_Window.py:2049-2052, `await content_container.mount(VoiceBlendsPane(...))`).
- The mixin's on_button_pressed (:398-431) routes add-voice-blend-btn, import-blends-btn and export-blends-btn. Those buttons are composed live by VoiceBlendsPane through VOICE_BLEND_ACTIONS (pane :107-123, :254).
- _export_voice_blends (:909) reads the blend file synchronously inside the button handler.
- _handle_import_file (:1166) and _handle_export_file (:1128) are sync push_screen callbacks, so they run on the loop. Import reads a user-picked file of any size, reads the blend file, then calls write_kokoro_ui_blends, which goes through atomic_private_write_text with os.fsync (private_paths.py:1401).
- _show_add_voice_blend_dialog (:1213-1237) is run_worker on a coroutine, which is not a thread, so its open/json.load/write+fsync also block the loop.
- speech_playback_mixin.py:1033: shutil.copy2 runs inside the FileSave callback handle_export (:982-986), reached from audio-export-btn (:305-306). It runs on the loop.

None of these are offloaded. No open task covers them: backlog greps for voice blend and Speech export turned up only Done tasks (1986, 15772). All are rare, user-initiated, non-hot paths, so P3 is right.

title: About 1.8k lines of dead legacy settings-form code are still shipped and mixed into live panes
trigger: speech_settings_contracts is on the boot import path: app.py:412 imports stts_events, which imports speech_settings_contracts at :82. speech_settings_mixin is imported with STTS_Window, which pulls in speech_settings_pane and then the mixin. The mixin's on_button_pressed runs through Textual's MRO dispatch on every Button.Pressed inside either pane. None of these is a hot path, and the dead methods themselves never execute.
cost:
Measured with an isolated `-X importtime` run: HOME, XDG_* and TLDW_CONFIG_PATH were pointed at scratch, with TLDW_TEST_MODE=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
- speech_settings_mixin self-import is about 0.29-0.34 ms, once per process.
- speech_settings_contracts self-import is about 2.2-2.6 ms at boot. Rebuilding the whole 84-record SPEECH_TTS_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY takes about 30 µs, and _build_ownership_index about 4.5 µs. So the ~2 ms is the live module's own class and dataclass definitions, and pruning the dead records would recover only tens of µs.
- speech_settings_group costs 0 at runtime.

The real cost is maintenance surface area, not speed. That makes it a P3 hygiene item.
fix: Delete speech_settings_group.py and its tests, and delete the unreachable legacy methods in SpeechSettingsMixin. Keep only the blend add/import/export and its _cli_setting/_tts_service_factory hooks, and move those into VoiceBlendsPane. Delete the overridden SpeechCatalogMixin._show_provider_specific_controls/_check_higgs_installation. Prune the dead control records from the ownership inventory.
fix_notes:
Before deleting the legacy SpeechSettingsMixin methods:
- Keep normalize_provider_voice_selection (mixin :70), which STTS_Window.py:1340 uses.
- Keep on_button_pressed's three blend branches plus the blend helpers, or move them into VoiceBlendsPane. SpeechSettingsPane.on_button_pressed deliberately defers blend ids to the inherited handler (:1545-1547), so that coupling breaks if the mixin handler is removed without moving the branches.
- Delete or port the tests that host the mixin and exercise _update_default_voice_options: Tests/UI/test_speech_kokoro_defaults.py:129, Tests/UI/test_stts_profile_library.py:1248 and Tests/TTS/test_local_provider_contracts.py:229. Also delete the two SpeechSettingsGroup tests.

Pruning the ownership inventory is a boot-path hazard. _build_ownership_index (contracts :573-601) raises ValueError at import if a record is missing from, or not listed in, speech_settings_model.ALL_SETTINGS_CONTROLS. That exception fires while app.py is importing stts_events, so it would crash boot. The inventory and ALL_SETTINGS_CONTROLS must be pruned in lockstep and checked with Tests/UI/test_speech_settings_contracts.py.

There is no measurable speed gain. Frame it as surface-area reduction, not a perf fix.
evidence:

# SpeechSettingsMixin: legacy_on_mount, _set_initial_values, handle_default_selects_changed,
#   _update_default_*_options, _save_settings, _discover_audio_cpp, browse handlers
# their ids (save-settings-btn, default-provider-select, kokoro-browse-model-btn,

Neither host nor any other prod file references legacy_on_mount, handle_default_selects_changed, _load_audio_cpp_config, _discover_audio_cpp, _save_settings, _set_initial_values, _update_default_* or any _browse_* method, apart from comments and Dictation's unrelated _save_settings.

The finding's runtime claims are overstated:

title: Left-rail WatchlistTree is fully rebuilt (plus sync source-row queries in compose) on every count refresh, including the debounced refresh after each article read
trigger: Yes. Opening any status=='new' item on the Read tab (j/k/click/space) leads to one rail+header rebuild 0.6 s after each reading pause. The same unconditional rail/header request fires after every tree-data load: visit, writes, scope reconciliation. Each expand, collapse or tag click also recomposes the whole tree through recompose=True reactives.
cost:
Setup: drove the real WatchlistsCollectionsScreen through the Tests harness (DestinationHarness + _build_test_app, conftest loaded via -p Tests.conftest, bootstrap_profile sandbox; TMPDIR, HOME and XDG in the scratch dir; the real profile's mtimes were unchanged afterwards). Terminal was 211x44, Read section, seeded scratch subscriptions DB with 5 sources per watchlist and 6 'new' items per source. I wrapped _drain_surface_refresh, workbench.refresh_region_content/refresh_header_content and _load_source_rows_for_tree, then opened 12 unread items with select_item_by_id and waited out the 0.6 s debounce after each. Bench script: scratch/lens2-slice56/test_bench_wl.py. The host was heavily loaded (load avg 25-60 on 18 cores), so the primary metric is loop-thread CPU (time.thread_time).

Results: 12 opens produced 12 drains, i.e. one full rail+header rebuild per unread article read.
- 10 watchlists, collapsed (54 tree widgets): drain CPU median 63.7-70.8 ms (rail 52-57, header 11-12); wall 69-76 ms in the less-loaded run.
- 30 watchlists, collapsed (114 widgets): drain CPU 141-146 ms (rail 127-131); wall 161-177 ms.
- 10 watchlists with 3 watchlists + All expanded (119 widgets): drain CPU 200 ms. The longest uninterrupted loop CPU chunk inside the drain was 150 ms. 36 sync list_source_rows calls over 12 drains, i.e. 3 per rebuild at 12-15 ms CPU each (list_source_rows takes a _db.transaction() for a read).
- 30 watchlists expanded (279 widgets): drain CPU 350-363 ms, longest single chunk 277 ms.

The drain is effectively the visible freeze. It runs as a call_next callback on the screen's own message pump (screen:5025), and Textual posts every widget repaint as messages.Update/Layout to that screen (textual/widget.py:4567/4577). So nothing on the screen repaints until the drain returns.

Trace: handle_item_selected (screen:12241, the only caller) -> _mark_item_read_on_open (:12381, fires only for status 'new') -> _request_tree_counts_refresh (:12446) -> set_timer(0.6) -> _load_tree_data (:1644; the snapshot read is off-loop via to_thread) -> _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces -> unconditional _request_surface_refresh(RAIL, HEADER, INSPECTOR) (:1809) -> drain -> refresh_region_content (watchlists_workbench.py:574-596). That last call removes and mounts fresh factory output with no diff or equality check. The fresh WatchlistTree has an empty _source_cache, so compose re-runs the sync loader for every expanded watchlist.

Verdict: at a default-size tree it costs ~64-71 ms per article read, so P1 stands. It crosses P0-level stalls (>100 ms, single chunks of 150-277 ms) at about 30 watchlists or with expanded roots. I kept P1 because that needs larger or expanded trees; note it as borderline P0.
fix: 1) Add WatchlistTree.apply_counts(counts, source_counts, unread_pin) that rewrites the affected Buttons' label/tooltip in place (ids are already deterministic: wl-tree-node-<kind>, wl-tree-node-watchlist-<id>, wl-tree-node-source-<occurrence>), and have _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces call it when the structural part of the snapshot (watchlists, all/unassigned source rows, tags) is unchanged -- only request _SURFACE_RAIL/_SURFACE_HEADER when structure changed. 2) Make expanded/expanded_root_kinds/active_tag non-recompose and mount/remove only the affected child rows after the toggled Horizontal. 3) Load expanded watchlists' source rows in the off-thread _read_tree_data_snapshot (it already calls service.list_sources for reconciliation) and pass them in, deleting the synchronous source_rows_loader from compose.
fix_notes: The in-place count path must treat one more case as STRUCTURAL: when the 'unread' aggregate root is expanded, its child rows are filtered by _source_counts[...]['unread'] > 0 (watchlist_tree.py compose, 'All Unread' node). Marking an item read can therefore remove a source row, which is more than a relabel. The signature must include the set of unread-positive source ids whenever 'unread' is in expanded_root_kinds, plus _unread_pin_source_id. Source badges switch between present and absent at 0, but that is still only a label change. _SURFACE_HEADER should likewise be requested only when the scoped summary inputs changed. Moving list_source_rows into _read_tree_data_snapshot needs list_source_rows (row dicts), not list_sources (ids only). Making expanded/active_tag non-recompose must preserve the TreeExpansionChanged/TreeTagFilterChanged watcher posts and the set_reactive seeding contract. Medium risk is fair.
evidence:
