title: Config encryption runs scrypt (N=16384) once per encrypted value on every config reload and every settings write
trigger: For opt-in encrypted-config users: every save_setting_to_cli_config/apply_settings_mutation write (119 UI call sites) and every cache-miss reload, all under _config_file_lock.
cost: Measured about 23 ms per encrypted value, so about 180 ms per write or reload with 8 stored keys (estimated), holding the config file lock and serialising other config readers and writers.
fix: Keep a per-session memo {ciphertext: plaintext}. Each ciphertext is unique because of its random salt and nonce, and the plaintext already lives in _CONFIG_CACHE, so the memo adds no new exposure. Clear it in clear_encryption_password and set_encryption_password. Alternatively cache derived keys per (password, salt). Either way, reloads and writes stop paying for scrypt except for newly written values.
fix_notes: Key the memo on (password, ciphertext), or at minimum clear it in set_encryption_password and clear_encryption_password. A ciphertext-only memo would return plaintext for a wrong password and bypass the decrypt_and_verify check that currently detects a bad password. Caching derived keys per (password, salt) is equivalent in effect, because each value has a unique salt.
reason: config_encryption.py:52 sets SCRYPT_N = 16384 with r=8. _derive_key (:151) runs scrypt inside every decrypt_value. _decrypt_config (:232-234) decrypts every encrypted value on each call. config.py:6939 (the post-write install in _publish_runtime_config path) and :7052 (_atomic_config_values_from_raw) both run _decrypt_config_section_with_status(strict=True) after writes, and cache-miss reloads do the same. I measured decrypt_value at 24.0 and 22.9 ms in isolation. Only is_sensitive_config_key values are encrypted, so the cost is about 23 ms × the number of stored secrets per reload or write. This only applies when [encryption] enabled=true and a password is set (_decrypt_config_section_with_status returns early otherwise). No open task mentions scrypt, decrypt_value or _derive_key.

title: The first tiktoken use per encoding (60–89 ms: import, bundle sha256 check, BPE build) runs on whichever thread asks first, including event-loop actions
corrected: also tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_chat_controller.py:21702 and :21928 (sync bound_messages_to_window inside async defs)
trigger: The first token count per encoding in a session, when it lands on a loop caller: inspector snapshot, Send-hover price tooltip, or the async controller preview builders.
cost: Measured a one-time 80 ms (cl100k) and 133 ms (o200k) per process; warm calls take 0.025 ms.
fix: Warm the default model's encoding in a deferred, staggered boot worker (thread) when TIKTOKEN_AVAILABLE is true: call get_tiktoken_encoding(default_model) after first paint. Alternatively route first-use estimation from UI actions through asyncio.to_thread with the chars estimate as a placeholder.
fix_notes: A deferred thread warm-up after first paint that calls get_tiktoken_encoding for the configured default model (and cl100k as the fallback) is low risk. Make sure install_tiktoken_runtime has run first, so the warm-up uses the bundled offline assets rather than a network fetch. Stagger it off the boot-critical window to avoid adding to the first-paint GIL contention.
evidence:
def get_tiktoken_encoding(model):
    import tiktoken  # deferred: see TIKTOKEN_AVAILABLE above
    ...return tiktoken.get_encoding(encoding_name)
tiktoken_runtime.py:141  if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != expected_hash:
chat_screen.py:6376  token_estimate = _estimate_factory()   # sync, inside an action (Ctrl+Shift+P)
reason: tiktoken==0.14.0 is a core dependency (pyproject.toml:77), so TIKTOKEN_AVAILABLE is true on every install. get_tiktoken_encoding (token_counter.py:384) imports tiktoken lazily, and tiktoken_runtime.py:141 sha256-verifies the bundled BPE blob on first load. Only tiktoken's internal per-encoding cache helps after that, and there is no warm-up anywhere (I grepped app.py, app_entry.py and chat_screen.py). I measured the first cl100k estimate at 80.3 ms, the first o200k at 132.9 ms, and warm calls at 0.025 ms. Event-loop callers exist. chat_screen.py:6376 calls _estimate_factory(), then estimate_tokens synchronously, in the inspector snapshot builder. The async defs _build_personal_context_snapshot and _build_project_instruction_preview_for_session (console_chat_controller.py:21702, :21928) call bound_messages_to_window, which counts tokens, synchronously on the loop. The Send-hover tooltip derivation also counts tokens. Whether the loop or a worker thread pays first depends on the session, but a loop caller paying first is plausible. No open task covers it.

title: A process-wide fd-protection lock is held across whole Chatterbox TTS generations, serialising unrelated STT and embedding model loads
corrected: tldw_chatbook/TTS/backends/chatterbox.py:870 (default isolated path that bypasses the lock); :903 and :467 are fallback-only
trigger: Only when Chatterbox has fallen back to in-process mode and an STT worker spawn, embedding load or transcription load starts during a generate() call. The default isolated-subprocess path does not hold the lock.
cost: Estimated. A coincident one-time model or worker start waits for the current generate() chunk, which can be seconds. Parakeet speculative start fails with fd_protection_busy after 0.5 s instead of waiting.
fix: Wrap only the from_pretrained and subprocess-spawn moment in chatterbox.py (move generate() outside the context manager). Consider a per-feature lock or making callers opt into a bounded timeout. File the follow-up the comment promises.
fix_notes: Before moving generate() out of protect_file_descriptors, confirm that chatterbox generate() never spawns subprocesses or triggers HF downloads (for example the watermarker or lazy weights on first call). Otherwise the macOS 'bad value(s) in fds_to_keep' crash comes back. Filing the follow-up the comment promises is the proportionate action.
reason: The code matches. fd_protection.py:59 defines a process-wide threading.Lock, and :112 acquires it with timeout=-1 by default. chatterbox.py:903 holds it across self.model.generate(). However, the finder missed that this is the fallback path. ChatterboxTTSBackend.initialize() starts _initialize_isolated_process, and the wrapper tldw_chatbook/TTS/backends/chatterbox_process.py exists, so by default generation goes through _generate_single_isolated (:870-872) in a subprocess and never takes the fd lock. In-process generation (and the :467 from_pretrained) only runs when isolated initialisation failed or the child died. The other lock holders are all one-time model or worker starts: STT/executor.py:754/771 (worker spawn), Embeddings_Lib.py:356, transcription_service loads, and parakeet_voice_worker.py:601 (timeout=0.5, which fails fast rather than waiting). Contention needs an optional backend already in fallback mode plus a coincident first model load. The module comment documents this as an accepted cost; the follow-up was never filed (tasks 640/641 are Done).

title: The UI responsiveness monitor keeps two daemon threads polling at 10 Hz forever (20 idle wakeups per second)
trigger: Always on by default: the watchdog from arm() at boot, and the drain thread from the first diagnostic record. Both run until close().
cost: Tiny CPU (the finder measured 0.033% of a core; I did not re-run it), but about 20 timer wakeups per second while idle, which affects battery and timer coalescing.
fix: Drain thread: use a blocking get() and put a sentinel on close(). Watchdog: sleep until last_heartbeat + limit (a computed deadline) instead of 100 ms ticks, which gives about 1 wakeup per heartbeat.
fix_notes: For the drain thread, use a blocking get() and have close() put a sentinel. The existing _diagnostic_closed check alone would then never be reached. For the watchdog, sleep until last_heartbeat + limit, re-read the heartbeat after waking, and loop. Keep a bounded maximum sleep so a stall that starts right after a heartbeat is still sampled within about one limit.
evidence:
component, event, record = self._stall_queue.get(timeout=0.1)   # drain loop, forever
...
poll = min(0.1, self.stall_threshold_ms / 2000)
while not self._diagnostic_closed:
    time.sleep(poll)
reason: ui_responsiveness.py:125 _drain_stalls loops forever on _stall_queue.get(timeout=0.1). It starts on the first record_diagnostic (:114-119) and exits only when _diagnostic_closed is set. ui_responsiveness.py:310 _watch_loop sleeps min(0.1, threshold/2000) per tick for the life of the process. arm() starts it (:296-305) when enabled, and enabled defaults to True (app.py:7963 and :11930, get_cli_setting('diagnostics','ui_responsiveness_enabled', True)). That gives about 20 idle wakeups per second across the two threads. No open task covers it (the tasks mentioning ui_responsiveness are Ruff/encoding hygiene and TASK-26834).

title: The token counter loads the native tokenizers library at import (and reads package metadata for tiktoken) on the boot path, even though most sessions never use a custom tokenizer
trigger: Every boot: tldw_chatbook.app -> Chat.console_display_state -> Utils.token_counter -> Utils.custom_tokenizers -> tokenizers (confirmed from importtime nesting). The tokenizers library is only used when the user has installed custom tokenizer mappings.
cost: Boot importtime: tokenizers cumulative 3.7 to 11.9 ms, and token_counter self time 2.8 to 3.0 ms (which includes the metadata scan). My probe: first metadata.version('tiktoken') call 1.48 ms max (0.2 ms median once warm), find_spec('tokenizers') 0.03 ms. The realistic saving is about 4 to 12 ms per boot, almost all from `tokenizers`.
fix: Set TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE from importlib.util.find_spec('tokenizers') (0.06 ms) and import Tokenizer inside load_tokenizer/install_tokenizer. Use find_spec('tiktoken') instead of metadata.version. Cache the directory listing in CustomTokenizerManager.
fix_notes: Do NOT replace version('tiktoken') with importlib.util.find_spec('tiktoken'). tldw_chatbook/__init__.py:25 installs Utils/tiktoken_runtime.py's _TiktokenRuntimeArmingFinder at sys.meta_path[0]. Its find_spec('tiktoken') removes the finder from meta_path (:226) and restores it only on failure or a None spec. A find_spec probe would therefore consume the one-shot finder: the later real `import tiktoken` would skip install_tiktoken_runtime(), which breaks the offline bundled-encodings guarantee. That is exactly what the TASK-24305 comment at token_counter.py:34-41 warns about. Leave the ~1.5 ms version() call alone. The `tokenizers` half is safe: set TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE from find_spec('tokenizers') and import Tokenizer locally in load_tokenizer (~:136/:160) and install_tokenizer (~:411). Wrap that local import in try/except ImportError, because find_spec cannot prove the native extension loads. Skip the listdir cache (memoised, and only relevant for opt-in users).
evidence:
try:
    from tokenizers import Tokenizer      # module scope, boot path via token_counter
    TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE = True
token_counter.py:47  version("tiktoken")   # importlib.metadata scan at import
custom_tokenizers.py:204/214  for tokenizer_name in os.listdir(self.tokenizers_dir):   # per estimate miss when mappings exist
reason: Code is as quoted on 840ed2ca58: custom_tokenizers.py:26 imports `tokenizers` at module scope, token_counter.py:47 calls `version("tiktoken")`, and the listdir loops are at :204 and :214. The boot importtime captures (scratch/boot-import/importtime_1/2.txt) show `tokenizers` imported first and only under custom_tokenizers (cumulative 3.7 ms and 11.9 ms in two runs), under token_counter, under Chat.console_display_state. Both modules are in Tests/Performance/boot_budget_snapshots/boot_import_modules.txt. No open task covers this. TASK-24305 is Done and deliberately swapped `import tiktoken` for `version()`. The listdir part is negligible and should be dropped. It only runs when custom_tokenizers_available() is true (the user installed mappings.json), and estimate_tokens memoises every result in _ESTIMATE_CACHE keyed on (model, provider, len, hash), so it runs once per new text, not per estimate.

title: The shared HTTP client factories rebuild a TLS context and re-read the certificate bundle for every new client (9 ms each), and a custom CA also rebuilds or re-hashes it on every call
trigger: Each new httpx client that uses the default verify=True. The on-loop sites are user-initiated and once-per-action (setup-card discovery, the settings-modal model probe). The per-request image-gen clients and per-agent-turn gateway clients run in worker threads. The custom-CA overhead only applies when [network] ssl_verify is a path.
cost: Re-measured in the isolated scratch env: httpx.AsyncClient() median 9.88 ms (max 189 ms), versus 0.04 ms with a shared SSLContext. ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) alone is 9.12 ms. This matches the finder. It is real per construction, but it lands on cold or off-loop paths.
fix: Cache one ssl.SSLContext per normalised ssl_verify value (functools.lru_cache keyed on the setting string) and return it from httpx_verify() and ssl_context_for_transport() even for the default True case. Cache the merged-bundle path per (certifi mtime/size, CA digest). In guarded_fetch_requests, default to a module-level pooled session built with create_default_session().
fix_notes: Caching one ssl.SSLContext per normalised setting is fine: httpx accepts a shared context and SSLContext is safe to share across clients and threads. For the custom-CA case, key the cache on (path, mtime_ns, size) or on the content digest, not the path string alone, or a rotated corporate CA stays trusted until restart. The merged-bundle code already guards against exactly this (qodo #2223 finding 7). The module-level pooled requests session for guarded_fetch_requests is NOT low risk. requests.Session is not documented as thread-safe, and its cookie jar would carry cookies across unrelated fetches from different callers and threads, which undermines the function's cross-origin credential-stripping intent. Its verify value would also be frozen at creation. Prefer a per-call egress.create_default_session(): the cost is irrelevant next to the network round-trip, and it also closes a real policy gap, because today's bare requests.Session() ignores the [network] ssl_verify custom CA.
evidence:
def httpx_verify():
    setting = tls_verify_setting()
    if setting is True or setting is False:
        return setting          # True -> httpx builds a fresh SSLContext + certifi load per client
_additive_context: ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()); load_verify_locations(custom)
_merged_bundle_path: cache_dir = Path(get_user_data_dir()) / "cache"   # F1 cost + sha256 per call
egress.py:1062  sess = session or requests.Session()   # 6 of 9 callers pass no session
reason: Code is as quoted: tls_trust.py:234-244 httpx_verify returns bare True/False, :129-135 _additive_context builds a certifi+custom context on every call, :170-201 _merged_bundle_path does get_user_data_dir, mkdir, stat and a sha256 of the custom CA on every requests_verify(), and egress.py:1062 has `sess = session or requests.Session()`. I traced all 23 factory call sites. None is a hot path on the event loop. (1) Console setup-card discovery (chat_screen.py:15443 run_worker of an async coroutine, so it is on the loop) runs once per screen, only while the setup card blocks, and uses one shared client for the whole gather. (2) console_settings_modal.py:943 probe runs on the loop once per user click. (3) Image_Generation/http_client.fetch_json/create_client builds a client per request inside the sync adapters, which run in worker threads. (4) console_provider_gateway._new_owned_http_client caches one client per loop; agent turns run on a fresh asyncio.run loop in a worker thread, so that is one client per turn off the loop. (5) TTS/base_backends builds one client per backend init. requests_verify() only costs anything with a custom CA, which is a rare config, and those WebSearch callers are sync requests running off the loop. No open task found.

title: optional_deps.check_dependency says it caches but never reads its cache: every call re-imports, logs debug, and for missing modules re-scans sys.path
trigger: Per image preview render, per Markdown parser-factory construction, per Kokoro language check. All are user-driven and none is per-keystroke or per-tick.
cost: Not re-measured. The finder's figures (6.2 us installed, 42.2 us missing) are plausible: __import__ of an already-imported module is a sys.modules hit, the f-string dominates, and a missing module re-walks the sys.path finders. Negligible.
fix: Return DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] / MODULES[module_name] when a previous probe has already set them; keep reset_dependency_checks() as the invalidation hook.
fix_notes: The proposed fix is incorrect. (1) DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE is pre-seeded with False for pristine keys ('pillow', 'textual_image', 'lxml', 'PIL', ...; _INITIAL_DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE at ~:79), so 'already probed' cannot be told apart from 'never probed'. (2) feature_name keys are shared across modules: check_websearch_deps probes lxml, bs4, trafilatura and langdetect all under 'websearch_core', and kokoro_languages uses f'kokoro_{extra}'. Returning DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] would report bs4 present just because lxml was. (3) The module deliberately re-probes on False instead of trusting a stale negative (lazy_embeddings_rag_available docstring, ~:905-935), so caching negatives would hide runtime installs. A safe minimal version is a positive-only cache keyed by module: `if module_name in MODULES: DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] = True; return True`, and/or brace-style lazy loguru formatting. The gain is about 5 us per call, so this is optional.
evidence:
def check_dependency(module_name, feature_name=None) -> bool:
    """Check if a dependency is available and cache the result."""
    ...
    module = __import__(module_name)
    MODULES[module_name] = module
    logger.debug(f"✅ {module_name} dependency found. ...")
reason: Code is as quoted: optional_deps.py:613 check_dependency writes DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE/MODULES but never reads them, and re-runs __import__ (:639) plus an eagerly formatted logger.debug f-string on every call, despite the docstring's 'cache the result'. The callers are as claimed: library_media_image_preview.py:132/:226 (per preview), markdown_parsing.py:98 front_matter_parser_factory (4 call sites), kokoro_languages.py:73, reranker.py:976, search_backend_settings.py:242, terminal_utils.py:62 and others (70 call sites total, most inside optional_deps' own group checkers). The cost is microseconds next to the image decode or Markdown construction it accompanies, so this is hygiene only.

title: The input validation module builds about 30 validation models (pydantic) and loads the regex package at import, on the boot path
trigger: Every boot: tldw_chatbook.app imports Utils.input_validation directly (app.py:95). It is also in boot_import_modules.txt.
cost: Boot importtime runs: input_validation self 10.2 to 13.3 ms, cumulative 22.8 to 28.7 ms, and regex cumulative 4.5 to 5.1 ms. My isolated probe with pydantic, loguru, metrics_logger and reasoning_config preloaded: own import 7.0 to 7.2 ms warm (14.1 ms cold first run), regex 4.2 ms warm (21.5 ms cold). About 4.5 ms (regex) is cleanly avoidable. The model-splitting share of about 7 ms is only partly avoidable, depending on which models boot-path modules actually use. The total is under about 10 ms per boot, so P3 holds; at most a borderline P2.
fix: Build the TypeAdapters lazily (functools.cache factories) and split rarely used models (terminal, canvas, buddy, worktree) into a submodule imported by their only callers; load regex lazily inside the grapheme helper.
fix_notes: Lazy regex is trivial and safe: compile the grapheme pattern in a functools.cache helper that imports regex locally. Do not reach for a blanket pydantic defer_build shortcut. In my probe, setting BaseModel.model_config['defer_build']=True before import made the import slower (21 to 28 ms), so measure per model before relying on it. If rarely used models move to a submodule, keep the public names importable from input_validation through a PEP 562 __getattr__ so the ~200 import sites don't churn. Otherwise the split is a structural change larger than the saving.
evidence:
import regex
_BATCH_TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER = TypeAdapter(Literal[...])
_TMUX_IDENTIFIER = TypeAdapter(Annotated[str, Field(strict=True, pattern=...)])
class ReasoningHistorySelectorInput(BaseModel): ...   # ~30 BaseModel classes at module scope
reason: Code is as quoted: input_validation.py:16 `import regex`, :32 and :35 module-scope TypeAdapters, and 28 pydantic BaseModel subclasses (counted by introspection) in a 1927-line module. app.py:95 imports escape_markup from it, and there are about 200 import sites. regex is used only for _EXTENDED_GRAPHEME_PATTERN (:99), and only inside the terminal-session-name validator (:960). I checked all 671 modules in boot_import_modules.txt: input_validation is the only boot module with a module-scope regex import, and none of the third-party packages in the boot importtime set are known regex users, so deferring regex really removes it from boot. No open perf task covers this. TASK-32855 and TASK-32807.6 touch the module for other reasons.

title: The durable-write primitives flush to disk twice per write (F_FULLFSYNC on file and directory), costing 4.5–8 ms median and up to 45 ms, which is about 47× a plain fsync
trigger: Every atomic_write_* / atomic_private_write_* call: config saves (mostly threaded; on the loop in lab_frame.toggle_lab_rail per click and in the one-shot apply-detected-local-server), the scheduler heartbeat every 30 s off the loop, and MCP log rotation every 500 records.
cost: Re-measured in the scratch dir: atomic_write_text on a 4 KB file had median 8.01 ms, p90 11.1 ms, max 24.6 ms, versus plain fsync+replace 0.17 ms. This matches the finder's 8.06 ms. A config save on the loop adds TOML serialisation and locking on top.
fix: Keep the durability, but make it explicit: add a `durable: bool` parameter (default True) so preference and UI-state writes can use a plain fsync, and add a debug assertion or lint (as in TASK-2834) that these helpers never run on the event-loop thread.
fix_notes: A `durable=False` parameter reverses a deliberate durability decision (the TASK-32896 work stream and file_durability's cost note), and config.toml holds credentials and settings, so it is an owner/ADR call, not a low-risk tweak. The lazier fix that keeps durability: move the remaining on-loop writers (lab_frame.toggle_lab_rail -> save_rail_layout, and _apply_detected_local_server) onto thread workers like every other rail or preference save already does. The 'never on the event loop' assertion is TASK-2834's scope (open), so fold it in there rather than filing it again.
evidence:
os.fsync(fd)
if platform.system() == "Darwin":
    fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_FULLFSYNC)
atomic_write_text: f.flush(); flush_file(f.fileno())  ...  fsync_parent_directory(parent_dir)  # dir fd -> flush_file again
reason: Code is as quoted: file_durability.py:63-67 does fsync followed by F_FULLFSYNC on Darwin. atomic_file_ops.py:123 calls flush_file on the temp file and :143 calls fsync_parent_directory, which does a second full flush through flush_directory -> flush_file. The cost is intentional and documented: file_durability.py:14-17 has a 'Cost note (measured ...) ~300x a plain os.fsync. That is the price of actually reaching the platter', and TASK-32896 (To Do) is the work stream that asked for exactly this barrier. On-loop callers: most UI config saves are @work(thread=True) or run_worker(thread=True) (chat_screen :13152/:13322/:13424, library_screen :21729/:21786/:27921/:29378, home_screen :862, settings_screen console toggles :7138, Console workspace wiring.py:1069, watchlists layout persist). I found real on-loop callers the finder missed. UI/Screens/lab_frame.py:536 toggle_lab_rail, reached from @on(Button.Pressed) handlers at ~:525/:531, calls save_rail_layout -> save_setting_to_cli_config -> atomic_private_write_text synchronously once per Lab rail click. chat_screen.py:15470 _apply_detected_local_server is a one-shot on-loop save. Also scheduler_heartbeat writes every 30 s poll through asyncio.to_thread (off the loop), and MCP execution_log uses the atomic writer only on rotation (every 500 records). No hot on-loop trigger, so P3 is right.

title: Warm load_settings()/get_user_data_dir() still pay the per-call storage-admission handshake (TASK-32804.1 fastpath covers only get_cli_setting)
trigger: Every warm load_settings / get_cli_providers_and_models / get_runtime_config_snapshot / get_user_data_dir / get_*_db_path call from the event loop. In this slice: CompactModelBar compose and on_mount (once per ChatScreen instance), and maybe_offer_project_skills_import (app.py:15573, workspace.py:5206/5220/5237, library/settings screens), which calls get_user_data_dir on the loop when there are discoveries. The repo-wide call-site counts make many more loop callers near-certain.
cost:
KEEP, and upgrade to P0. The finding is real, and the warm load_settings admission turns out to be almost the whole cost of the Console's idle 4 Hz poll and of every composer keystroke. The Widgets-slice call sites on their own only justify P2/P3.

(1) Primitive micro-benchmark. Isolated scratch profile, audit tree on PYTHONPATH, host loadavg 40-65 on 18 cores, so absolute numbers are inflated.
- Warm cost per call (thread-CPU min / median): load_settings 15.2-22.6 / 27-30 ms, 647 opens, 1 admission. get_cli_providers_and_models 16.6 / 24 ms. get_user_data_dir 56-76 / 77-86 ms, 1723 opens. get_cli_setting 0.002 ms.
- The fix sketch, an unguarded warm _SETTINGS_CACHE hit ahead of @guarded, costs 0.002 ms and returns the identical object.
- Opens grow by exactly 39 per path level (load_settings) and 104 per level (get_user_data_dir). Each ancestor walk from / to HOME/.config/tldw_cli/recovery-bootstrap is repeated 39 times per call.
- cProfile: 59% of the time is posix.open, from acquire_storage (3.44 of 4.41 s) and admission_authority/_registry (1.49 s).
- In-process decomposition that times the walks separately: at the real depth (6 components, not 15 in scratch) the cost is about 0.6-0.8x the scratch figure. Applied to the first verifier's quiet-host 8.6 ms min, that gives about 5-7 ms per warm load_settings and about 20+ ms per get_user_data_dir on a real macOS profile.

(2) Headless isolated boot. TldwCli.run_test(235x52), network_guard on with 0 blocked attempts, ChatScreen current, app_config disk-loaded = True. Two runs; A/B with a lock-free load_settings warm hit patched into the importing modules.
- ChatScreen._poll_console_credential_readiness, the idle tick: baseline 21.1-22.0 ms min / 29-33 ms median, exactly 1.0 load_settings admission per tick. With the warm hit: 0.06-0.07 ms. About 99.7% of each tick is this handshake.
- _sync_console_workbench_actions_from_draft, the per-keystroke handler: 21.8-21.9 ms min / 32 ms median, 1.0 admission per call. With the warm hit: 0.14-0.17 ms.
- get_cli_providers_and_models stayed at about 24 ms in the fast arm, because config.py calls its own load_settings. So the fix must live inside load_settings itself, as the finding proposes.

(3) Trigger trace, exhaustive for the hot paths.
- Poll: chat_screen.py:16947 set_interval(0.25, _poll_console_credential_readiness) is armed unconditionally in _start_console_view_after_reconciliation and stopped only at 17135. In the poll body (11994-12020), _console_derivation_scope creates a fresh memo every tick (7651-7674). _active_console_settings_readiness_uncached then reaches _provider_readiness_app_config (7700), which calls load_settings() because app.app_config = load_settings() (app.py:7824) makes the disk-loaded predicate true. The snapshot early-return happens after that call, so nothing caches across ticks.
- Keystroke: ConsoleComposerBar posts DraftChanged on every printable key (console_composer_bar.py:4489/4502). The @on handler at chat_screen.py:22872 calls _sync_console_workbench_actions_from_draft, which opens a new scope and makes 1 admission.
- Cost: realistic 5-7 ms x 4 Hz = about 20-28 ms/s, roughly 2-3% of a core, constant while idling on the Console. That meets the rubric's P0 background-tax bar. Keystrokes add about 5-7 ms each (P1).
- This residual is exactly what TASK-32804.3's notes leave open ('~8 ms/tick'), and it is the per-call cost behind TASK-24454. One fix in config.load_settings (and memoizing get_user_data_dir) closes all three. Dedupe against TASK-32804.1, 32804.3 and 24454.

(4) Widgets-slice sites, full caller trace.

The animation interval (0.01-0.1 s) then ticks until the category or screen unmounts. The ticks skip rendering while the screen is not current but still wake up.

Pick a value of at least the card duration plus a margin, or add a separate 'stop after N s' timer that does not feed the compression. The 'Play selected' button already remounts, so replay stays available. Debouncing the highlight (about 150 ms set_timer, cancelled on each new highlight) is safe. Tests that assert an immediate preview mount on highlight would need to wait for the debounce. Probable extra waste, not verified: _get_terminal_size runs in on_mount before layout, so #splash-display likely has size 0 and the effect falls back to app.size, computing a full-terminal grid for a smaller pane. Sizing from the preview container after the first layout would cut per-frame cost further.

In splash_screen.py:325 the auto-close timer is armed only when duration > 0, so the preview gets no close timer. The reveal compression at :381-389 is also skipped, because it needs self.duration > 0. The set_interval at :404 then runs until close() or unmount. _update_animation (:471) returns early only when the widget is detached or the screen is not active. On every other tick _render_animation_frame calls effect_handler.update(), and base_effect has no completion or stop state. Display.update(layout=False) is skipped only when the frame is unchanged. title: llama.cpp snapshot manager runs a 1 Hz layout-refreshing tick even when no operation is in flight
trigger: From the first selection of the llama.cpp view in the LLM management window until the window unmounts, the timer fires every second regardless of whether an operation is running. The layout pass happens only while that screen is current.
cost: Estimated well under 1 ms per second: one wakeup, a bounded view() build, one query_one, re-visualizing a short string and a partial layout. That is hygiene-level idle cost, not a measurable percentage of a core.
fix: Arm the interval only while view.started_at is set (start it from _paint when an operation begins, stop it when it ends); skip the update when the text is unchanged; use update(..., layout=False).
fix_notes: Start the interval in _paint or _paint_elapsed when view.started_at becomes non-None, and stop it and set it to None when started_at returns to None. Paint the final status once on the transition so the elapsed suffix disappears. Also skip the Static.update when the composed text equals the last painted text. layout=False is only safe if #snapshot-operation-status has a fixed height. It is a plain Static whose content length varies with the status message and may wrap at narrow widths, so keep layout=True unless the CSS pins its height. title: Every outermost ChaChaNotes transaction() now pays a ~7-12 ms storage-admission handshake (cross-cutting root of F1/F2/F3/F6/F7; outside the slice)
trigger: Every outermost `with db.transaction()` on the app's file-backed ChaChaNotes DB, on any thread. Confirmed on-loop instances: the Console send snapshot (F1, via prompt_queue._stage_normal_chain -> launch_chain -> _admit_console_turn_to_runtime) and the persona-scope paths. Off-loop but always-on: the 1 Hz legacy trace maintenance run_batch.
cost:
Scripts are in scratch/second-lens-slice6/ (f0_bench.py, f0_floor.py, f0_split.py, probe_app2.py). The host was heavily loaded throughout (load average 33-65 on 18 cores), so absolute wall times are inflated. The real-depth figures below are extrapolated from measured minimums and a depth scan.

(1) Microbenchmark, app-equivalent state: config import runs admit_startup(), the DB is at the config path, and the startup lease is live. transaction()+SELECT 1 = exactly 1 acquire_storage. execute_query costs 0.017 ms. posix.open per transaction grows with HOME depth: 261 @11 components, 309 @14, 357 @17, 453 @23, i.e. +16 per component, plus ~16 fstat, ~16 close and 6 lstat per component. Syscalls are 74% of the time (cProfile). Floor (minimum of 1200 runs): 5.7-5.9 ms @11 and 7.8-8.2 ms @17, so ~2.5 ms at a real 2-component home (/Users/x). Loaded median extrapolates to ~3.6 ms. Working figure: ~2.5-4 ms per outermost admission at real depth.

(2) Headless TldwCli (Pilot) in a scratch profile. I wrapped acquire_storage on MainThread and classified callers by stack.
- Outermost ChaChaNotes transactions on the loop per steady Console send: 12-14. On the first send of a new conversation: 28, 20 of them from console_context_repository.load_applicable_branch_memory via context_control_inputs. Boot: 8. Per send that is ~30-56 ms at real depth (~70-112 ms on the first send). That consumer alone is P1.
- The same handshake is paid far more often on the loop by other consumers. Steady send: ~450-460 on-loop acquisitions (config 214-232, recovery_activation 153, AgentRunsDB 22-29, WorkspaceDB 13). First send: 834. Idle: 8 per second, all config (_maybe_refresh_stale_default_console_settings -> load_settings).
- At 2.5-4 ms each, that is ~1.1-1.8 s of loop time per send and 2-3% of a core at idle.

The P1 downgrade relied on single-transaction arithmetic. Both proposed fixes (a lease/flag fast path, or caching verified directory identity per generation) land in storage_admission.acquire_storage/_repository_operation and retire every one of these consumers. As a root-cause item it is therefore P0 on both the per-send-stall and the idle-tax criteria. If the fix plan scopes F0 to ChaChaNotes consumers only, rate it P1.

Known-task overlap: TASK-32804.1 (In Progress) amortises the same handshake only for config reads. load_settings callers still pay it at 840ed2ca58. No open task covers acquire_storage itself. Merge F0 with that task and with the MCP recovery_activation consumer (153 per send) as one root item.
fix: Make admission a per-session or per-thread lease that is acquired once and revalidated only on pause, maintenance or generation-change events. The uncontended path of `_core_operation` should be a flag check, like the TASK-31502 AC for the quiescence registry. At minimum, skip `acquire_storage` for read-only transactions and for callers already inside an operation. Slice-local mitigations are F1/F7: use `execute_query` for reads.
fix_notes: Treat the fix as high risk and a design decision for the backup owner. TASK-32562's notes record deliberate 'no cached authority / no validation cache' choices, so a per-session lease reverses a stated design and needs sign-off. Do not skip admission for 'read-only' transaction() blocks. transaction() is used for read-then-write and immediate=True paths, and a read during capture or restore can observe a file being replaced. The safer equivalents are: (a) route pure reads through execute_query/get_connection, which already enforce the pause via _core_access; (b) cut the per-acquire syscall work, e.g. cache the verified directory identity (st_dev/st_ino) of the bootstrap root and registry, revalidated on a generation counter bumped by pause, enroll or maintenance, rather than re-walking every path component 10x per acquire. self._maintenance_context.__enter__()

title: Dictionary version-history sidecar grows without bound: every edit appends a full dictionary snapshot and rewrites the whole file with the pure-Python indent encoder; loaded at boot
trigger: Every dictionary mutation: update, add/update/delete/reorder entry, import, revert. Every dictionary-service call through the deepcopy. Boot load. Calls run on to_thread or a _DictionaryJob via ChatDictionaryScopeService._call_backend, but the pure-Python encode and deepcopy hold the GIL.
cost:
New and worse than filed: growth is O(n^2) on the ordinary authoring path. The Personas-screen dictionary editor calls scope add_entry (personas_screen.py:6492). Each add bumps the version and _record_history appends a FULL snapshot. There is no cap anywhere: a full-file grep for MAX_/slice/pop(0) returns 0 hits, and there are 10 _record_history/_persist_history sites.

Measured (f234_bench.py), one dictionary built entry-by-entry through LocalChatDictionaryService.add_entry:

| Entries | Sidecar | add_entry | list_dictionaries | get_dictionary | boot build_dictionary_service |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 0.27 MB | | | | |
| 50 | 1.03 MB | | | | |
| 100 | 3.98 MB | | | | |
| 150 | 8.86 MB, 151 versions | 114 -> 550 ms | 40 -> 339 ms min | 63 -> 274 ms min | 352 -> 445 ms min |

The 150-row timings run from the start of the build to 150 entries, under load.

Pure-CPU split on the 8.86 MB file (minimum of 7):
- json.loads 17 ms: boot, pre-paint, on the loop via build_dictionary_service in __init__.
- copy.deepcopy(_history) 57 ms: paid on every guarded dictionary-service call, reads included, via chat_source_participants.operation's rollback snapshot.
- json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys) 124 ms per edit, against 19 ms compact (6.5x).

The service calls themselves run off-loop (ChatDictionaryScopeService._call_backend uses to_thread/_DictionaryJob) but hold the GIL, and the boot load is on the loop. At 300 entries this extrapolates to ~35 MB, ~70 ms boot load, and ~0.5 s dump per edit.

Unbounded durable growth that scales quadratically with user data on the boot path is P1. Compact JSON and skipping the read-path deepcopy are safe now; the retention cap is a product decision.
fix: Cap history per dictionary (for example the last 20 versions and 200 activity rows, oldest dropped). Write compact JSON (indent=None uses the C encoder, 5-10x faster). Better: move versions into a SQLite table or per-dictionary sidecars so an edit writes only its own bucket and boot reads nothing.

title: Visual-identity resolution re-reads and fully decodes the chosen expression image (every frame) on every resolve under 2 admissions; the Console avatar pipeline resolves 2-3x per request change

Textual 8.2.8 DOMNode.remove_class/add_class call update_node_styles -> app.update_styles -> stylesheet.update_nodes immediately when the class set actually changes. So remove w-0/add w-0/remove h-0/add h-0 is 4 real applies even when nothing changed. The cap>0 branch (w-auto/h-1) does the same. git show ae9093a714 confirms these lines replaced set_styles(width=0/height=0), which is a no-op when unchanged, so this is a regression of TASK-21120 leg 1. The re-verification that dismissed that leg as 'microseconds' predates this commit. Trigger corrected: insert_text calls _sync_current_action_state once per printable key. The screen's DraftChanged handler (_sync_console_workbench_actions_from_draft -> _push_console_control_state_if_changed) never calls composer.sync_action_state; the screen's only call is inside _sync_console_control_bar_under_config (chat_screen.py:22333). So the cost is 4 update_nodes per key, not 8. The finder's probe doubled it by calling _sync_current_action_state explicitly after insert_text. The strip's 4 layout arms add no extra layout because they coalesce with the other two per-key layout sources (see F2). At ~1 ms per key it is below the P1 bar of 10-20 ms. title: Every keystroke still forces a whole-screen layout; the three triggers are all removable (TASK-24453's 'floor' is not a floor)
trigger: Every printable key, delete, word delete and paste in the Console composer: insert_text -> _sync_hidden_input + _refresh_visible_draft + _sync_current_action_state.
cost:
Probe: the real TldwCli booted headless in a scratch profile (HOME, XDG_* and TLDW_CONFIG_PATH asserted to be under scratch/sl60-lens2; null keyring; network guard on). Console was the initial screen at 211x44. Typed 45 keys with Pilot, then counted Screen._refresh_layout calls and attributed every Layout post and refresh(layout=True) to a widget and call site. Script: scratch/sl60-lens2/probe.py; outputs are the out_*.json files there. Machine load average was 25-45, so the figures below are thread CPU, not wall time.

Results:
(a) Base: the composer arms exactly one layout per key from three widgets: visible-text 1.04/key (_refresh_visible_draft), hidden Input 1.00/key (_sync_hidden_input, via Input._watch_value writing virtual_size), and the reason strip 1.00/key (4.1 refresh(layout=True) calls per key, from _sync_send_disabled_reason plus fastpath apply).
(b) Arm f2 (layout=False on visible-text, plus the hidden Input skipping the virtual_size write): still 1.24 layouts/key. The reason strip alone keeps the layout, so F2's two legs are worth nothing unless F1's gate lands with them.
(c) Arm f2f1 (both legs plus the strip gated on an unchanged signature): composer-originated layouts fall to about 0.02/key, confirming the removal on the real Console, not only the 500-filler model. The residual is 0.36-0.44/key, all from the 0.2 s debounced ConsoleDraftSpendRefresh: _apply_console_settings_summary_state (temperature and max-tokens Statics), the cost chip, 12 settings rows and the right-rail reconcile. So '0 layouts/key' holds only for bursts faster than 5 keys/s. At ~40 WPM that debounced sync fires after most keys and arms its own layout, which is a separate issue.
(d) Cost of the removable layout, as median layout CPU per key: 5.5 and 4.8 ms on an empty conversation (532 widgets); 9.35 ms with 200 seeded messages and 8.86 ms with 1000 (both 883 widgets, because the transcript mount window is capped, so the cost plateaus near 9 ms). That is lower than the finder's 10-12 ms and the verifier's 8-12 ms.
(e) Context: total main-thread CPU per key is a median of 87-134 ms, dominated by config-admission and readiness work (cProfile: config_participants.operation, private_paths posix.open, _provider_readiness_app_config, SpendRefresh). That work is already tracked by TASK-24454 and related tasks, so this layout is about 5-10% of per-key cost.

Verdict: real and on the hottest path, but at the floor of the P1 band. Keep P1 only as a bundle with F1. Corrected cost: about 1 full-screen reflow per key, 5 ms (empty) to 9 ms (populated) CPU. Cadence caveat as in (c).
fix: (1) update(renderable, layout=False) in _refresh_visible_draft -- the Static's size is pinned (w-fill + inline height/min/max set by _apply_draft_height, nowrap/clip), the same reasoning TASK-21692 already applied to the blink path; _apply_draft_height keeps its own refresh(layout=True) when geometry changes. (2) Stop mirroring the draft into the hidden Input per key: route the screen's @on(Input.Changed, '#console-command-input') consumer (chat_screen.py:20221) to a composer-posted message and make the mirror lazy (write on send/flush), or subclass the hidden Input to skip the virtual_size write while display is none. (3) F1's gate.
fix_notes: (1) is safe only because every geometry-changing path goes through _apply_draft_height, _apply_collapsed_geometry or a display toggle, which trigger layout themselves; keep it that way. (2) is the medium-risk part. The Input.Changed consumer must keep firing on EVERY draft mutation (unknown-command disarm, fleet_wake.retry_soon, draft-spend route_edit). draft_text(), _has_any_draft_content() and _display_draft_text() also read the Input before segments initialise. Two options: a hidden-mirror Input subclass that skips the virtual_size write while still posting Changed (private Textual API; pin it with a test), or a composer-posted message plus a lazy mirror. Measured with the mirror stubbed out, so correctness of the replacement needs its own test.
evidence:
# _refresh_visible_draft (per key): Static.update defaults to layout=True
self.query_one("#console-command-visible-text", Static).update(renderable)
self._apply_draft_height(row_count)  # already refresh(layout=True)s on real geometry change
# _sync_hidden_input (per key): Input._watch_value sets virtual_size (Reactive layout=True)
self.query_one("#console-command-input", Input).value = canonical
reason: Verified all three layout sources per key. (1) _refresh_visible_draft (:3660) calls Static.update(renderable), which defaults to layout=True. The Static's geometry is pinned: w-fill is `width: $ds-width-fill !important`, height/min/max are written by _apply_draft_height, and text is nowrap/clip. TASK-21692 already uses layout=False on the blink path with the same reasoning, and _apply_draft_height keeps its own refresh(layout=True) when geometry really changes. (2) _sync_hidden_input (:1829): Textual's Input._watch_value sets virtual_size = Size(content_width, 1). content_width is cell_len(value)+1, so it changes on every key, and virtual_size is Reactive(layout=True). Widget._check_refresh posts messages.Layout without checking display, so display:none does not help. (3) The strip dance from F1. TASK-24453 (Done) recorded ~1.04 layouts/key as a 'legitimate floor'. The probe shows the floor is removable, which is new evidence against that claim. The only outside consumer of the hidden input is chat_screen.py:20221 @on(Input.Changed, '#console-command-input') (count 1 outside the composer), so the mirror can be re-routed.

title: ADR-161 class-dance pattern performs synchronous stylesheet applies on unmounted widgets at every compose/recompose (composer mount 29 -> 95 update_nodes)
trigger: Boot first paint: the Console composes ConsoleComposerBar and ~24 other dance-bearing widgets. Also every refresh(recompose=True) of those widgets and every modal open. Per-visit re-mint no longer applies (TASK-31520).
cost:
Probe: the same isolated real-app boot, Console as the initial screen at 211x44. Every Stylesheet.update_nodes call was classified by whether its root node is_attached and attributed to the Textual API that app code called. Stylesheet.apply was CPU-timed.

(a) Boot to first Console layout: 533-555 update_nodes calls on unattached nodes, one node each, costing 171-269 ms CPU (5 runs). By API: dom.add_class called directly from app code (the ADR-161 class dance) accounts for 284-291 calls and 75-97 ms CPU. Textual's own Button.__init__ reactive watchers (the TASK-24452 watch_flat chain) account for 234-248 calls and 115-130 ms. set_class, remove_class, Input.__init__ and reactive.__set__ add 14-16 more.
(b) Top call sites: composer _bounded_button 46, left_rail.compose 41, destination_rail.compose 37, workspace_context 33+24+10, inspector_section.compose 25, run_inspector 21, composer.compose 19.
(c) Interleaved A/B, 3 reps each, boot only. Arm f3 makes DOMNode.update_node_styles a no-op when not is_attached. Boot applies drop from 2754-2757 to 2163. Total apply CPU goes from 1314.8/1379.4/1187.0 ms (mean 1294) to 1244.7/1011.3/1090.7 ms (mean 1116), a net saving of about 180 ms CPU at first paint. The dance share is about 75-97 ms of that.
(d) Safety: a digest of all 532 first-paint widgets (classes, computed display/size/min/max/colours/spacing/border, plus region) is identical between base and f3 across all runs once session UUIDs are normalised, so skipping pre-attach updates changes no first-paint style.
(e) Trigger trace: the chat route is reusable=True (screen_registry.py, TASK-31520), so there is no per-visit re-mint; the cost is paid once per launch at boot first paint. Inspector-section recompose happens only on a structural row change (console_inspector_section.py:807) and costs about 6-8 dance applies, around 3 ms each time (P3). The settings modal has 22 sites, about 10 ms per open (P2/P3). Transcript per-message builders carry no dance: console_transcript.py:7755 only removes classes, which returns early.

Corrections: the cost is about 180 ms CPU net per boot for all pre-attach style updates, of which the dance is about 75-97 ms. P1 stands on the boot/first-paint criterion (known context: TASK-24452).

Better fix than codemodding the 227 sites: one override, TldwCli.update_styles(node), that returns early when node is not the App and not node.is_attached. It is the single funnel, since DOMNode.update_node_styles calls app.update_styles, and App._register re-applies the stylesheet at attach. It also removes the Button-constructor share, which the per-site helper would miss. is_attached (not is_mounted) keeps on_mount self-class changes working, as the first verifier noted. Pin it with a first-paint style-digest test.
fix: One shared helper (e.g. Widgets/design_tokens.set_token_class(widget, prefix, cls)) that (a) no-ops when cls is already the only prefix-matching class, (b) passes update=widget.is_mounted to remove_class/add_class, and (c) for compose-time construction, prefer classes='... w-fill h-1' in the constructor (no update_styles). Codemod the 227 sites to it; keep Tests/UI/test_component_pattern_governance.py satisfied by teaching it the helper.
fix_notes: The proposed update=widget.is_mounted is UNSAFE. Textual sets _is_mounted only after the widget's own Mount handler returns (message_pump.py:612), but _register has already applied the stylesheet by then. Class changes a widget makes to itself in on_mount (e.g. the composer's on_mount -> _apply_draft_height -> self.remove_class('h-*')) would be skipped and never re-applied, leaving stale styles. Use update=widget.is_attached: unattached means _register will apply later. Better still, pass the token class through the constructor's classes=, which costs no apply at all. The no-op-when-already-the-only-prefix-class check (part a) also fixes F1. Teach Tests/UI/test_component_pattern_governance.py about the helper.
evidence:

visible_draft.remove_class(*(name for name in visible_draft.classes if name.startswith("w-")))
visible_draft.set_styles(width=None)
visible_draft.add_class("w-fill")   # -> DOMNode.update_node_styles -> app.update_styles -> stylesheet.update_nodes NOW
# repeated for h-*, for every child in compose; 227 sites / 25 files repo-wide, 107 in this slice
reason: MessagePump.app resolves through the active_app contextvar, so class changes on widgets built in compose (not yet attached) still reach app.update_styles -> stylesheet.update_nodes -> apply(). App._register (app.py:3656-3670) then applies the stylesheet to every new widget with a shared cache, so the pre-attach applies are pure waste. Site count confirmed: 227 dance sites in 25 files repo-wide, 200 in Widgets/Console, 39 in the composer. All cited sites exist (composer:6299, rail_handle:83, steering_bar:159, outcome_notice:105; the inspector_section cite is file-level, real compose sites at :457+). Trigger correction: 'every Console visit' no longer applies. TASK-31520 (Done) made the chat route reusable (screen_registry.py:99), so the re-mint is gone. The remaining triggers are boot first paint (Console is the initial tab), inspector-section recomposes on structural row changes (console_inspector_section.py:807), and modal opens (settings modal 22 sites, session switcher, image viewer). The composer alone clears the first-paint P1 bar.

title: Composer re-wraps the ENTIRE draft 2x per keystroke and 3-4x per Up/Down although only 8 rows render; long unbroken tokens wrap quadratically
trigger: Every edit with a large display draft (_refresh_visible_draft on each key) and every Up/Down (_move_cursor_vertically/_caret_visual_row plus refresh).
cost: Rerun of the wrap bench (isolated, width 140, row_count+renderable per key). Prose 2K/8K/20K: 0.31/1.15/2.78 ms. Code 20K: 3.52 ms. No-space blob 2K/8K/20K: 0.99/6.65/30.66 ms. The blob case is clearly quadratic.
fix: 1-entry memo of _wrap_draft_line_slices keyed (text, width) shared by row count, caret-row and vertical-move within one keystroke; _visible_draft_row_count stops after MAX_DRAFT_ROWS+1 rows; render only the logical lines around the caret window; ASCII fast path in _extend_fitting_cells/_cell_wrap_line (text.isascii() -> slice width-len(prefix) directly, no per-char cell_len of the joined string, no re-slicing of the remaining chunk). Keep the existing 100k-trial textwrap differential fuzz as the parity check.
fix_notes: An ASCII fast path must require printable ASCII: rich cell_len gives 0 width to control characters, so isascii() alone breaks the textwrap parity. A shared (text, width) memo will NOT be shared between the row count (wraps text+cursor glyph) and the renderable (wraps the caret-spliced text) because they wrap different strings. Memoise per wrapped string, or derive the row count from the renderable's slices. Capping the row count at MAX_DRAFT_ROWS+1 only helps multi-line drafts; a single 20K logical line still needs the per-row cost fixed (no per-character join measure, no per-row cell_len of the remaining chunk). Keep the 100k-trial differential fuzz as the parity gate.
evidence:
row_count = self._visible_draft_row_count(draft, width, ...)   # full wrap #1
renderable = self._current_visible_draft_renderable(draft, width)  # memo miss -> full wrap #2
# _extend_fitting_cells: O(W^2) per row on a long token
while end < len(text) and cell_len(prefix + text[: end + 1]) <= width:
    end += 1
# _cell_wrap_line re-slices the remaining chunk every row: chunks[-1] = chunk[len(piece):]
reason: Code confirmed. On a memo miss, _refresh_visible_draft wraps the whole draft twice: _visible_draft_row_count (:3076, wraps text+cursor glyph) and _current_visible_draft_renderable -> _draft_renderable -> _wrap_draft_line_slices (:2800), although MAX_DRAFT_ROWS=8. Up/Down adds full wraps in _move_cursor_vertically and _caret_visual_row (:5301). _extend_fitting_cells (:2598) grows one character at a time and measures cell_len(prefix+text[:end+1]) each step, O(W^2) per row. _cell_wrap_line re-slices the remaining chunk and calls cell_len on it every row (uncached for strings of 512+ characters), which is quadratic for long tokens without spaces. The TASK-22218 memo helps only the blink tick, not edits. There is no open task for this. The trigger needs a large uncollapsed display draft: pastes over 50 chars collapse by default, so it takes expanded pastes, collapse turned off, history recall, loaded drafts or dictation. That is a large-data-only path, so P2.

title: ConsoleActivityDisclosure.sync_activity/sync_header are unconditional and the transcript re-syncs every disclosure in a turn per thinking delta
trigger: Live agent/reasoning turns: any 0.2 s transcript poll whose turn activity_signature changed (every thinking delta and every tool status/result change) resyncs every disclosure in the turn.
cost: Rerun of the isolated disclosure probe with the app's fastpath, 30 unchanged disclosures, 300 fillers: 5.48 ms handler plus 1.0 Screen layout (23.9 ms) per pass. At 5 Hz that is up to ~27 ms/s of handler time, and more when layouts are not otherwise armed. The transcript-side widget construction in _activity_components comes on top and was not measured.
fix: In console_assistant_turn: short-circuit sync_activity/sync_header/_sync_visibility when (label, status, expanded, expandable, selected, raw_cli_presentation, tool_presentation) is unchanged; update label/status Statics only when their Content differs, with layout=False (header is height-pinned). In console_transcript._sync_activity_widgets: keep a per-disclosure signature and only build components / sync disclosures whose own signature moved.
fix_notes: An equality short-circuit in sync_activity/sync_header must cover detail_available and _has_actions (the transcript mutates both just before sync_activity) and tool_presentation.result_preview (drives preview.set_output). The bigger saving is skipping _activity_components for a disclosure whose own slice of the signature is unchanged; that is where the discarded widgets and large strings are built. Use layout=False on the label/status Statics only if the header's width/height do not depend on label length (check the header CSS).
evidence:
def sync_header(...):
    ...; self._sync_classes()
    self.label_widget.update(self._label_content())   # layout=True, no change check
    self.status_widget.update(self._status_content())
# transcript activity_signature embeds the full thinking text:
    self.thinking_detail_text(item.activity_id),
# -> _sync_activity_widgets rebuilds components + sync_activity for ALL disclosures
reason: Confirmed. The per-turn activity_signature (console_transcript.py:6996-7030) embeds thinking_detail_text(...) for thinking refs, so every thinking delta or tool status change breaks the turn-level gate (:7252-7257). _sync_activity_widgets (:7578) then loops over ALL disclosures of the turn. For each one it calls _activity_components (:7427), which builds a fresh Static holding the full args+tool-output string plus action/message row widgets, then discards them when the per-disclosure signatures match. It then calls sync_activity (:425) -> sync_header (:260), which does 2 unconditional Static.update(layout=True), ~8 set_class calls and an unconditional preview.set_output rewrap. The transcript poll runs every 0.2 s during runs (chat_screen.py:18947). The thinking label is fixed and a collapsed thinking row has an empty detail_signature, so the full resync on each delta is mostly avoidable. The answer header/body sync on the same row may still arm a layout on its own, so the removable layout is uncertain; the handler cost is certain. No open task found.

title: Conversation Inspector runs trace-capture projection/sanitization for every call of a turn on the event loop
trigger: User selects a Usage/Turn row in the Conversation Inspector. Runs once per message_id (cached in _trace_calls), N captures per agent turn.
cost: Isolated bench of project_capture_for_viewer on a synthetic FULL capture. 50 msgs / 23 KB request: FULL 17.3 ms, SAFE 8.7 ms. 400 msgs / 185 KB: FULL 129 ms, SAFE 48 ms per capture. A 10-call turn on a long conversation is a 0.5-1.3 s loop freeze on the first click. That is worse than the finder's sanitize-only estimate.
fix: Move the sort+projection loop into the thread: calls = await asyncio.to_thread(_project_all, captures, self._viewer_profile) and assign _trace_calls/_exchange_capture_by_call_key after the generation re-check (same shape as the existing _call_detail_text offload).
fix_notes: The projection is pure, so asyncio.to_thread is safe. Read self._viewer_profile and the bindings into locals before the thread. Mutate _trace_calls and _exchange_capture_by_call_key only on the loop, after re-checking generation, is_mounted and revision. Cheap extra win: project_capture_for_viewer discards json_text, so skip the json.dumps (a flag, or a payload-only variant of project_exchange_export).
evidence:
async def _show_trace_detail(...):   # run_worker(coroutine) -> event loop
    captures = await self._exchanges_loader(message_id)
    for ordinal, (capture, abandoned) in enumerate(sorted(captures, ...)):
        projected = (project_capture_for_viewer(capture, self._viewer_profile) ...)
# -> project_exchange_export -> build_request_capture + sanitize_capture_value (CredentialSanitizer walk)
# while the call-detail text right above IS offloaded: await asyncio.to_thread(self._call_detail_text, ...)
reason: Confirmed. The pane selection handler runs self.run_worker(self._show_trace_detail(...)), which is a coroutine and not a thread (console_conversation_inspector.py:662). After awaiting the loader, it sorts and runs project_capture_for_viewer (:762) for every capture of the message on the loop. That goes through project_exchange_export: build_request_capture, sanitize_capture_value on the response, sanitize_capture_value on the whole payload, CredentialSanitizer().sanitize, and json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True). The json text is then discarded because project_capture_for_viewer uses only .payload. It finishes with a deep `projected == capture` comparison. The per-call detail text right above is already offloaded with asyncio.to_thread (:712), which is the precedent. Production wiring passes capture_policy_bindings (chat_screen.py:12410), so the projection branch runs. The result is cached per message, and the inspector is a less frequent path, hence P2 despite the large freeze. No open task; TASK-32804.12 does not mention it.

(:1884). LocalPromptService.search_prompts and list_prompts are sync and call the Prompts_DB cursor directly. title: Character context runs an always-on 2 Hz poll that rebuilds a progress dict per row and never pauses while the reusable Console is suspended
trigger: The timer fires at 2 Hz on the event loop for the life of the reusable ChatScreen, including while another tab is active. The per-row counts rebuild only happens when rows exist and the scope fingerprint and authority guards pass, i.e. once the user has character conversations listed. With no rows, a tick costs one small subtree query.
cost: Estimated, not measured. Rows are bounded by CONSOLE_CHARACTER_GROUP_LIMIT=4 x ROW_LIMIT=5, so up to about 20 rows, not the 5-8 claimed (the search view caps at 8). Each rebuild is dict and list work over live sessions, around 10-50 us. That is at most about 1 ms per tick and well under 0.2% of a core, plus 2 permanent wakeups/s. Hygiene only.
fix: Compute the progress dict once per tick (hoist _progress_counts() out of the row loop / pass it in), skip when not self.screen.is_active, or better make it push-based from the fleet MessageStore inbox change; pause in ChatScreen.on_screen_suspend alongside the other visit timers.
fix_notes: Hoisting the counts fetch out of the row loop is safe, but keep pending_progress_count's per-row scope/database-identity/data-authority guard: pass the precomputed dict in rather than dropping the guard. An early return on `not self.screen.is_current` is cheap and safe, since counts refresh within 0.5 s of resume. Stopping and re-arming the timer from ChatScreen.on_screen_suspend/on_screen_resume also works, but needs a handle to the widget's timer. Making it push-based from MessageStore inbox changes is the better long-term shape but is larger scope.

title: Expression avatar ticks at 30 Hz and re-renders each frame's mosaic every loop cycle; activity elapsed timers tick at 10 Hz (documented as 1 Hz)
corrected: tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:142; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:216; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:232; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_assistant_turn.py:220 (stale comment only); sibling 0.1 s ticker at tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_transcript.py:1544
trigger: Needs a character with a multi-frame animated expression asset (for example Petdex or buddy pets) shown in the Console rail with motion enabled. After that, 30 Hz ticks run for the life of the reusable ChatScreen, including on other tabs, until the avatar is replaced or unmounted. Frames are re-rendered off-loop while the avatar is visible. The 10 Hz elapsed ticks run only while an activity is in the running/stopping state.
cost: Measured under an isolated profile against the audit tree with a random-noise image (the worst case for run merging): mosaic_from_image median 0.483 ms at 24x12 and 1.343 ms at 40x20, which reproduces the finder's numbers. At typical 7-15 fps that is about 0.3-2% of a core in a worker thread, which still contends for the GIL, plus the on-loop Static.update render per frame, for as long as the avatar is visible. Hidden 30 Hz ticks are a few attribute checks each: a wakeup tax, not CPU. P3 fits because the cost is conditional on a niche feature and each tick is well under 10 ms.
fix: Cache rendered mosaics per frame index in PreparedExpression (render each frame once), pause the avatar timer instead of early-returning when not visible (resume via on_screen_resume / visibility), and set _RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS to 1.0 with whole-second copy (or keep .1f but only while on screen).
fix_notes: Per-frame mosaic caching needs a memory cap. Frames go up to MAX_EXPRESSION_FRAME_COUNT=512, a 40x20 styled Text is roughly 100 KB or more, and _preparation_bytes does not account for renderables. Cache only under a byte or frame budget, per widget instance; box and monochrome are fixed per instance, so no extra invalidation is needed. Widgets do not receive ScreenSuspend/ScreenResume. To pause the timer while hidden, either stop it on `not self.screen.is_current` and re-arm from ChatScreen.on_screen_resume via a hook, or just drop to a slow cadence while not visible. A naive stop with no resume path would freeze the animation for good. Changing the elapsed ticker to 1 Hz is a UX and copy change that breaks pinned tests. Recommend only fixing the stale 'Once-per-second' comment.
evidence:
self._timer = self.set_interval(1 / 30, self._tick)   # infinite for plays == 0 (frame_at)
# _tick -> _visible() does screen.get_widget_at(region.center) every tick
# _paint(index) -> asyncio.to_thread(render_character_avatar_mosaic, image, ...) on every frame change, no per-frame cache
_RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1
# comment in _tick_raw_cli_elapsed: 'Once-per-second elapsed repaint'
reason: character_expression_avatar.py:142 arms `set_interval(1 / 30, self._tick)` only when the prepared expression has more than one frame. `_tick` (232-257) stops the timer only when `_current()` goes false or when `frame_at` reports finished. `frame_at` never reports finished when plays == 0, i.e. a WebP/GIF with loop=0 (character_expression_playback.py:69-83, 166-173). A plays=1 asset hidden mid-play also never advances elapsed time, so it keeps ticking too. While the Console is suspended, `_is_current` is still true: it checks `request == _latest_built_request and _is_mounted()` (character.py:445), and the screen stays mounted. `_visible()` then returns early on `self.screen.is_current`, so a hidden tick is cheap but still a wakeup, 30 per second. When visible, every tick also calls `screen.get_widget_at(region.center)`. On each frame change, `_paint` dispatches `asyncio.to_thread(render_character_avatar_mosaic, ...)` and there is no per-frame renderable cache, so every loop of the animation re-renders every frame. That path only applies in pixels mode, which is the default (`_console_image_default_mode() or 'pixels'`); graphics mode just swaps `_graphics.image`. The avatar only animates when `expression_motion_enabled` holds: Dynamic mode, react or manual, animations_enabled, and not reduce_motion. The elapsed-timer sub-claim is weak. `_RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` (console_assistant_turn.py:28) is deliberate: the copy is formatted `{elapsed:.1f}s` (lines 61 and 90), and tests pin tenths (Tests/UI/test_console_raw_cli_transcript.py:964 `"Running · 0.5s"`). Only the 'Once-per-second' comment at line 220 is stale. Each tick is a single `layout=False` update of a one-row Static, and the timer runs only while a tool or raw CLI command is running. TASK-32023 (Done) introduced the playback. No open task covers this.

title: Message-row class sync removes and re-adds managed classes on every sync, doubly restyling the whole Markdown reply subtree each streaming tick
known_task: none specific (TASK-26834 AC#2 is a related umbrella for Console subtree restyles on click interactions; it does not name streaming or this site)
trigger: Yes. The 5 Hz Console transcript poll runs for the whole duration of every streamed reply and agent turn. Each content delta or activity-status change alters the assistant-turn signature, which reaches _sync_message_classes on the Markdown answer row. Affects the default ROLE_ACCENTS style and IMMERSIVE_RP.

Timings are CPU time (thread_time) on a heavily loaded host (load average 24-46 on 18 cores), so absolute values run about 2-4x the finder's idle numbers; ratios and counts are load-independent. (1) One UNCHANGED _sync_message_classes call makes exactly 2 App.update_styles calls, covering 126 / 268 / 768 node applies at 20 / 40 / 120 blocks (subtree 63 / 134 / 384 nodes). It costs 46 / 95 / 536 ms. The diff version (set_classes(current - managed | want)) makes 0 restyles and takes 0.0 ms. With churn a restyle costs about 4x a no-change restyle at 120 blocks (536 ms vs 133 ms for one plain subtree restyle), so the waste grows faster than linearly. (3) Trigger trace (untruncated): refresh_messages has exactly 1 external await site, chat_screen.py:18460, gated by refresh_key != last. The key embeds _native_console_transcript_fingerprint (chat_screen.py:18176), which includes message content and status, so it changes on every tick while content streams. That runs from set_interval(0.2, _poll_transcript) at chat_screen.py:18947, i.e. 5 Hz for the whole reply. The other 12 callers are call_later(self.refresh_messages) inside console_transcript.py for selection, reveal and prune. It is a one-function change covering both row types. Add a regression test that counts update_node_styles calls on an unchanged sync.

No test references _sync_message_classes. Add a regression test that counts update_node_styles on an unchanged sync, and one that runs under NEUTRAL style.

title: Selecting or deselecting an assistant Markdown row restyles its entire Markdown subtree on every j/k or click

The restyle share is 30-33 / 52-55 / 191-208 ms. The remaining ~35 ms is a constant action-row mount that does not depend on block count. It scales linearly with the reply's Markdown block count and lands on every j/k step onto or off an assistant row and every click selection (select_message at console_transcript.py:5319 -> call_later(refresh_messages); on_key down/j and up/k -> action_select_next/previous -> _select_relative). Descendant rules also depend on it: _console.tcss:1631-1639 and _console_panels.tcss:1208. So Textual must at least invalidate every descendant's style cache. I agree with the first verifier that the finder's partial update_nodes([row, header, body]) fix would leave stale inherited styling. A safe fix needs a descendant notify_style_update walk without selector matching, or moving the accent off inherited properties. Risk is medium-high and it needs a snapshot test. Severity: per-keystroke cost of about 30 ms at 20 blocks and 50 ms at 40 blocks on this host (finder idle: 31.6 ms at 40, 109.6 ms at 120), scaling with user data. That meets P1 (per-keystroke ≳10-20 ms) but not P0: it only fires on explicit navigation, not continuously. Fix F1 first; F2's independent value is only the residual restyle. Known-task: TASK-26834 AC#2 (open umbrella: Console subtree restyles >100 ms; it does not name selection).
fix: Keep the root class but add it with update=False. Then restyle only the nodes that have selection-dependent rules: the row itself, its header, and the .console-markdown-body direct child. Call self.app.stylesheet.update_nodes([...]), not the whole Markdown block tree. Restyle the roleplay-block descendants only when presentation.transcript_style is IMMERSIVE_RP or the row has a roleplay class. Alternative: move the selection accent to a sibling or inline style (styles.border_left) for non-RP rows.
fix_notes: The proposed fix is UNSAFE as written. '.console-transcript-message-selected' sets inherited properties on the row root (color: $ds-focus-fg; text-style: bold underline), and every Markdown descendant inherits them. Textual's Widget.visual_style caches on the node's OWN styles._cache_key (widget.py:4168-4176). _visual_style_cache and _rich_style_cache are cleared only by notify_style_update (widget.py:4683), which Stylesheet.replace_rules calls during a restyle. Restyling only the row, header and .console-markdown-body would therefore leave descendant paragraphs rendering stale selected or unselected styling. A safe variant: after update=False plus a root/header/body restyle, walk the descendants and call notify_style_update() + refresh() without selector matching (restyle the roleplay rp-* nodes fully). Alternatively, move the selection accent off inherited properties. Needs a snapshot test of selected-row rendering. Risk: medium-high.

The residual cost scales with the Markdown block count, so the subtree restyle dominates, not the action-row mount. title: Whole-transcript O(n) walks run every 0.2 s tick regardless of the mounted window

title: TerminalViewport keeps a snapshot and frozen Text for every terminal session ever projected (never pruned)
trigger: Traced the chain: manager view update -> ConsoleTerminalWorkspace.project -> _apply_projection -> _project_selected -> TerminalViewport.project(session_id, snapshot), which stores state for the previous session id; _remember then stores it again for the current one. cost: Estimated, not measured. Each stale entry holds one TerminalScreenSnapshot plus one page-sized Text copy. The snapshot contains the screen lines plus scrollback, capped at 5000 lines or 4 MiB of accounted text, and Python object overhead roughly doubles that. Worst case is a few MB per closed heavy-output session, with growth linear in sessions closed during the ChatScreen's lifetime. A typical short session retains far less.
fix: In ConsoleTerminalWorkspace._apply_projection, drop _states keys not in view_state.sessions (a one-line dict comprehension).
fix_notes: A prune placed in _apply_projection BEFORE viewport.project() gets undone. project() at :162-172 first re-stores state for self._session_id, which is usually the session that was just closed, because closing the selected session makes the manager select another one. That write reinserts the stale key. So prune AFTER the viewport.project(...) call, or do it inside TerminalViewport: after the switch, drop keys not in the live id set. Also clear _session_id/_snapshot when selected is None, so the next project() does not re-save a dead session. Prune against view_state.sessions (all sessions), not visible_sessions: while unarmed, visible_sessions filters out live sessions whose state must survive re-arming. A related CPU note, outside this finding: a non-switching project() call, which runs once per terminal output frame, copies the rendered Text twice, once at :166-170 for the same session and again in _remember at :364. The first copy is redundant when session_id == self._session_id.
reason: The code exists as quoted in tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_terminal_workspace.py. _states is created at :153 and written at :163 (project) and :364 (_remember).
