title: File preview renders up to 200k characters in one Static on the event loop, re-wrapped on every resize
trigger: Yes. The Workspace Files modal file preview, and each resize while it is shown. This is a modal path.
cost: Measured with an isolated headless probe: a 197,689-character Static costs 287 ms CPU on first mount, and 211-260 ms per terminal resize (180x44, 211x44 and 160x40). That is at or above the finder's figures.
fix: Show the preview in a read-only TextArea, which renders only visible lines, or in a Log widget. Alternatively, cut the preview page to about 16-20k characters (the paging contract already exists), and keep 100k only for an explicit 'show more'.
fix_notes: TextArea(read_only=True, soft_wrap=True) still re-wraps the whole document on a width change (WrappedDocument), but renders only visible lines, so measure it before claiming a win. Log/RichLog with wrap off avoids re-wrapping. Lowering PAGED_TEXT_THRESHOLD or TEXT_PAGE_SIZE changes the inspector contract, and Tests/Workspaces/test_workspace_file_inspector.py:259-274 pins the 100_000 page size with literal asserts. A UI-side slice (about 16-20k characters per view, with a 'show more' that reuses the existing page offsets) avoids touching the inspector. Keep markup=False, or plain-text semantics, for safety.
evidence:
await viewer.mount(Static(result.text or self._state.status_copy, id='console-workspace-files-preview', markup=False))
# file_inspector: if total <= PAGED_TEXT_THRESHOLD (200_000): return whole text
#                else TEXT_PAGE_SIZE = 100_000 chars per page
reason: console_workspace_files_modal.py:861 mounts Static(result.text, markup=False) inside a VerticalScroll. file_inspector.py:39-40,966 returns the whole text when total <= PAGED_TEXT_THRESHOLD (200_000); larger files use 100_000-character pages via TEXT_PAGE_SIZE. METADATA_ONLY_BYTES is 8 MiB, so files up to that size reach the text path. Static content is wrapped as a whole for height and render, and is re-wrapped on every width change. The trigger is a file click (_request_file -> _publish_file -> _render_viewer), plus Previous/Next, Refresh and terminal or rail resizes while the preview is mounted. No task covers it.

title: Files modal attention line re-laid-out on every Console sync even when unchanged
trigger: Yes, but only while a Console run is active and the Files modal is open: 5 Hz via the transcript poll, plus every other Console sync.
cost: Measured with an isolated headless probe with 800 Button rows mounted: a same-text update with layout=True costs 27.0 ms median, layout=False 18.1 ms, and an idle pause 17.7 ms. That is about 9 ms extra reflow per push, roughly 4-5% of a core at 5 Hz, narrowly scoped.
fix: In update_attention, return early when attention == self._attention (it is a frozen dataclass), and/or call Static.update(..., layout=False), since the line has a fixed height.
fix_notes: Keep the generation bookkeeping, then skip Static.update when attention == self._attention. Also pass layout=False, which is safe given the fixed one-cell height in CSS. This is a one-line change and low risk.
evidence:
# workspace.py: every sync bumps the generation, so the push is always 'newer'
self._workspace_files_attention_generation += 1
modal.update_attention(self._workspace_files_attention_snapshot(), gen)
# modal:
if self.is_attached:
    self.query_one('#console-workspace-files-attention', Static).update(attention.status_copy)
reason: update_workspace_files_attention (workspace.py:1294-1307) bumps the generation on every call. It is called unconditionally at the end of ChatScreen._sync_console_workspace_context (chat_screen.py:14219), outside the state_changed gate, so it runs on every 5 Hz run tick while the modal is open. There is no is-current-screen guard in _sync_native_console_chat_ui. ConsoleWorkspaceFilesModal.update_attention (:395-412) always calls Static.update. Textual 8.2.8 Static.update re-visualizes and calls refresh(layout=True) (textual/widgets/_static.py:85-95). WorkspaceFilesAttention is a frozen dataclass (:136-144), so an equality early return is trivial. CSS (_console.tcss:1864-1871) pins #console-workspace-files-attention to height $ds-size-1 with overflow hidden, so layout=False is also safe.

title: Ingest queue panel is uncapped and fully recomposed (summary and every row) on every job transition
trigger: Every job lifecycle transition (submit, parsing, writing, done or failed, 3-4 per file) while Library > Import is the selected, unsuspended canvas. The listener is registered at library_screen.py:9517.
cost:
Harness: the real LibraryIngestQueuePanel fed by the real build_library_ingest_state, with the shipped tldw_cli_modular.tcss bundle, run headless at 211x44 (script: scratch/sl63-lens2/f1_panel.py). CPU calibration was 5.7-6.8 ms against ~6 ms on an idle core, so the CPU numbers are reliable even though machine load average was about 40-50.

Cost of one job transition (state build + panel recompose + layout/render, CPU), with the longest single loop block from a 1 ms ticker in brackets:
- 10 rows: 90 ms [59 ms]
- 20 rows: 154-172 ms [84-109 ms]
- 50 rows: 374 ms, of which the recompose is 230 ms [161 ms]
- 200 rows: 1.37-1.63 s [0.81-1.22 s]
- 500 rows: 3.8 s [4.2 s]

Without the CSS bundle, 50 rows cost 141 ms and 200 rows cost 728 ms, so the real bundle roughly doubles the cost. These figures are 2-4x worse than the finder's 68-114 ms at 50 jobs.

New evidence that makes it worse: the growth is not limited to one session.
- `_MAX_PERSISTED_INGEST_JOBS = 500` (app.py:2403), and `_apply_ingest_job_restore` calls `merge_restored` (app.py:3037), which re-seeds every persisted non-dismissed job into the visible queue at boot.
- `dismiss` accepts only FAILED/CANCELLED jobs (library_ingest_jobs.py:1499), so DONE rows persist until the user presses Clear finished.
- As a result, up to 500 rows carry across restarts. Every Import visit composes all of them (canvas.py:2078), and every later transition recomposes all of them.

The code path matches the first verifier's trace: library_screen.py:20529-20530 runs the two `refresh(recompose=True)` calls, the only early return is the non-Import row id, and the grouping collapses only FAILED/SKIPPED/CANCELLED rows (library_ingest_state.py:1457).

Why P1 and not P0: the rubric names import/export as a less-frequent path. This is still the top of P1, because the cost grows O(rows) per transition and the rows accumulate across sessions.
fix: Key queue rows by job_id and patch them in place: update a row's line and progress Static, mount only new job ids, remove dismissed ones. The progress listener already patches `#library-ingest-progress-{job_id}` in place (library_ingest_controller.py:1386), so that is the precedent. Bound the rendered rows (newest ~50 plus a 'N more' line) and skip the summary recompose when its state slice is unchanged.
fix_notes: Queue row Statics use index-keyed ids (`library-ingest-row-{index}`), and `jobs()` is newest-first, so every submit shifts every index. A keyed in-place patch must re-key rows by job_id first; the action buttons are already job_id-keyed. Collapse and expand of outcome groups changes structure, so keep a recompose fallback there. A cheaper first step shares the F2 coalescing: one repaint per loop turn or frame, plus a rendered-row bound with an 'N more' line. The in-place patch would also close TASK-31583's focus loss.
evidence:
# library_screen.py:_update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions (every registry notify)
summary.state = new_state
queue.state = new_state
summary.refresh(recompose=True)
queue.refresh(recompose=True)
# library_ingest_canvas.py compose: one row group per visible job, no cap
for group in group_ingest_queue_rows(state.queue_rows, expanded=self.expanded_groups):
reason: Code matches the pin. library_screen.py:20529-20530 run `summary.refresh(recompose=True); queue.refresh(recompose=True)` at the end of `_update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions`. The only early return is `_library_selected_row_id != LIBRARY_ROW_INGEST_MEDIA`, plus a structural-change branch that recomposes even more. `_handle_library_ingest_registry_changed` (library_ingest_controller.py:1135) calls it at :1218 whenever Import is the selected row and the screen is not suspended. The registry calls `_notify_listeners()` on submit, release_dispatch_hold, attach_remote and every mark_* method (library_ingest_jobs.py:743+). `LibraryIngestQueuePanel.compose` (library_ingest_canvas.py:556) loops `group_ingest_queue_rows(state.queue_rows, ...)` at ~603. `queue_rows` is built from every visible job in `build_library_ingest_state` (library_ingest_state.py:2929) with no cap. `_GROUPABLE_ROW_STATES` is only FAILED/SKIPPED/CANCELLED (:1457), so DONE rows each render a Static plus an actions Horizontal with buttons. Only telemetry-only progress changes are patched in place (controller :1386). No coalescing exists beyond Textual's per-turn recompose flag, and `mark_*` calls arrive through `call_from_thread` as separate loop turns, so each one pays a full panel recompose. No open task covers the perf side; TASK-31583 (To Do) covers only the focus loss from these same recomposes.

title: Folder-import submit is still O(N^2) on the loop through the Library screen's registry listener
trigger: Pressing Start on a folder in Library > Import, which is necessarily the visible canvas when Start is pressed, so the `_library_selected_row_id == LIBRARY_ROW_INGEST_MEDIA` gate passes on every per-file notify.
cost:
Benchmark: the real LibraryIngestJobRegistry with a listener that does exactly what the screen listener rebuilds on every submit (script: scratch/sl63-lens2/f2_bench.py and f2_bench_b.py). Per submit it runs jobs() (deepcopy of every job), library_ingest_analyze_skipped_ids, build_library_ingest_state, counts() and count_duplicate_done().

Thread-CPU totals for one folder submit loop:
- Empty ingest_options: 100 files 109 ms, 500 files 2.30 s, 1,000 files 9.38 s. This matches the first verifier's 2.03 s and 8.28 s.
- Realistic options snapshot (30 keys across 4 groups from get_capabilities, deep-copied per job per notify): 100 files 156 ms, 500 files 3.49 s, 1,000 files 14.7 s.
- NEW: 400 finished jobs already in the queue (history persists up to 500 across restarts, see F1) plus a 100-file folder: 0.91-1.38 s. So even a small folder freezes for about a second once the queue history is large.

Full trace, all synchronous on the UI thread:
1. Start runs `_submit_library_ingest_form` (controller:2329).
2. It calls `_do_submit_ingest` (library_screen.py:28783). Only the Parakeet external-dir branch detours to a thread worker, and that branch re-enters at :29075 on the UI thread.
3. `_enqueue_library_ingest_snapshot` (:29203) takes its own full `registry.jobs()` copy for prior_job_ids.
4. The folder loop at app.py:3233 calls `_submit_library_ingest_job_admitted` → `_submit_local_library_ingest_job` → `registry.submit`.
5. `submit` calls `_notify_listeners` synchronously (library_ingest_jobs.py:853/856).

The registry has exactly 4 add_listener sites: app.py:2586, app.py:4616, library_screen.py:9517 and Audio/meeting_owner.py:2007. The screen listener's gate always passes, because Start can only be pressed on the Import canvas.

TASK-32804.5 (In Progress) has AC#1 ('1,000-file submit does not block for more than a fraction of a second') ticked. That AC is false for every real UI folder submit: only the app-level listener was converted to iter_jobs_for_listeners.
fix: Coalesce registry notifications in the screen: the listener sets `_ingest_dirty = True` and schedules one `call_later(_flush_ingest_repaint)` if one is not already pending, so N submits in one handler cost one rebuild. Alternatively, add a `registry.batch()` context the folder loop enters, which notifies once at exit. Keep the done-count and settle-toast bookkeeping O(1) per notify.
fix_notes: A registry.batch() or suppress-notify context around the app.py folder loop, notifying once at exit, is the smallest root-cause fix and also covers the app-level listener. If coalescing in the screen instead, keep consent disarm, the clear-finished disarm and the done-count/settle-toast baseline per notify, or compute them once at flush from counts(); the toast baseline logic depends on seeing the 0->N active transition. `counts()` and `count_duplicate_done` are also O(N) per notify, so they stay O(N^2) with a small constant unless batched. Extend TASK-32804.5's AC#4 benchmark to run with the Library screen listener attached.
evidence:
# app.py folder loop (UI thread): one registry.submit -> _notify_listeners per file
for expanded_path in expanded:
    job = self._submit_library_ingest_job_admitted(...)
# Library listener, synchronous per notify while Import is visible:
self._update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions()  # -> _build_library_ingest_state()
jobs = jobs_fn()   # registry.jobs(): _copy_job for ALL jobs, then rows for all
reason: Traced the chain end to end. Start / Enter runs `_submit_library_ingest_form` (controller :2329, synchronous UI handler), then `_do_submit_ingest` (library_screen.py:28783), then `_enqueue_library_ingest_snapshot`, then `app.submit_library_ingest_job`. For a folder it loops `for expanded_path in expanded:` at app.py:3233-3234 on the UI thread. `_submit_library_ingest_job_admitted` → `_submit_local_library_ingest_job` → `registry.submit` → `_notify_listeners` synchronously. The Library listener (registered at library_screen.py:9517) runs `_update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions` (:1218) → `_build_library_ingest_state` (library_screen.py:20598). That calls `registry.jobs()` (a deepcopy-based `_copy_job` of every visible job, library_ingest_jobs.py:1592-1607), then `build_library_ingest_state`, which builds every row, the groups, the counts and the analyze-skipped ids. TASK-32804.5 (In Progress, AC#1 ticked) changed only the app-level listener to `iter_jobs_for_listeners`; the screen listener still copies and rebuilds everything per submit.

title: Folder Files polls a full reconcile every 1.5 s, re-renders even when nothing changed, and keeps polling while hidden
trigger: The 1.5 s timer while the Library screen is top of stack and the workspace is mounted: in Folder Files mode, and also after returning to Database Notes, where the workspace stays mounted with display=False.
cost:
Harness: the real LibraryFileNotesWorkspace, headless with the shipped CSS bundle at 211x44 (210 screen nodes), pointed at a scratch folder with a scratch replica (script: scratch/sl63-lens2/f35_ws.py). A counting wrapper on Screen._refresh_layout counts screen layouts.

- **Worker-thread reconcile with nothing changed:** 46.9 ms at 30 files, 74.1 ms at 1,000 files, every 1.5 s tick. It is Python-heavy, so it contends for the GIL.
- **Loop side per unchanged tick:** 41.8-42.7 ms of main-thread CPU and 2 screen layouts. With `_render_projection` stubbed (the finder's fix b) it drops to 14.1-14.2 ms and 0 layouts, so the no-change re-render alone costs about 28 ms plus 2 layouts per tick.
- **With the file search 'note' active:** 51-58 ms per tick, about 37-43 ms of it re-render.
- **Hidden-gate gap confirmed live:** with workspace.display=False and the screen active, `_start_poll()` launched the reconcile worker.

Total is roughly (28 + 47..74) ms per 1.5 s, about 5-7% of a core (about 2% of it on the loop). It runs whenever the user sits in Library > Notes: in Folder Files, or in Database Notes after visiting Folder Files. The retained-switch path at library_screen.py:22065 only sets display=False, and nothing clears `_active`.

Scope bound, which is why this is not P0: `on_unmount` (workspace:2389-2415) stops the timer when the Notes canvas is swapped for another Library canvas (library_screen.py:11931 host), and TASK-22219's `screen.is_active` gate stops it off-screen. So this is not an always-on app-wide tax. It is a per-tick cost ≳20 ms on a timer, which is P1.
fix: (a) Skip the tick when hidden: add `or not self.display` (or `not self.is_on_screen`) to `_start_poll`'s gate. (b) Skip `_render_projection` when the reconcile has no created, modified or deleted paths and the deleted set is equal. (c) Re-run the active search only when entries changed. (d) Optional: short-circuit the walk when directory mtimes are unchanged since the last tick, or back off the cadence while idle.
fix_notes: Gate on the workspace's own visibility (`not self.display`), not `is_on_screen`, which is False when merely scrolled out. Keep the timer ticking so the first visible tick is the catch-up, matching TASK-22219's design. When skipping `_render_projection` on an unchanged reconcile, still run `_handle_open_external_change`, which is harmless because it acts only on modified or deleted paths. Check whether anything relies on the poll to refresh `_refresh_session_changes` or the push state (`_rehydrate_push_state`); owner-side changes from autosave or git may currently surface only through this tick.
evidence:
self._poll_timer = self.set_interval(self._poll_interval, self._start_poll)  # 1.5 s
# _start_poll gates on _active/is_attached/screen.is_active -- NOT on self.display
result = await asyncio.to_thread(service.reconcile)   # os.walk + 2 lstat/file
# _render_projection runs every tick, even when rebuild_tree is False:
self._update_root_surface(...); self._refresh_active_search()
self._refresh_session_changes(); self._update_controls()
# library_screen.py:22068 leaving Folder Files: workspace.display = False (stays mounted)
reason: library_file_notes_workspace.py:2376 arms `set_interval(self._poll_interval, self._start_poll, pause=False)` in on_mount, with a default poll_interval of 1.5 s (:1248). The production factory at library_screen.py:2384 passes no override. `_start_poll` (:6249) gates on `_active`, `is_attached`, `screen.is_active`, the two transition flags, the service and an in-flight worker, but not on the widget's own display. `_return_to_library_database_notes` (library_screen.py:~22065) only sets `workspace.display = False`. Nothing in `_set_library_notes_source` (library_notes_controller.py:2482) deactivates the workspace, so `_active` stays True. `refresh_files` (:6163) runs `to_thread(service.reconcile)` plus `to_thread(replica.list_deleted)`, then `_apply_reconcile` → `_render_projection` (:2779). That runs `_update_root_surface`, `_refresh_active_search` (restarts a search worker and `_rebuild_search_results` whenever the search box is non-empty), `_refresh_session_changes` and `_update_controls` on every tick; only `_rebuild_tree` is gated on change. TASK-22219 (Done) added only the screen-level gate and explicitly kept the fixed cadence; the hidden-within-screen case and the no-change re-render are new scope.

title: Each file-notes service call (every poll tick, every autosave) re-runs Backup_Recovery storage admission, ~1,000 directory-fd opens
trigger: Every Folder Files poll tick through `refresh_files` → `to_thread(service.reconcile)`, plus each `open_file` and scan. Not triggered by autosave.
cost: Measured in an isolated scratch profile set up like Tests/Backup_Recovery/test_activation_notes.py in the 'ordinary' state (profile authority registered, 30-file folder, file-backed replica): wrapped `reconcile()` 37.6 ms vs `reconcile.__wrapped__` 7.6 ms, with 1,629 vs 261 `os.open` calls per call. Admission is ~80% of the call, confirming the finder's ratio. The scratch config path has 13 components; a real ~/.config/tldw_cli profile has ~5, and the pinned-directory opens scale with depth, so real overhead is plausibly ~10-20 ms per tick. It runs on a worker thread every 1.5 s, roughly 1% of a core plus GIL contention while Folder Files is active.
fix: Hoist admission out of the read-only reconcile path. Take it only when the reconcile will write (non-empty created, modified or deleted), or cache the verified admission per service or binding with invalidation on the recovery-registry generation. Coordinate with the Notes/Backup_Recovery slice owner.
fix_notes: High-care fix. This is a security and recovery admission whose docstring requires the scope to be retained inside the worker through the effect. Taking admission only when the reconcile will write turns walk-then-write into walk, admit, re-validate, and must re-check under admission to avoid a TOCTOU against a restore. Any cache must invalidate on the recovery-registry generation, the effective config path, and lease or pause state. Cheaper and safer: fix F3 so fewer reconciles run, or back off the idle cadence. Needs sign-off from the Backup_Recovery owner. Drop the autosave claim from the finding.
evidence:
# cProfile, 10 x reconcile() on a 30-file folder (0.70 s total):
#  20 _replica_execution_scope        cum 0.564 s
#  50 storage_admission.acquire_storage cum 0.516 s
# 1400 bootstrap.pinned_directory      cum 0.366 s
# 10130 private_paths._native_open     cum 0.278 s
#  10 recovery_review.require_pairing  cum 0.272 s
reason: `_serialized` (file_notes_service.py:60) wraps only `scan`, `open_file` and `reconcile` (:71) in `_replica_execution_scope` (:253). That runs two `execution_scope` calls (Backup_Recovery/activation.py:181, each with `acquire_storage`, `execution_context` and `activation_permission`) plus `require_pairing` on every call. The finder's claim that every autosave goes through it is wrong: `save_file`, `create_file` and `move_file` are `@_serialized` but take only the maintenance operation and the lock, not the admission scope. The real triggers are the 1.5 s reconcile poll (F3) and file opens and scans. No open task covers it.

title: Every Folder Files editor keystroke re-derives the whole control surface and forces a screen layout
trigger: Every character typed in the Folder Files editor (#file-notes-editor) when a file is open, editable and not in conflict.
cost:
Same workspace harness (f35_ws.py): opened dir0/note_0001.md (editable), focused #file-notes-editor, and pressed 'a' 20 times through the pilot. Save state was already 'dirty' and no delete confirmation was armed, so nothing visible changes after the first key.

| Handler | Main-thread CPU per key | Screen layouts |
|---|---|---|
| Real `_editor_changed` | 43-48 ms (median over 2 runs, 30 and 1,000-file roots) | 20-21 per 20 keys |
| Reduced to `_arm_autosave` only (the proposed early return) | 22-23 ms | 0 per 20 keys |

That puts about 22-24 ms of each keystroke on this handler plus one full screen layout per key. Timed parts of that:
- `_set_save_state('dirty')`: 7.5-8.1 ms. It runs `_render_status_channels` and `_update_controls` even though the state is unchanged.
- `_set_delete_confirmation()`: 3.2-3.3 ms (explicit `refresh(layout=True)` on delete and toolbar, plus `_schedule_editor_action_layout`).
- The rest is the forced screen layout.

This was measured on an isolated 210-node screen. The real Library screen mounts more widgets, so the per-key layout there is larger. Per keystroke that is above the P1 threshold. No open task covers it: TASK-32804.11 is about DB Notes and the git-panel probe.
fix: Early-return in `_editor_changed` when `self._save_state == "dirty" and not self._delete_confirmation_path`, doing only `_arm_autosave()`. Make `_set_delete_confirmation` a no-op when the path is unchanged, and make `set_mutating` return early when `active` is unchanged and there is no detail. Optionally cache the coalesced session-change count by change-log length.
fix_notes: The early-return guard must be `self._save_state == 'dirty' and self._save_detail == '' and not self._delete_confirmation_path`. `_set_save_state('dirty')` with an empty detail also clears a prior 'save interrupted' detail and resets `_conflict_resolution_active`, so the first keystroke after any other state must still take the full path. Make `_set_delete_confirmation` a no-op when the path is unchanged, and never skip `_schedule_editor_action_layout` when the label actually changes.
reason: `_editor_changed` (library_file_notes_workspace.py:6504) runs its three calls unconditionally on every TextArea.Changed that passes the guards. `_set_delete_confirmation()` (:3241) reassigns the label and calls `delete.refresh(layout=True)` and `toolbar.refresh(layout=True)`, then `_schedule_editor_action_layout` (:3226). That runs `_apply_editor_action_layout` synchronously and, when not already scheduled, `self.refresh(layout=True)` plus `call_later`. `_set_save_state('dirty')` (:5186) always runs two set_class calls, `_render_status_channels` (`_ensure_repository_probe`, `_status_channels` with session-change coalescing, 3 query_one) and `_update_controls` (:5396, ~20 query_one/query calls in its body plus the git panel `set_mutating` → `_update_actions` at git_panel.py:3057), even when the state is already 'dirty'. No short-circuit exists. TASK-32804.11 covers the DB Notes canvas and the git panel arrow-key probe, not this handler.

title: Conversation reader progressive load is O(N^2): every page or continuation sync re-updates every mounted message
trigger: Opening any conversation in Library > Conversations (progressive paged load), then every reader sync: mode toggle, find submit, select-mode row toggles.
cost:
Harness: the real LibraryConversationReader with the shipped CSS at 211x44, driven like the controller's `_load_library_conversation_reader` (script: scratch/sl63-lens2/f6_bench2.py). Each 20-message page runs sync_state, then sleep(0), then a simulated off-loop page read of 3 ms (a to_thread SQLite read). Messages are ~370 chars. Static.update calls on message rows are counted.

**Cost stands, mechanism needs correcting.** The claimed O(N^2) row.update storm is mostly coalesced away in practice:
- The controller never awaits `_sync_messages`, and each queued sync returns early unless its generation is current.
- Row updates during the load were only 20 / 220 / 240 at 100 / 400 / 1,000 messages, not the finder's 221 / 3,881 / 24,701.
- With slower page reads they rise, but only to 560 (30 ms reads) and 1,020 (150 ms reads) at 1,000 messages.

**The real load cost is the one-awaited-mount-per-row loop.** Progressive load CPU (wall in brackets):
- 100 messages: 352 ms [0.66 s]
- 400 messages: 1.65 s [2.4 s]
- 1,000 messages: 4.67 s [5.9 s]

The longest single loop block during the load was 83-155 ms, because the loop yields between mounts. Fix attribution:
- Skipping unchanged rows alone: 237 ms / 954 ms / 3.84 s.
- Skipping unchanged rows plus `mount_all`: 116 ms / 439 ms / 1.70 s.

**Header-only resyncs are real per-interaction loop blocks.** These are Read/Info toggle, find submit, and every select-mode row click (library_screen.py:22729 calls `_sync_library_conversation_reader`). Each one re-updates every retained row synchronously:
- CPU: 36 / 94 / 212 ms at 100 / 400 / 1,000 messages.
- Longest single block: 32 / 76 / 183 ms.
- With unchanged rows skipped: 12 / 19 / 138 ms blocks.

Fix priority should be `mount_all` for new rows, plus skipping `_sync_messages` on header-only syncs or skipping unchanged rows. A per-row revision check alone would not fix the load. Severity stays P1: the per-click cost is 32-76 ms at typical 100-400 message conversations, and the load grows superlinearly on a Library visit path.
fix: Track the rendered (revision, text length) per message_id and call `row.update` only when it changed. Mount all new rows with a single `mount_all`. Schedule `_sync_messages` only when `state.messages` changed by identity, not on header-only syncs such as mode, bulk or find. Longer term, window or virtualize the transcript, as `VirtualizedRawContent` does for media.
fix_notes: `_message_copy` embeds a relative age computed from `datetime.now()`, so today's unconditional re-update also refreshes the '27m'/'2d' labels. Skipping unchanged rows freezes those ages until content changes; accept that or refresh ages on a coarse timer. Add a generation check inside the mount/update loop so a superseded sync stops early, and use `mount_all` for new rows.

title: Every autosave triggers a full Folder Files navigator rebuild on the next poll tick
trigger: Type in the Folder Files editor. The autosave timer (2.0 s) calls service.save_file, which changes mtime, size and hash. The next 1.5 s poll tick runs refresh_files -> _apply_reconcile (navigator_changed=True) -> _render_projection(rebuild_tree=True) -> _rebuild_tree on the event loop. External edits to any file under the root trigger it too.
cost: Not re-measured. The finder measured 1.5 ms sync per rebuild. From the code, the deferred cost is one call_later per expanded folder, each materialising up to 100 Tree nodes, plus a Tree layout pass. The cursor reset every autosave is a real UX side effect.

fix_notes: The fix is safe: base `rebuild_tree` on `new_entries.keys() != self._entries.keys() or deleted != self._deleted_paths`, and keep storing the full entries, because `_handle_open_external_change` reads `entry.content_hash`. Extra scope in the same function: `_render_projection` calls `_refresh_active_search()` on EVERY successful poll whether anything changed or not. With a search query active, every 1.5 s tick starts a replica search thread and `results.reset()` the search-results Tree, losing its cursor even when no file changed. Gate that on navigator_changed as well.
reason: The code matches the pin. `_apply_reconcile` (library_file_notes_workspace.py:2809-2823) sets `navigator_changed = new_entries != self._entries or ...`. `FileNoteEntry` (Notes/file_notes_service.py:95) is a frozen dataclass with size, mtime_ns, content_hash and editable, so any content change makes the dicts unequal. `_save_draft` updates only `self._opened` and never updates `self._entries` (the only writers of `_entries` are :2770 and :2818). Every autosave therefore changes the next reconcile's entry and forces `_rebuild_tree`. The poll is `set_interval(1.5s) -> _start_poll -> run_worker(refresh_files(), exclusive=True)`. `service.reconcile` runs off the loop through `asyncio.to_thread`, but `_apply_reconcile -> _render_projection -> _rebuild_tree` runs on the loop. The resume path at :2525 uses the same function. `_rebuild_tree` (:3380) calls `tree.reset()`, re-adds up to FILE_TREE_BATCH_SIZE=100 rows, and schedules one `call_later(_restore_folder_expansion)` per remembered expanded folder. The labels come only from `_build_folder_index(tuple(self._entries))`, which reads keys only, plus `_deleted_paths`. The tree never shows size, mtime, hash or editable, so the rebuild is pure waste. `tree.reset` also drops the navigator cursor about every 2 s while the user types. No backlog task covers this: I grepped for _rebuild_tree, navigator_changed, file-notes-poll and _apply_reconcile. P2 is right: it fires on every autosave in Folder Files mode, the cost is small for typical folders and grows with the number of expanded folders.

cost:

It mounts the REAL PersonasInspectorPane and PersonasLibraryPane (248 widgets on screen) in ConsolidatedCSSApp with the production bundle tldw_cli_modular.tcss, driven by the REAL PersonasConversationsController. - Placeholder swap from 21 rows to 1: 9.3 ms of mutation, 18.1 ms including render.
- Result render from 1 row to 21: 35.1 ms of mutation, 66.5 ms including render.

End-to-end typing of 'dragon castle' (13 keystrokes via Input.value, not blocking on pilot):
- 120 ms gap: undebounced runs 13 thread workers, 13 ensure_keyword_index BEGIN IMMEDIATE txns and 13 page applies. Loop-thread CPU is 603 ms (46 ms per keystroke), max loop stall 124 ms. Debounced runs 1/1/1, 196 ms (15 ms per keystroke), max stall 20 ms.
- 60 ms gap: undebounced is 50 ms per keystroke with a max stall of 141 ms; debounced is 16 ms per keystroke with 26 ms.
- CPU across all threads: 3.1 s (120 ms gap) and 11.2 s (60 ms gap) undebounced, versus 0.65 s and 0.73 s debounced. Superseded workers are not cancellable and read self._conversation_query live, so late threads all re-run the newest and most expensive phrase. GIL contention from those threads also inflates the loop stalls.

DB costs off the loop: steady-state ensure_keyword_index (READY) 4.6 ms; read-only keyword_index_status 4.3 ms; keyword_search 21-87 ms per partial query. The synthetic corpus makes the full phrase pathological (453 ms), so treat the absolute thread CPU as corpus-dependent. The xN multiplier is not.

The trigger is confirmed exactly as the first verifier traced it, and no open task covers it; the only backlog hits (task-2084, task-445) are Done UX tasks.

Not P0: stalls exceed 100 ms only under fast typing, and this is a niche Personas inspector search box, not a common path. About 30-35 ms of extra loop CPU per keystroke is squarely P1. Debounce alone cut loop CPU per keystroke by about 3x and worker/txn count 13x, which confirms the fix direction.
fix: (1) Debounce ConversationSearchChanged the way the library search is debounced: a set_timer(PERSONAS_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS) in the screen handler, or a widget-level timer like the pickers. (2) Call ensure_keyword_index once per character selection or first non-empty query, and use the read-only keyword_index_status() on later queries. (3) Skip the loading-placeholder rebuild when rows are already visible (just swap the tail text). (4) Longer term, render rows through OptionList or recycled ListItems (shared with F2).
fix_notes: (1) Debounce alone captures most of the win: reuse the PERSONAS_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS set_timer shape from :4068 and cancel it in _cancel_search_debounce or on character change. (2) Be careful about calling ensure_keyword_index only once. It also folds the dirty ledger and repairs a stale or failed generation for the current source revision. Using keyword_index_status afterwards would miss conversations created while the box is open (keyword_search revalidates existing candidates but cannot add new ones). A cheaper safe variant: skip ensure only when keyword_index_status() reports READY for the current revision. (3) Skipping the placeholder rebuild when rows are visible is safe via the existing _replace_conversation_tail path. (4) An OptionList conversion must preserve the ListView.Selected tail-action semantics and focus_conversation.

title: Change Review snapshot runs an O(index entries x depth) double-stat ancestor walk (_nested_owner) for every staged file, twice per agent turn
trigger: Every agent turn in a workspace with Change Review capability and consent enabled, twice per turn per admitted root, on the finalization coordinator worker (off-loop). The baseline half is on the critical path of the 3 s first-mutating-tool gate. A fast local model that emits a tool call within ~1 s waits on it, and a timeout invalidates the turn's review. The realistic ceiling is DEFAULT_MAX_FILES=20,000, because discover_baseline marks larger roots over budget and skips them.
cost: Benchmark: scratch/sl67-lens2/bench_f3.py. It calls the real ShadowRepo._nested_owner (an instance built via object.__new__ with root set) over this repo's real `git ls-files` output: 24,212 entries, average depth 3.12, 1,151 dirs. For comparison it runs a per-directory memo (string rpartition to the parent plus one os.path.lexists(dir/.git) per directory); the owner maps were asserted identical. Load avg ~44. Current code: min 5,609 ms per snapshot for 24,212 entries, and min 4,292 ms (median 5,785) at the 20,000 DEFAULT_MAX_FILES cap. Memo: 8.3 ms and 5.2 ms. The finder saw 1,091 ms and the verifier 1,716 ms on a less-loaded machine. The loop covers ALL stage_entries (change_tracking.py:507-515), not only new ones, and does 2 stats per ancestor with no memo (:446-458). It runs for both the B ('turn baseline', change_turn_tracker.py:295/299) and E snapshots of every Change Review turn per admitted root. B gates the first mutating tool through await_baseline(CHANGE_REVIEW_BASELINE_WAIT_SECONDS=3.0) (console_agent_bridge.py:324/372). Under load the Python loop alone at the 20k cap (4.3 s) exceeds that 3 s gate, before git add -A, ls-files and ls-tree run, so the baseline times out and the turn loses its review. Trigger scope: the global capability defaults True (change_bounds.py:44), but per-workspace consent defaults DISABLED (a missing row is disabled, registry_service.py:~3207), so the feature is opt-in. Once enabled it runs on every agent turn. The work is off-loop but holds the GIL through the pathlib portion. Kept at P1 as per-turn cost that scales with user data and sits on the critical path of tool dispatch. The memo is the safe fix (100-700x); reusing scan_root's nested_repos is not semantically equivalent, as the verifier noted.

Better still, reuse scan_root's already-computed nested_repos set: the owner is the nearest ancestor prefix in that set, a pure string operation with no syscalls. Only entries that are new or whose directory is a candidate need the check.
fix_notes: The per-directory memo (os.path.lexists(dir/'.git'), recursing to the parent) keeps the exact semantics and is the safe choice. Reusing scan_root's nested_repos is not exactly equivalent. scan_root prunes _SKIP_DIR_NAMES before descending, so a nested repo under a skipped dir is not in nested_repos, while _nested_owner would still find it for an index entry there. Also, the scan and the index read happen at different moments. Use the memo, or fall back to it for prefixes the scan never visited.

title: Environment local tier spawns ~10 git processes (~0.5 s CPU) and re-stats every backlog task file every 10 s while the Inspect rail is open
trigger: Every 10 s while the Console is the active screen, the Inspect rail is open and the workspace root is a git repo. The rail state persists, so this runs indefinitely while the user sits idle with the rail open. Off-loop (thread worker plus child processes); the landing is on the UI thread.
cost: Benchmark: scratch/sl67-lens2/bench_f4.py. It calls the real gather_git_env and BacklogTaskScanner.scan on the audit tree. It is read-only: _user_git_env itself pins GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0. Machine load avg ~44. The audit tree has a detached HEAD, so a tick makes 8 spawns: rev-parse --show-toplevel 28 ms, symbolic-ref 51, rev-parse --verify 54, remote -v 74, status --porcelain=v1 -uall 149, diff HEAD --numstat 49, rev-parse --short HEAD 28, rev-parse --git-dir/--git-common-dir 26. Total per tick: 388-475 ms wall and 460-489 ms child CPU. A branch with an upstream adds @{upstream} (27 ms), for-each-ref (34 ms) and rev-list --left-right --count (36 ms), which gives the finding's 10 spawns. Warm BacklogTaskScanner.scan (4,478 task files, 950 entries) took 51-68 ms of GIL-holding Python per tick; cold took 1,619 ms, which is TASK-31628's subject. That totals ~0.5 s CPU per 10 s tick, ~5% of a core. Trigger confirmed: set_interval(10.0, _poll_console_environment) (chat_screen.py:825/16944) -> poll_tick requires rail_open_accessor = active Console screen and #console-right-rail displayed (chat_screen.py:8524-8527), then _dispatch_local runs run_worker(job, thread=True) each tick with no change detection. The right rail defaults closed (CONSOLE_RAIL_RIGHT_DEFAULT_OPEN=False, console_rail_state.py:14), but right_open is a persisted preference. That makes the cost a persistent tax while the rail is open, not an always-on one, so P1 (per-tick timer) rather than P0. The scanner half applies only to roots that contain backlog/tasks; the git half applies to any git-root workspace. The verifier's correction stands: do not skip numstat on an unchanged porcelain line plus index mtime; key the skip on the listed paths' (mtime, size).

Cache toplevel, remote -v and worktree name per root, keyed on the .git/HEAD and config mtimes. Skip `diff --numstat` when the status payload and index mtime are unchanged since the last tick. In the scanner, return the previous TasksEnvState object when no (mtime, size) signature changed, and have _land skip _on_snapshot when the snapshot is equal. TASK-31628 (cold scan per visit) is related but separate.

Skipping `diff --numstat` when the status payload and index mtime are unchanged would serve stale +/- counts: editing an already-modified tracked file keeps the same ' M path' porcelain line and does not touch the index. Key any numstat skip on the (mtime, size) of the paths the status lists instead. porcelain=v2 --branch replaces symbolic-ref, verify, @{upstream} and rev-list, but not remote -v, remotename or the toplevel check; cache those per root keyed on .git/HEAD and config mtimes. Returning the previous TasksEnvState on an unchanged signature, and skipping _on_snapshot on an equal snapshot, are safe.

title: Each Change Review turn walks the root three times in Python, re-spawns 7 git config pins per snapshot and re-acquires storage admission for every git command
trigger: Every Change Review-enabled agent turn, per root, on the coordinator worker (off-loop). The B snapshot is on the 3 s first-mutating-tool gate path.
cost: Not re-measured. Using the finder's figures (scan_root 168 ms vs 69 ms scandir at 24k files; ~10 ms per config spawn; ~2.7 ms per admission, which matches F2's measured per-acquire cost), the estimate of ~0.3 s avoidable per large-root snapshot is plausible. Estimated.

Write the config pins only on init, or when one `git config --list` read differs. Have _run skip acquire_storage when snapshot() already holds it (pass a flag or use a thread-local held marker).
fix_notes: Reusing discover's RootScan for B is only valid when it was not over budget. discover uses max_files=20k and returns early, while B uses sys.maxsize. The scan is also taken moments earlier, so a file that grows past max_file_bytes in between would be staged; that is acceptable, but note it. Keep the config self-heal by comparing one `git config --list` read, not by writing only on init. The _run admission skip needs a thread-local 'held for this git_dir' marker set by snapshot(); do not pass a boolean bypass, because acquire_storage's docstring forbids boolean bypasses ('never a boolean bypass here').

scan = scan_root(self.root, max_files=_sys.maxsize, ...)  # again in EVERY snapshot (B and E)
for key, value in pins: self._run("config", key, value)  # 7 spawns per snapshot
def _run(...): with acquire_storage(self.git_dir): subprocess.run(...)  # admission per git cmd
# scan_root: os.walk + Path(dirpath)/name + is_symlink() + stat() per file

No open task covers it.

title: Change Review consent workers and finalization publisher poll forever (~80 wakeups/s) once first used
trigger: Starts on the first Change Review scheduling (a send or binding add in an enabled workspace) or the first reservation. It then persists for the whole session, including idle: ~2x20 + 40 = ~80 wakeups/s.
cost: Finder's replica measured 0.137% of a core idle; not re-measured. That is far below the 1% P0 threshold, but it is a permanent 80 Hz idle-wakeup and battery tax for the rest of the session once used. P2 is on the high side of fair; P3 would also be defensible.

Do not rely on put_nowait. The publisher's timed alternation is deliberate: the comment describes a 'bounded scheduling quantum' for the regular lane. A single Condition over both lanes must keep that preference or fairness, or it reintroduces the direct-lane starvation the comment fixed.

    try: work = self._queue.get(timeout=0.05)   # x2 workers
    except Empty: continue
...

title: Retention runs reflog expire + gc --prune=now on every live shadow repo on every launch, even when nothing was pruned
trigger: Yes, but off-loop: once per launch at about 65 s after start, then every 24 h, via asyncio.to_thread (app.py:19010-19016, 19080).
cost: Measured: a no-op gc on an already-packed repo takes 70-170 ms of background CPU per live root. The expensive gc (about 2.6 s on 41-96 MB of loose objects) only happens when there is real packing to do, and that packing is needed.
fix: Skip reflog/gc for a root when this pass deleted no rows for it, or persist a last-gc timestamp and gc at most weekly, or use `gc --auto`.
fix_notes: The proposed fix is harmful. Skipping gc when no rows were pruned would let loose objects pile up without limit, because gc.auto=0, and every later git operation would slow down. `gc --auto` is a no-op under the pinned gc.auto=0 unless it runs as `git -c gc.auto=N gc --auto`. If anything is worth doing, it is that (gc only past a loose-object threshold), or a `count-objects` check first. Neither is worth doing for about 0.15 s of background work per launch.
evidence:
repo._run("reflog", "expire", "--expire=now", "--all", check=False)
repo._run("gc", "--prune=now", "--quiet", check=False)
# scheduled: set_timer(DEFERRED_MEDIA_CLEANUP_DELAY_SECONDS + 60) + set_interval(24h)
reason: The code exists as quoted: change_retention.py:168-173 runs reflog expire and gc --prune=now for each live root. app.py:19010-19016 schedules it with set_timer(5+60 s) plus set_interval(24 h), and _perform_change_review_retention (app.py:19061) offloads it with asyncio.to_thread, so it never runs on the event loop. The premise is wrong, though. change_tracking.py:19/376 pins gc.auto=0 on every shadow repo ('GC is scheduled by retention, never mid-turn'), so this pass is the ONLY thing that ever packs the loose objects that snapshots (git add/commit) and revert staging write. Row pruning cannot free objects in a live repo anyway, because ancestry keeps every snapshot reachable (module docstring lines 8-13). So gating gc on rows_pruned is unrelated to whether gc has work to do. I measured the cost in scratch repos. The first gc of a repo with loose objects took 2.6-2.7 s, and that is necessary work. A repeat gc on an already-packed repo took 0.07 s (10k files, 1.8 MB pack) and 0.15-0.17 s (5k incompressible files, 96 MB pack). reflog expire took 0.01 s. So a 'no-op' launch wastes about 0.1-0.2 s of background CPU per live root, once per launch, off-thread. Repo size is also capped by change_bounds (20k files / 2 GB per root).

title: Revert preflight spawns one `git show` (plus an admission handshake) per path and runs twice per Undo

That compares without reading any blob contents. disk_state still needs sha256 of the disk bytes. Keep the second revalidation preflight, since it guards against a stale confirmation; only make it cheaper. The per-path `git checkout` in revert_paths could be batched too, but that changes the per-path failure semantics, so leave it.

title: Workspace file filter re-walks the whole tree per debounced keystroke and re-opens root plus every path component for each directory
trigger: Yes. The files-modal filter Input.Changed (console_workspace_files_modal.py:1076-1083) fires after a 150 ms debounce and runs via asyncio.to_thread in the filter lane (:217, :721). Superseded walks are cooperatively cancelled per entry, and the settled query runs a full walk capped at 50k entries.
cost: Measured on a 46.8k-entry synthetic tree: the full walk takes 602-661 ms, of which the per-directory root re-open is 297 ms. A query truncated at 500 matches takes about 67-72 ms. This is off-loop worker time and delays results rather than freezing the UI.
fix: When the new query extends the previous one, filter the previous matches instead of re-walking. Walk with a parent-fd stack (openat relative to the parent fd) instead of re-resolving from the root.
fix_notes: Do NOT keep an open fd for every entry on the `pending` list. On wide trees that list holds thousands of directories and would hit EMFILE. Use a depth-first stack of (fd, scandir iterator), so open fds are bounded by depth, and open each child with openat(name, O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, dir_fd=parent_fd). The per-directory root re-open is a deliberate binding-swap re-check against root dev/ino, so keep one root revalidation per walk, or re-check periodically. Refining from the previous query's matches is only valid when the prior result was COMPLETE (not TRUNCATED at 500 or PARTIAL at 50k visits) and the new casefolded needle contains the old one. It also serves stale results if files change between keystrokes. Separately, time-throttle on_progress (for example every 100 ms or 1000 entries) so the walk does not keep the event loop repainting the status line.
evidence:
while pending:
    parent_parts = pending.pop()
    root_fd, error_code = _open_root_descriptor(current)
    directory_fd, ... = _open_target_descriptor(root_fd, parent_parts, "dir")  # openat per component
reason: The code matches. filter_paths (file_inspector.py:437-499) pops each pending directory, calls _open_root_descriptor (open+fstat of the root, :443), and then _open_target_descriptor, which dups the fd and runs openat for EVERY path component plus an fstat (:857-894). Every directory is re-resolved from the root. The caller is ConsoleWorkspaceFilesModal: Input.Changed at :1083 sets a 150 ms timer, then _request_filter submits to the latest-only _OperationLane, which runs the walk in asyncio.to_thread (:217). The finder missed that is_cancelled checks `generation != self._generation`, so a superseded walk stops at its next entry. Wasted work is therefore bounded by the gap between keystrokes, and only the settled query walks the whole tree. That part of the claim is overstated. I benchmarked the real filter_paths on a synthetic 46.8k-entry tree (4681 dirs, depth <= 5) with only _revalidate stubbed. A full no-match walk took 602-661 ms, and the per-directory root re-open alone took 297 ms, about 45-50% of the walk. That is avoidable latency on each settled query in a modal, it scales with tree size, and it holds the GIL for the Python-side work. So P2, not P3. A related cost: on_progress fires per entry, and the coalesced _FilterProgressReady is re-posted as soon as the UI drains the previous one. That keeps the event loop running Static.update continuously for the whole walk.

title: Server mode: the first TLDWAPIClient construction imports client.py plus 51 schema modules (about 420 ms) on the event loop, 0.1 s after first paint
trigger: Server-mode boot: after first paint, a 0.1 s set_timer runs a sync callback on the loop: `_deferred_wire_collections_capture_services`, then `_activate_collections_capture_authority`, then `provider.build_client()`, then a function-local import of tldw_api.client. Each run is a fresh process with warm .pyc; the script times `import tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client` in three realistic pre-states, 6 interleaved rounds each (18 runs).

The finder's 396-437 ms wall on a quieter machine is a credible lower bound. Construction alone is `TLDWAPIClient(...)`, 0.01 ms, and the httpx client is created lazily, so the entire cost is the import.

- The only non-TYPE_CHECKING routes to client.py are the function-local import at runtime_policy/bootstrap.py:195 (reached from server_context.py:334 `build_client`) and app.py:10920-10929 (unified-MCP factory, also on first use).
- The only module-scope `TLDWAPIClient` importers, Sharing/server_sharing_service.py:8 and WebClipper/server_web_clipper_service.py:8, are imported only by their own package __init__, and those packages have 0 production importers.

- The staggered boot workers (scheduler_loop, ingest_restore, actor_pack x2, two FTS backfills) do not touch the server.
- The screen pre-import timer (0.2 s) is itself a loop timer, so it cannot start while the loop is inside the 0.1 s callback.
- There are exactly three callers of `_activate_collections_capture_authority`: app.py:9851 (end of `_wire_collections_capture_services`, reached from the 0.1 s set_timer at app.py:16343 via `_deferred_wire_collections_capture_services` / `ensure_collections_capture_services`), app.py:11548 (async `handle_runtime_backend_changed`), and app.py:7433 (Collections first-use via `ensure_collections_capture_services`). All three are sync-on-loop, and the server branch reaches `provider.build_client()` at app.py:9915 once `get_active_context()` yields a token-derived principal.

Result: one stall of about 0.4-0.65 s on the event loop, about 0.1 s after the first interactive frame, on every server-mode boot with credentials, plus again on the first local-to-server switch.

Severity stays P1, not P0, only because server mode is opt-in. For those users it is a boot-path stall well over the 100 ms P0 line.

Fix note confirmed: `await asyncio.to_thread(provider.build_client)` from a deferred-startup task (`_create_deferred_startup_task` already exists). This also moves the sync keyring read in `_resolve_auth_token` off the loop. The loop must await the thread, not race it, because of the import lock. Combining with F2 (fewer or deferred schema modules) is the structural reduction.
fix:
Cheapest fix: warm the import off the loop.
- In `_schedule_deferred_startup_work`, when `runtime_policy.state.active_source == 'server'`, run `await asyncio.to_thread(importlib.import_module, 'tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client')` before the capture wiring. For example, turn `_deferred_wire_collections_capture_services` into a deferred-startup task that awaits the to_thread import first.
- Do the same at the top of `handle_runtime_backend_changed` before `_activate_collections_capture_authority`.
- Alternatively, run `build_client()` inside the thread.

Add a guard test: in server mode, `tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client` must be in `sys.modules` before `_activate_collections_capture_authority` runs on the loop, or the activation must not import it.

The structural reduction is F2.
fix_notes:
Reuse what already exists rather than adding new machinery. Make the server branch of `_activate_collections_capture_authority` wait on an off-loop warm-up: `await asyncio.to_thread(importlib.import_module, 'tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client')`. Better, `await asyncio.to_thread(provider.build_client)`, which also moves the keyring and credential reads in `get_active_context()`/`_resolve_auth_token` off the loop.

That requires converting the sync timer callback into a deferred-startup task (`_create_deferred_startup_task` already exists).

Three caveats:
1. Do not race the warm-up. If the loop imports client.py while a thread is mid-import, the loop blocks on the per-module import lock for the rest of the import, which is no better. The loop must await the thread.
2. A thread import still holds the GIL during pydantic class construction. The loop only gets switch-interval slices, the same trade-off the codebase measured for the splash pre-import at app.py:844-860. The UI stays responsive but runs slower during the warm-up.
3. `handle_runtime_backend_changed` needs the same await. Combining this with F2(a) (defer_build) halves the remaining thread time.

A guard test asserting that client.py is in sys.modules before activation runs on the loop is reasonable.

title: client.py god module needs 544 schema names at runtime from 51 modules, so every consumer of TLDWAPIClient pays for about 1,300 pydantic models; defer_build alone halves it
known_task: TASK-285 (Done; it identified client.py as the remaining cost centre but no follow-up task was filed)
trigger: The first TLDWAPIClient resolution in any process pays it: server-mode app (F1), MCP stdio server, tools and tests. It is paid in full even when a session uses one domain. The import cost itself is a one-off per process.
cost: I reproduced the finder's scratch experiment on pydantic 2.12.5 with no repo edits. Baseline import took 600 / 601 ms; with `pydantic.BaseModel.model_config['defer_build']=True` it took 263 / 299 ms, a reduction of about 50 to 56%. The deferred model reported `__pydantic_complete__=False` until first use. The 51-schema-module and 86-new-module counts were confirmed in the F1 probe.
fix:
Two-step plan:

(a) Low risk: add `model_config = ConfigDict(defer_build=True)` through a shared base, or on each schema module's root models. Keep the existing `extra=` settings by merging configs. This halves import cost and changes no API.

(b) Structural: stop importing response and request classes at `client.py` module scope.
- Move the 382 annotation-only names under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (the file already has `from __future__ import annotations`).
- Resolve the 544 runtime names lazily through the existing PEP 562 facade, for example `from . import __init__ as _api` and then `_api.NoteResponse.model_validate(...)`, or per-method function-local imports. The facade's `__getattr__` then imports only the domains actually used.

Alternative for (b): split `TLDWAPIClient` into per-domain mixin modules that are imported lazily.

Keep `Tests/Packaging/test_tldw_api_import_closure.py` and add a probe asserting that `import tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client` loads fewer than N `*_schemas` modules.
fix_notes:
(a) defer_build. Do it through a shared base or a per-module `model_config`. Never mutate `BaseModel.model_config` globally, because that would leak into every pydantic model in the process, including LLM and config models. Merge with each model's existing config (extra=, populate_by_name and so on). The trade-off: the first validation of each model builds its schema (about 0.5 ms or more, more for nested models), and on a hot path such as a streamed-chunk model that lands on the first chunk. That is acceptable, but be aware of it.

(b) Do not use the suggested `from . import __init__ as _api`. It imports a SECOND module object, `tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.__init__`, and re-executes the package body. Use `from tldw_chatbook import tldw_api as _api` or function-local imports instead.

The ~550 runtime sites make (b) a sprawling mechanical rewrite, which is exactly why TASK-285 stopped. Do (a) first, then (b) per domain. The proposed probe in `Tests/Packaging/test_tldw_api_import_closure.py` is a good regression net.

title: Each TLDWAPIClient owns a private httpx pool and SSLContext; about 30 from_config services mean about 30 fragmented pools, each paying about 9 ms of SSLContext build on the loop plus a fresh TLS handshake
trigger: Server mode: the first call through each distinct from_config service (Tools, MCP governance, Text2SQL, Evaluations, Watchlists, Kanban and so on) runs `_get_client()` on the loop inside an async service method. This is once per service per process, on less common screens.
cost: Measured with httpx 0.28.1: `AsyncClient(verify=True)` construction has a median of 9.8 ms (minimum 9.1 ms) over 15 runs, against 0.14 ms when passing a shared `create_ssl_context()`. The extra handshakes per pool are real but estimated and do not block the loop.
fix:
Option 1: in client.py, cache one process-wide SSLContext per verify setting. For example, add `_shared_ssl_context()` using `functools.lru_cache` over `httpx.create_ssl_context()` when `ssl_verify is True`, and pass it as `verify=`. An SSLContext is safe to share across clients.

Option 2, the larger win: build the `from_config` services from `self.server_context_provider`, or have `build_runtime_api_client_provider_from_config` return one app-wide memoized provider per resolved config. That gives one pool and one handshake, and shutdown closes everything.
fix_notes:
Option 1, done centrally: return a process-cached SSLContext from `tls_trust.httpx_verify()` (lru_cache over `httpx.create_ssl_context()`) instead of `True`. That reaches every httpx client in the app, not only TLDWAPIClient. There are two risks:
- Tests that assert `verify is True` will break.
- A cached context freezes SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR and trust-env at first use.

Option 2 is NOT a pure performance change. The legacy from_config providers resolve the endpoint and credentials from the legacy `[tldw_api]` app_config, whereas server_context_provider uses the active server target plus keyring credentials. Rerouting them changes which server and credential each service talks to, so it needs a behavioural review, possibly under the scope-service consolidation (TASK-32898/ADR-177).

At minimum, close the legacy providers' cached clients at shutdown.
reason:
client.py:1303 `_get_client` lazily builds `httpx.AsyncClient(..., verify=self.ssl_verify)` for each TLDWAPIClient.

ssl_verify comes from `Utils/tls_trust.httpx_verify()`, which returns the bool `True` under the default policy. httpx 0.28 therefore builds a fresh SSLContext and loads certifi on every client. It only returns a (possibly shared) SSLContext when a custom CA is configured.

app.py has exactly 29 `Server*Service.from_config(` sites (for example ServerToolsService at 10880). Each creates its own `LegacyConfigServerClientProvider` (bootstrap.py:263-266), which caches a private client (build_client near line 250). There are 13 `from_server_context_provider(` sites, which share `RuntimeServerContextProvider`'s single cached client.

Shutdown closes only `server_context_provider.close_cached_client()` (app.py:17801-17808), so the legacy providers' AsyncClients are never closed.

`_get_client` is awaited inside async service methods called from screen handlers, so the ~10 ms construction runs on the loop the first time each legacy service is used. No open task covers this.

title: All binary downloads are fully buffered in memory (_binary_request -> response.content); the chatbook export download then writes the whole blob synchronously from a button handler
trigger: A user action: pressing 'download-server-job' in Chatbook export management runs an awaited chain in the button handler on the loop. The network transfer is async, but the full body is held in RAM, and the sync write plus full fsync of the whole blob then blocks the loop. The path is infrequent.
cost: Estimated, not measured. The RSS spike equals the export size. The loop freeze is the write plus a full-barrier fsync of the whole blob, which on macOS F_FULLFSYNC can reach hundreds of ms for exports of 100 MB or more. Sizes of 50 to 500 MB are plausible for exports that contain media but were not verified.
fix:
Add one streaming primitive to `TLDWAPIClient`: `async def _download_to_path(method, endpoint, dest, params=None)`.
- Use `client.stream(...)`, with the same redirect and error handling as `_stream_request`.
- Write `aiter_bytes(1 << 20)` chunks to a temp file through `asyncio.to_thread(f.write, chunk)`, or open the file in a worker.
- `os.replace` at the end, keeping the 0o600 temp-file semantics of `atomic_write_bytes`.

Expose `download_chatbook_export_to_path` and use it in `ServerChatbookService.download_export_job`. Keep `_binary_request` for small payloads.

Its callers are server_context.py:334 (RuntimeServerContextProvider.build_client), bootstrap.py:240/253/278 (legacy provider, chatbook builder) and app.py:10923/10929 (MCP target, action-driven). The screen pre-import thread (0.2 s) cannot warm it because no screen module imports it at module scope. on_mount and _post_mount_setup (app.py:14734-16330) contain no server-client calls. _schedule_deferred_startup_work arms set_timer(0.1 s, _deferred_wire_collections_capture_services) (app.py:16342). That runs ensure_collections_capture_services (9864), then _wire_collections_capture_services (9851), then _activate_collections_capture_authority (9881). Local mode returns early at 9889. Server mode runs get_active_context(), then event_principal_id_from_active_context, which is non-None for any non-empty token (server_event_scope.py:15-25), then provider.build_client() at 9915, all synchronously on the loop. The second trigger is handle_runtime_backend_changed (async, on the loop, app.py:11546-11547), reached from settings_screen.py:25544/25597.
Verdict: real. It is a one-time ~0.4 s freeze (floor) shortly after first paint on every boot of a server-mode user with a token; locally it measured 0.7 s under load. That keeps P1 rather than P0 only because it is gated to server-mode users and fires once per session. Keyring and config costs in get_active_context sit on the same chain and were not measured (keyring is unsafe to exercise).
fix: Move the import off the loop. (1) Warm `tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client` in the existing screen pre-import thread (_schedule_screen_preimport / _preimport_screens pattern), or in a dedicated to_thread, when the runtime source is server. Schedule it ahead of the 0.1 s capture-wiring timer, or make _activate_collections_capture_authority obtain the client via `await asyncio.to_thread(provider.build_client)`. (2) Combine with F2 (defer_build), which halves the block. (3) Longer term: client.py already has `from __future__ import annotations`, so annotation-only schema names can move under TYPE_CHECKING and runtime ones can use per-method or per-domain lazy imports. Add a guard test that boots with a server-mode fixture config and asserts tldw_api.client is not imported on the loop. Related umbrella: TASK-32804 (sync work on the event loop).
fix_notes: Do NOT call provider.build_client via asyncio.to_thread as proposed. RuntimeServerContextProvider.build_client mutates _cached_client/_cached_client_key with no lock (server_context.py:325-339), and other loop callers use it too, so running it off-loop races. The safer root-cause fix warms only the module import in a thread (`await asyncio.to_thread(importlib.import_module, 'tldw_chatbook.tldw_api.client')`) and runs capture activation after that completes, e.g. as a _create_deferred_startup_task that awaits the warm import and then calls _deferred_wire_collections_capture_services. Starting a warm thread in parallel is not enough: if the loop reaches the import while the thread holds the module import lock, the loop blocks until the thread finishes. The warm thread still contends for the GIL, but with a 5 ms switch interval the UI stays responsive instead of freezing for 0.5 s. Do the same for handle_runtime_backend_changed before line 11547. Combine with F2. Moving client.py's names under TYPE_CHECKING only helps for annotation-only names; most are constructed or validated at runtime inside methods, so that is a large diff. The proposed server-mode boot guard test is worthwhile.

title: Every depth-0 ChaChaNotes transaction pays a ~7 ms storage-admission handshake; Console message writes cost 8-11 ms and 2-3 run on the event loop per send
known_task: TASK-32804.1 (related: same admission handshake, fixed only for config reads; DB transactions not covered)
trigger: Every Console send: at least 2 depth-0 transactions run synchronously on the event loop in the async _run_direct_provider_reply (the trajectory flush in _attach_stream_usage, and the terminal update_message_content in mark_message_complete). Also every on-loop feedback, trace-event and usage-only write, and every agent tool marker (worker thread).
cost:
Scripts are in scratch/lens2-s7c1 (f1_send.py, f1_chain.py, f1_depth.py, run.sh), all run in an isolated profile. The machine was heavily loaded throughout (loadavg 32-46 on 18 cores).

(1) Real send path, not a synthetic one. I used a real ConsoleChatController, ConsoleChatStore and ChatPersistenceService, wired as production wires them: the CitationTraceRepository is attached and canonical writes are off. The ChaChaNotes DB sits in the isolated data dir, and the provider is a fake that streams 4 chunks. I recorded every acquire_storage call along with its thread, whether a loop was running on that thread, and its call chain. A steady send (every send after the first) makes exactly 3 depth-0 ChaChaNotes admissions on the event loop:
  a) console_chat_store.py:6873 publish_durable_turn_owners -> _hydrate_durable_turn_owner_messages -> write_trajectory_rows (chat_persistence_service.py:3201), reached from controller:12346, which runs inside submit_draft.
  b) controller:26680 _attach_stream_usage -> record_trajectory_timing(flush=True) -> write_trajectory_rows.
  c) controller:27275 mark_message_complete -> store:16928 -> _settle_owned_dispatch_terminal -> console_dispatch_repository.py:920 settle_with_assistant, a transaction(immediate=True).
  Location correction: the terminal write on this path is dispatch settle_with_assistant, not update_message_content at chat_persistence_service.py:2873. I also found 12 off-loop admissions per send.
  At scratch depth these 3 cost 41.8-54.9 ms wall and 34.6-41.9 ms CPU per send.
  Sibling site with the same root cause: prompt_history.py:229 _append_impl opens `_FileJob` on the loop, which runs _async_source_selection -> default_prompt_history_path -> get_user_data_dir. That adds 5 more config-route admissions on the loop per send, costing 85-89 ms at scratch depth.
  A/B test with acquire_storage stubbed to StorageLease(None): max loop stall per send was 142-176 ms real vs 20-29 ms stubbed, and summed lag was 482-806 ms vs 166-344 ms.

(2) Micro-benchmark of an empty depth-0 transaction(immediate=True): 16-18 ms median (10.9-12.6 ms p10) with admission, vs 0.3-0.5 ms with admission stubbed.

(3) Depth sweep: 5 depths x 3 interleaved rounds, root path from 14 to 30 components. Each transaction does 265 + 16*k opens, plus 10 listdir and 7 flock. A linear fit gives cpu_p10 = 11.0 + 0.73 ms per extra level. Production root (/Users/<u>/.config/tldw_cli/recovery-bootstrap) is 5 components, i.e. k = -9. That extrapolates to about 121 opens and 3.6-6.0 ms per transaction under this load, or roughly 2.5-4 ms on a quiet machine, scaled by the finder's quiet 7.0 ms against my loaded 11-14 ms at k=0.

Production estimate per send on the loop: 3 x 2.5-6 ms = about 8-18 ms of ChaChaNotes admission, plus about 12-30 ms from the prompt-history config admissions. That totals about 20-45 ms, and a real provider adds usage and exchange writes on top. This is solidly P1 for a per-send cost. It is not P0 (at least 100 ms) at production depth.
fix: Amortize admission the way TASK-32804.1 did for config reads (_warm_config_cache_hit). Cache a validated admission lease per (pid, bootstrap root, db path) on the participant, revalidate only when the registry/pause generation changes (storage._changed notifications), and keep the full _scope walk for the first acquisition and after a pause. Nested and borrowed transactions already skip BEGIN, so make sure they also skip the handshake. In-slice follow-up: for update_message_content with writes disabled, avoid the extra citation owner-transition work (about 2.8 ms).
fix_notes: Risk is high, as the finder says. Admission exists so that a local pause (backup capture or restore) can close admission and drain every holder. A cached lease must still re-check `_pause is None`, `participant.closed` and core retirement under _lock on every operation (those checks are cheap), and the pause and drain path must invalidate or retire cached leases, or drain() will wait forever on a live lease. Before adding a new cache, consider reusing the process-lifetime startup hold (_startups[key] from admit_startup) and re-deriving _scope only when a registry or control-record generation changes. At minimum, move the _scope file I/O out from under the global _lock. Nested transactions already take the reuse branch, so they need no change. The citation-owner-transition sub-fix (~2.8 ms) is separate and low-value.

# chat_persistence_service.py:2873 (citation repo always wired by console_runtime)
    with self.db.transaction(immediate=True) as cursor:
        result = coordinated_update()
# controller:27275 (async, on loop)

TransactionContextManager.__enter__ (ChaChaNotes_DB.py:24222) calls participants._core_operation -> _RepositoryParticipant.operation -> storage_admission._repository_operation. At depth 0 that path calls acquire_storage(path) (storage_admission.py:835/854). Every call redoes bootstrap.startup_permission, qualified_for, admission_authority and two _scope passes: _records, _registry with flock and a JSON read, _binding with pinned_directory walks. Nested transactions reuse the outer operation, so they are cheap. I re-measured in an isolated scratch profile: an empty depth-0 transaction() costs 6.7-10.6 ms and an IMMEDIATE one 7.9-10.1 ms. acquire_storage+close alone costs 4.3-5.9 ms. A raw sqlite BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT costs 0.003 ms. cProfile shows 245 posix.open, 69 lstat, 36 stat and 10 listdir per transaction.
